10.title: No disappointment here, ladies and gentlemen
10.content:
It was difficult enduring month upon month of media frenzy concerning "The Dark Knight" and Heath Ledger's performance. Was it Oscar-worthy? Is The Dark Knight the greatest superhero movie of all time? Is it worth paying 7-ish bucks to go see? Yes!

The Dark Knight follows the path of its predecessor, "Batman Begins". Christopher Nolan reunites with Welsh actor Christian Bale in continuing the clean slate that lifted the hopes of so many Batman fans around the world. The movie is set not long after the last; Bruce Wayne/Batman (Bale) is as unsure as ever as to what his duties to Gotham involve and what he represents. The Joker (Ledger) has come to fruition about what needs to be done to prevent Gotham from being completely cleansed in deciding to "kill the batman". Lieutenant-Commissioner Jim Gordan (Oldman) faces the challenge of keeping the Batman and the Joker in check all while keeping a weather eye on his own shifty department. District Attorney Harvey Dent (Eckhart) faces almost the same as Gordon, with a little more love-triangles and politics thrown in there. Rachel Dawes is involved with that love triangle, and last but certainly not least, Lucius Fox needs to keep Batman's secrets and provide the cool stuff.

Now to the part that everyone really wants to hear about. The acting. It is superb, to say the least. I dare to compare the performances to that of legendary movies "The Godfather" and "Pulp Fiction". Christian Bale does the job as well as he did in Batman Begins, having more on his plate this time around with showing that 'darker' side of Batman. Heath Ledger does what everyone was talking about - he brings a "psychopathic, schizophrenic, mass-murdering" clown to life in a way that no other could possibly do. It was stunning. The Joker stole every scene he was involved in. The amount of change undergone from a witty Nicholson to a bone-chilling Ledger is unnerving. Everything from the terrifying cackle to the gangly posture - Ledger certainly brought his A-game here. Hannibal Lecter has a replacement as the most frightening villain in film. Anything less than a posthumous Oscar wouldn't be fair.

Fantastic performances go all the way through to supporting actors in Gary Oldman and Aaron Eckhart. Oldman does a fantastic job in personifying a stressed out Commissioner who's mind is juggling on three different fronts at once. Eckhart, I will admit, surprised me. I was a little uneasy when I heard of his casting, but I'm glad the doubt was proved to be out of place. He finely portrays Harvey Dent's masculinity and fire as a District Attorney. Maggie Gyllenhaal puts Katie Holmes to shame with the amount of depth portrayed upon a near-flat performance from Holmes. And of course Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman do what they do best in playing the guiding, authoritative voices in Batman's background that leads him through the tough times. I can honestly say I was not disappointed with one performance throughout the entire movie.

The cinematography and special effects are Oscar-worthy. Chrisopher Nolan succeeded in preventing The Dark Knight from becoming a over-zealousness of CGI and explosions, and the city of Chicago never looked so dark and gloomy to me before. Well done.

One thing I would never mention in any other movie, but the music in this movie was top-notch. I'm not talking a random alternative song thrown into the background of a car chase, but a superlative composition that makes the darker moments darker, and the colder moments colder.

In the end it seems only fair to commend the genius hiding behind the curtains: Christopher Nolan. The man has not only rebooted a quickly dying series, but he has done it in such a way that there is no turning away from the pending sequel. The depth that he has injected into the characters. The direction of the film. The technical quality overall. Truly amazing. I'd get into all the details concerning the theme of morality and the brilliant message that the ending provided, but I don't want to ruin it for any potential viewers. I was scared the movie wouldn't be able to find a proper ending for itself, that it would be like so many other lax endings to superhero movies, but the ending capped off a true masterpiece that had the entire theater in a standing ovation. Christopher Nolan along with his writing staff have created a masterpiece of the filming industry, one that can only fairly be called the greatest superhero movie of all time; arguably even bigger than that. Step aside Spielberg, your CGI mish-mash is outclassed here.

In 152 minutes you get a hero born, a hero that's doubted, and a psychopath that wants them both dead, all amongst twists and turns that are enough to plunge one into a feeling of euphoria that will last a lifetime.

10.title: You critics who give this a 1/10...go F**K yourselves
10.content:
What can i say other than WOW!! what a movie, what a way to portray one of the most characters of comic books. this movie i know blew everybody away!!! first day it came out, i saw it, the lines were too long and the fans were over excited, it was going to be a good movie!!! in the movie, people cheered, chanted and applauded every exciting twist and appearance.

heath ledgers was out of this world to say the least, give that man the Oscar, give him every Oscar for the next ten years. even if he had not passed on the hype about this movie would have still just blown everybody away. Christian bale, easily the best batman ever put on the screen!!

well done to the entire cast and lets make a trilogy people!!!

10.title: Wow!
10.content: Five hours ago, I walked out a movie theater and realized that I had just seen Heath Ledger's last performance. Let me tell you, it was the best portrayal of any villain I have ever seen in any movie. Ledger was the sadistic, maniacal, creepy, and funny Joker that was in the Batman comics. Was Jack Nicholson a good Joker? Yes, he was. Was Heath Ledger better than him? Big time. Ledger got into the role, the way a great actor should. Christian Bale played Batman. Heath Ledger was the Joker. Ledger, however, was not the only good part of The Dark Knight. All the other actors performed their roles beautifully. Christian Bale was great, and in my opinion, is the best Batman that there has been. I like Michael Keaton, but Bale brings out all the true qualities of Batman and Bruce Wayne. He shows how intimidating Batman really can be. Gary Oldman did a wonderful job as Liutenant Gordon. His monologue at the end really showed who Batman is, and the purpose that he serves for the city of Gotham, and the way he is,their dark knight. Aaron Eckhart, who I must admit I had never heard of before anything about the movie came out, was superb as Harvey Dent and eventually Two Face. He did a much better job as Two Face than Tommy Lee Jones did in Batman Forever. Maggie Gyllenhal, who played Rachel Dawes, was great. She wasn't the normal damsel-in-distress that you would see in any other superhero movie. She was great. Michael Caine, was the Alfred you would expect to see, wise and always there to help his master.He did well. Last but not least, there is Morgan Freeman. He acted the way Morgan Freeman acts, well. He did a fantastic job with the role of Lucius Fox. The fighting and special effects were phenomenal as well. Christopher Nolan did a phenomenal job directing The Dark Knight. This movie is more than just a movie about a superhero that dresses up like a bat and saves the day from a manical freak. It shows both sides of the story, hero and villain. It shows two ways a society can live, in order or anarchy. If you haven't seen this movie yet, go see it. If you saw it, see it again. 10/10! R.I.P. Heath Ledger

10.title: Christopher Nolan please take a bow
10.content:
The Dark Knight

Yes i have watched it four times and still have not got enough of this movie.

The first time, i was so awestruck to even notice anything other than the grandeur and the sinister mood of the movie. The second time i went to watch it for the chase sequence where the Joker is chasing Harvey Dent. It kept on lingering in my mind after the first watch. The scene where the Joker sticks out his head of the police car sums up the perfection of this movie.

The third time, what hit me hard was the characterization of every single person. I think a good movie is the one which makes you go through the same feeling as depicted on the screen.Here we have a gamut of them , chaos,guilt,endurance,sacrifice,faith...in other words a complete exhibition of human emotions and how they face the test of dilemma when such conditions arise. This movie gives you both cerebral and visceral quality. The agent here being Joker. It is really sad that we will not be able to see Heath Ledger in any other movie but i thank god that i was lucky enough to see his masterpiece. "either you die a hero or you live long enough to see yourself become a villain"--A tribute to Heath Ledger.

I cringed for Harvey dent, felt sorry for him, i laughed at the sinister jokes and felt guilty of having done so, I could feel the dilemma of our beloved Batman, and at the end could feel a sigh of relief and resignation to the fact that he is not a hero, he is much more than that.

Each and every character undergoes a change (morally, physically) under the chaos created by Joker (the best depiction of a psychotic Joker -- who at times is a child but a grown up person who likes to fiddle). The greatest fiddler in the history of cinema. Even the disappointment, bewilderment and guilt in the face of Rachel,when she comes to know of Bruce Wayne's decision, has been beautifully captured.

Music is awesome. It gets your heart pumping and racing even if the story does not (which is not possible here). Gotham city looks very much in chaos and the dark sets enhance the dark mood of the movie. Cinematography is excellent. Dialogues have been very carefully written (Jonathan Nolan seems to keep on churning thought provoking dialogs in each and every movie).Especially the monologue that the joker gives to Harvey dent is amazing. "i am like a dog chasing cars, i would not know what to do with it once i caught it"

Lastly Christopher Nolan had you not been the director, this movie would have failed to live up to the expectation after Batman Begins or even surpass it.

To tell you the truth i am being unfair to the beauty of this movie by selecting a few scenes to drive home the point. You will have to see it in order to feel the anarchy , the chaos and the thirst for more of this movie.

10.title: Most Valuable Action Movie of 2008
10.content:
This simply is the best action film of this year.

There was never a dull moment in the movie, never a lull in the action, even when the characters were engaging in small talk.

'Batman Begins' was simply an action movie, whereas 'The Dark Knight' was an absolute and engaging detective story, with all the makings of Oscar potential.

The only qualm I have with anything, is the cowl. It still looks like the children's toy, bulky and over-sized for the head. I know the writers were pursuing a more realistic approach, but you can fabricate some misstruths that would allow all that gadgetry to be more streamline inside the cowl.

Besides that everything about this film is masterful.

The Joker is everything himself says he is, a new kind of criminal. And the best kind, is the kind that you want to copy, want to talk like, wan to act like, want to feel like. A likable character, something which the magnificent Ledger must have understood, and employed.

If you haven't walked out of this movie thinking, speaking or even walking differently, then I suggest you buy another ticket.

10.title: the joker wins
10.content:
Just got home from watching the Dark Knight and wow, and i mean wow. The acting was great, the plot, the build up, the climax and everything was excellent and it has surely surpassed its hype! Christian Bale delivered another strong performance as the Batman and his Bruce Wayne character is even stronger now than the first film. Aaron Eckheart did also a very good Harvey Dent/Two Face; and by the way, the effects for the disfigured face of Two Face is awesome (looks like the one in the long halloween). And hell, Heath Ledger even surpassed Jack Nicholson's Joker.

And at the end of the day, after all that happened, Batman didn't get what he wanted, Harvey Dent surely didn't get what he deserved and Gotham City as a whole surely lost. It was actually only the Joker who won. It would have been better if they showed one after credits shot of the Joker laughing his ass off inside Arkham Asylum; but that would be wishful thinking.:)

10.title: Best. Magic Trick. Ever.
10.content:
If you've seen the film yet. you'll understand. My favorite scene aside this movie is simply amazing; great action, solid performances from everybody and Oscar worthy direction brought to us by Chris Nolan. I'll try and not just talk about Heath Ledger - I'll just say I respect him the same way I do Robert Di Nero and Al Pacino and he deserves his posthumous Oscar. OK, Katie Holmes dropped out. Great! They replaced her with a real actress, Maggie Gyllenhaal who earns her pay as Rachel Dawes. Gary Oldman, a great actor who finally gets to play a good guy. Aaron Eckhart is a man I always liked in his movies and steals his non-Joker scenes as the enigmatic "White Knight" of Gotham, Harvey Dent.

There is practically non-stop action. This movie is very loud and very violent and it creates the perfect sense of anarchy and chaos. The Joker is a very menacing villain and the citizens of Gotham are in constant danger from him. Batman has to fight hard to save the people in the Joker's way and he doesn't always succeed.

All in all The Dark Knight is never boring, totally engaging and without a doubt the best superhero movie I've seen in a while. And the people in my theater applauded at the end, during my favorite magic trick scene and when Batman does something totally awesome with a truck (I won't ruin it) so what's that tell you?

10.title: Movie-Making at it's Finest
10.content:
What a fantastic film! Expecting quite a bit after the level of reality the last one chose to maintain, I was NOT disappointed. Rare is it that a comic property brings you a superhero in the world instead of the world of a superhero.

Truly mesmerizing acting from Heath Ledger, who went out on top of his game. His performance leaves you not with 'The Joker' as a character, but rather a real person.

Great acting all around, unexpected twists, and plausible plot development make for an entertaining and satisfying movie experience of almost three hours.

Don't get the large soda, you won't want to leave your seat for a minute. Leave the kids at home, this ain't your daddy's Batman.

10.title: Superlative !!!
10.content:
< This review does not contain spoilers of any sort > Today morning witnessed a phone call ... a phone call to my boss ..claiming I was unwell. It was made by aliens who took over my body and made that phone call in my own voice.

Then they dragged my behind to PVR Saket where I watched the movie first day first show , which I had been tracking closely for almost 2 years now.

I know I came out drooling ! Why ? Here's why ! Nolan's Batman .. in his original self ... in his Gothic best ... giving his utter class performance in an utterly hopeless Gotham .. trying to save the good men and women who still reside there from the likes of the Joker.

Directed by Christopher Nolan, this , movie witnessed Christian Bale reprising his role as the caped crusader, Aaron Eckhart as the District Attorney Harvey Dent , Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon, Michael Caine as Alfred and last and in no means the least Heath Ledger as the Joker.

When I started with the movie and Mr J made his first appearance it was totally mind blowing. I can only speak superlatives of Ledger, who is mad-crazy-blazing brilliant as the Joker. Miles from Jack Nicholson's Broadway like take on the role in Tim Burton's 1989 Batman, Ledger takes the role to the shadows, where even what's comic is hardly a relief. No plastic mask for Ledger; his face is caked with moldy makeup that highlights the red scar of a grin, the grungy hair and the yellowing teeth of a hound fresh out of hell. To the clown prince of crime, a knife is preferable to a gun, the better to "savor the moment".

Joker was a man without rules. He himself admits that - Joker was like a mad dog chasing a car .. didn't know what he would do once he caught it.

The director used an IMAX camera to film six major action sequences, including the Joker's first appearance in the film. The Batsuit was redesigned, with a cowl allowing Bale to move his head. The film also introduces a recreation of the Batcycle, known as the Batpod.

It will be a great success, I guarantee, the gadgets (especially the Bat-Pod, responsible for a acclaimed action sequence ) are crazy and Heath Leger might receive a deserved indication for his Joker, 'a mixture of a fool/clown, schizophrenic, sadistic, and crazy. The guy delivered, got himself into the role and it's unrecognizable. There will be no other Joker after him.

Rest in peace. Heath Ledger: 4/4/1979-1/22/2008.

10.title: "This world deserves a better class of movie... and Dark Knight gonna give it to us"
10.content:
Craft , skill, excellence , creativity, technology and an excellent spell binding script combine to create one of the masterpieces of all time. Surely it would take more than the above said virtues to surpass The Dark Knight and I am pretty damn sure that a sequel to this will have expectations sky high. As Heath Ledger's Joker may have said " This industry deserves a better class of movie... and I'm gonna give it to them ". And dint they deliver the goods.

Unlike its predecessors , for that matter any movie which has a do-gooder superhero movie, the Dark Knight stands out for the immaculate articulation of a wide range of extremely high caliberd artist into a carefully woven masterpiece of all times. Heath Ledger as Joker left the world only after leaving us with the most perfect villain that the tinsel world has ever produced and surpasses Jack Nicholson's Joker for the shrewdness n cunningness and boy sure there is a chill that runs down the spine every time Joker appears on the screen. Its such a pity that the world lost this gem of an actor at such a young age.

The caped crusader had to change suits and upgrade his armory in every possible way to stand up against his nemesis. Christian Bale started of from where he had left of in Batman Begins. Aaron Eckhart was totally scintillating as Harvey Dent. The love triangle that featured Bruce Wayne, Rachel Dawes and Harvey Dent was pretty short , but classic .... simply classic. Morgan Freeman returns as the caped crusader's arch-in-chief and he does that with bang. The Batpod and the bat bike ... both were worthy of the superhero it got.

And yes a final word about the background score by James Newton Howard and Hans Zimmer was simply mind blowing. In short Christopher Nolan wove out a masterpiece which enthralls, enthrills and keeps u on the edge of ur seats making u wish that u could come back day after day to see the whole spectacle again and again.

Folks ... why so serious??? Chill n go out to ur nearest theaters to watch the Movie of the Millennium.

Rating : Had I the authority I would have given it 100 out of 10 hmmm

10.title: Stop bashing the most minuscule things. This movie was great
10.content: Alright, first let me go about saying that I saw the 1989 Batman and thoroughly enjoyed Jack Nicholson's Joker. Then this film came out. This Joker was much different than any other character I have ever seen. Those of you who say things like "he had no back story" or "no motives at all." . Let me just say that most great villains have no back story and are enjoyed, such as last year's Anton Chigurh from "No Country For Old Men." Heath Ledger, who I really did not know much about prior to the film, did most likely one of the best jobs I ever saw in film. He was scary and just, all-around creepy. Also, last I checked, the Joker is an anarchist, so those of you that say "he has no motives"; that was the point Christopher Nolan had in mind. Everybody else did great jobs in their roles, Christian Bale did great as Batman/Bruce Wayne; the only complaint I have is his chain smoker voice as batman, but it wasn't that bad. Everybody else did great jobs in this movie, including Aaron Eckhart and Gary Oldman. All in all, I think this film should get Heath an Oscar, and I get severely annoyed by people bashing this film and saying that Jack's joker was better. The Joker's are not capable of being compared, Jack did a great job being the campy joker and Ledger did well as the schizophrenic clown in "The Dark Knight". They are two different Jokers, so stop comparing them so harshly. However, I personally prefer Heaths, and his will be a Joker who will be quoted for years to come. 10/10

10.title: First mythology of the 21st century
10.content:
There's not much left to say, everyone here's already said it. I'd just suggest seeing this film a few times. In the first viewing the movie overwhelmed. In subsequent viewings I had a chance to catch the details that really make it special. The facial expressions of Ledger's Joker; the little mocking moue he pulls after his interrogation-room guard answers that 6 of his friends had been killed and his brief pause as he plumbs his dark mind for his next words calculated to break the officer. The hysterical glee, that seemed to have little to do with acting, as the Joker tells the interrogating Batman that he does not want him dead.

Just about every word this creature says is a lie, the only literary creation to even approach this Joker's essence of pure evil is Lucifer. And for all his heroism and his having survived the film's moral minefield Bale's Batman leaves off alone and seeming essentially doomed.

Nolan has created a visceral, three-dimensional, fully realized Gotham, I could so easily see myself living there, then turns it into a battlefield for warring gods.

There is something mythic in this production that for me only increases on subsequent viewing. Pretty magnificent stuff!

10.title: "Not only is TDK the best superhero movie ever made, its quite honestly one of the best movies period."
10.content:
First off, Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight is not a superhero movie. It has nothing to do with comic book movies really. TDK is so far beyond the limits of its supposed brethren its really in a class of its own, with comparisons to Iron Man, Spider-Man 2, and even Batman Begins doesn't come close to touching upon the greatness of this film. Not only is TDK the best superhero movie ever made, its quite honestly one of the best movies period.

Nolan has really outdone himself here. Not just himself, but everyone else that has made superhero flicks. He doesn't just adapt a comic book, he has created an entire world, one that just happen to involve comic book characters. His take on Batman is the most inspired I've ever seen; getting the character's inner conflicts so right and make them ring so true is incredible. Christian Bale is great as the Caped Crusader (although his harsh growl is still the lone weak spot in his performance). Thankfully he has an excellent supporting cast who all get their time to shine. Michael Caine is perfect as Alfred, who keeps Bruce from falling from grace and helps him when he just doesn't know what to do, and their banter is fun to watch. Morgan Freeman also shines as Lucius Fox, a mentor of sorts to Wayne who, like in Freemans best roles, just radiates wisdom. Aaron Eckhart is simply powerful as Harvey Dent, a district attorney who's character arc is one of the most tragic story lines in any movie. Maggie Gyllenhaal gets the short stick here, as Nolan just doesn't know what to do with her character.

They may all be great, but two performers here easily trump them all: Gary Oldman and Heath Ledger. Oldman gets a bigger, juicier role as Jim Gordon, Gothams Lieutenant who helps Batman and Dent to try and stop the rise in crime thats plaguing the city. His story arc is compelling to watch. That explanation leads me to one of the most inspired and creative villains ever conceived: the Joker.

Heath Ledger is simply incredible as the Joker, a man who has no past whatsoever (which is emphasized by his contradictory explanations of the origin of his scars), who seems to live just to create destruction. He is chaos incarnate, someone who wants to burn down Gotham just for the fun of it, and a part of you will want him to just see how he'll do it. He has no remorse, he is twisted in every way, and he is in short, brilliant. Ledger puts everything into this role. He is the Joker, he'll make you laugh at all the wrong moments, and he will make you cringe so much you're face will get stuck. His performance will stick with you for a long time. Hes an instant icon. All the Oscar talk is not hyperbole. Give the guy an Academy Award, he deserves it. Its the role of a lifetime, the role he was made for. Saying hes the best Joker ever portrayed is underselling him. Hes one of the best villains ever portrayed.

In Batman Begins, my one big complaint was that the action, while sometimes invigorating, was handled poorly, with the close ups and shaky cam inducing a sense of nausea instead of suspense. He not only fixes these problems, he expands on the overall action. When Batman fights, he takes them in quick succession, using the kind of lyrical poetry unlike nothing I've seen since Bourne Ultimatum. The big explosions don't matter however, as with the best of Nolan's work, a lot of the action is psychological. The movies plot rises to epic status because the characters within it are so compelling. It makes the tragic story resonate more than it probably would have otherwise.

Simply calling The Dark Knight a superhero movie is wrong. Its an epic crime drama that just happens to be based on a comic book. It trumps everything and everyone that has come before to be one of the best movies ever made. When the movie ends you may find yourself applauding, as you have witnessed a masterpiece unlike anything you've ever seen.

10.title: Ledger's Joker the best character portrayal ever
10.content:
The principal reason behind the movie's super-success is probably the portrayal of the character of JOKER by Heath Ledger.The death of Ledger had triggered a worldwide interest in the film and this role has definitely made him into a cult figure.Juvenile yet sinister,Ledger transcends the sophistication and 'goofiness' of Jack Nicholson.Beside the brilliant speeches on morality,chaos and order,there are certain moments in the film which are really kick-ass:

1)the 'pencil trick' 2)when he meets Rachel and finger-combing his hair says 'hello beautiful' 3)just the simple utterance of the word 'Hi' when he comes to meet Harvey Dent at the hospital,made so other-worldly by the expression of his eyes and raised eyebrows 4)he comes out of Gotham Hospital in a nurse's dress and tries to trigger off explosions with his remote;it malfunctions for a second or two and he bangs the remote on his palm like a child does with his toy and suddenly the explosives go off!

'Moments' like these make us feel that THE DARK KNIGHT is,after all,Heath Ledger's movie.One of the most remarkable quotes of the Joker is 'Introduce a little anarchy...Upset the established order...And everything becomes Chaos.I am an agent of Chaos'.As Ledger says these words to Harvey Dent,he reminds us of Satan in Milton's Paradise Lost keen of upsetting and toppling the order of God in Paradise.It's something like Satan meets the modern day anti-establishment punk rock,Ledger is so bloody good!When Batman asks him why he wanted to kill him,he rubbishes it by saying 'I don't wanna kill you,I would never do that!What am I without you?To them, you are just a freak,like me.You complete me!'Even at the end,the Joker reasserts this view when Batman doesn't kill him although he is beaten to pulp 'You won't kill me out of some misplaced sense of self-righteousness and I don't want to kill you...because you are too much fun'.Evil and Good complete each other,one has no value or significance without the other.He constantly tries to say that Batman is not a hero but more of a fallen angel who is nothing but a 'freak' like the Joker.The psychological treatment of the movie is just brilliant.The Joker is self-contradictory when he says that 'everything is part of a plan' and later he tells Harvey Dent that he is not a schemer,he is a 'dog chasing cars' and confesses 'I don't know what to do when I get the carI just do things'.Here lies the brilliance of the Joker,he is a careful manipulator with the inherent sadistic sinisterness,often interpreted as madness by others.The Joker pushes Harvey to the psychological twilight zone of confusion until he recognizes his suppressed 'spatial self' in himself.Morality takes a backseat as Harvey tries to find order in a world of chaos.He is made to choose what is 'fair' even though it is evil.Harvey chooses the wrong path but what the Joker points out is that by being an 'agent of Chaos',he is being amoral and not immoral.The manner in which the Joker introduces Harvey to his 'dark side' lying deep in his sub-conscious self has reverberation of Pink Floyd's THE DARK SIDE OF THE MOON.The song 'Brain Damage' has lines - 'The lunatic is in my head/You raise the blade, you make the change, you rearrange me till I'm sane/You lock the door and throw away the key/ There's someone in my head,but it's not me'.Sanity and insanity,if considered in the domain of order and chaos of the modern world,puts to light the fact that the fear of the unknown 'Other',which cannot be understood or interpreted,has often been linked to madness or insanity and it has the potential to destabilize the established order of sanity and normalcy.The Joker initiates a revolution against the normal order of society and in regard to this,he says to Batman'Madness is like gravityAll it needs, is just, a little push'.

Ledger is funny with his nurse's dress and certain mannerisms but the character of Joker is very disturbing and morbid too,especially when he gives his explanation behind the scars on his face and keeps on asking in a resonating voice 'Why so serious?'His authoritativeness overshadows Batman when he says these words as he is confronted by the latter'This is what happens when an unstoppable force meets an immovable object'.

If we discuss the Modernist theories of Absurdism and Nihilism, we can connect the Joker's character to it.Absurdism states that 'The pursuit of intrinsic or extrinsic meaning in the universe is a futile gesture' and Nihilism argues that 'existence is without objective meaning, purpose, or intrinsic value'.According to Nietzsche, objective morality does not exist in a world bereft of a higher order or God.In the absence of morality,existence has no intrinsic higher meaning or goal.Hence, the Joker's confession that he doesn't know what to do when he finally gets an object he chases.He just 'does things' without completely understanding the purpose of his action or the value of the object.To the Joker,morality is just an excuse to suppress the hidden 'inner self'.He has fun disturbing the established order of the society and he does that with an amoral stand.

As mentioned before that although the film revolves around the good guys like Gordon and Harvey Dent,the Joker is the heart and soul of the movie.I just forgot that it's a Batman movie after all!Christian Bale does a terrific job as a lonely and world weary Batman thinking about 'retirement'.He is way better than Keaton and Val Kilmer who were made to behave like a 'perfect' and essentially moralistic superhero whereas Batman is actually a flawed superhero who has no half measures when he deals with evil.To add to all these,the gravity defying stunts are just mind blowing!A special mention must be made about Christopher Nolan for reinventing the Batman cult.A top notch script with brilliant camera work.Most of the film is shot at night and the murkiness of the chilling,dark ambiance is captured in a Dante-esquire world where evil reigns supreme.

10.title: True to the character's spirit, and great movie in general.
10.content:
I went to see this movie with extremely high expectations and the movie just blew my expectations up with a huge bang.

The tight pacing(hard trick to pull, for a movie 2 1/2 hours long), the style, the very epic feel of The Dark Knight, and just the overall technical fireworks, drama, and action, is reason enough to give this movie at least 8 stars.

But the true genius of the movie is in the characters, and the actors playing them. Batman in this movie, to me, feels more faithful to the comic book character than in previous movies. The late Heath Ledger pulls off a very creepy and very intense version of The Joker, who practically steals the show as the Caped Crusader's nemesis. Harvey Dent, well, I don't want to spoil anything for you, but you'll love him.

And lastly, my personal favourite is the understated Gary Oldman as (pre)Commissioner Gordon, whose portrayal of a seasoned cop just doing the best he can with what little resources he has, really managed to tug on my heartstrings at points in the movie.

So I'm giving this movie 10 stars, because it's my definition of the perfect movie, comic book or not. I'll definitely be watching this movie again, many times more.

10.title: The Dark Knight, a new kind of comic book movie
10.content: Last night I was privileged enough to see The Dark Knight. The local radio stations offered press screener passes in exchange for waiting in line for more than three hours (don't mock me, I was number 80 in line, number 1 got there 4 hours before I did). I had been anticipating this release for months now, and I was not let down. Before I go into specifics, let me tell you that all the hype, all the crazy viral campaigns to build up support for this movie did not oversell it. All the waiting was worth it. The Dark Knight is the best Batman movie yet. First, let's discuss the elephant in the room, Heath Ledger. There has been a lot of talk about how his portrayal of The Joker might get him an Oscar. I think there is a good chance he will. I say this because last year's Supporting actor award winner was the same level of insanity. The Joker is to The Dark Knight what Anton Chigurh is to No Country for Old Men. Instead of a villain with any moral convictions or rules or even goals, you get something almost elemental. Every time Joker is in the scene you tighten up because you don't know what he's thinking (just wait for the magic disappearing pencil scene). The acting is superb. I had to stop and remind myself who was behind that makeup. Ledger was able to take a character that is so complex and bring him to life. I will grant that the sick and twisted games played by Joker are the writing of Christopher Nolan, David Goyer, and Nolan's brother, BUT that's not what makes the Joker complete. It's all the little things. It's the way he stalks around people, the way he licks his scars, those little... quirks that make him real. One scene still gives me shivers just because of the way the Joker responds to a cop when the cop says that Joker killed six of his friends. There is almost a torture movie slant to the character. What can I do to inspire the most possible terror in this city? The relationship between Joker and Batman is very loyal to the comic books as well. Nolan doesn't even try to explain the Joker's past existence. As far as we should be concerned, he didn't exist until Batman came to Gotham city. One of the parts I loved about the movie was how Joker puts together stories of his past that keep changing. In truth, everyone seems to bring their A-game to the show. The Dark Knight adds depth to all of the characters. Gary Oldman makes Jim Gordon come alive. Hell, there's one part of the story that pretty much brought tears to my eyes concerning Gordon. Michael Caine gives more depth to Alfred, providing some clues to his background. Aaron Eckhart does a fantastic job as Harvey Dent/Two-Face (I'm assuming that's no spoiler. If you don't know Harvey Dent is Two-Face, then you shouldn't care about my review in the first place). Eckhart makes for an excellent pretty boy DA who has real thoughts and real qualms about Gordon and Batman, and his transition to Two-Face is startling. It's hard for the audience to hate him as Two-Face after we loved him as Harvey Dent. Christian Bale does some fantastic work with the Batman persona and the Bruce Wayne persona. Both have added depth and weaknesses which are addressed. The methodical detective that I have come to love about the Batman is more evident in The Dark Knight, as are the repercussions for such a life. In one scene, Bale removes his shirt, showing a series of scars all over his back. That really helps to show the hard life Batman leads. The only negative side is I don't care for the raspy voice Bale uses for Batman. I know Bale has to change his voice and make it menacing, and there are limits to the vocal abilities of a man, but when Batman is involved in lengthy dialog is seems evident Bale is having trouble with the voice. As for the story, the plot is surprisingly the main focus. This is not a comic book movie that has you waiting for the big fight scene, the plot is actually rather complex. There are a lot of elements of movies like The Godfather and The Untouchables which add depth to the story. When The Dark Knight ends, you don't feel like everything has been resolved and everything is going to be OK. It's almost upsetting, the way the movie treats these comic book characters so realistically. When Bale lifts his shirt revealing all those scars, that's how everyone ends up when the credits roll. Remember how the sequels to Pirates of the Caribbean decided to add complexity to the plot and ended up making the whole thing such an incomprehensible mess in those 2 1/2 hours? The Dark Knight does not do that. All of the plot lines are kept in order and there is very little quick explanations. One thing about the movie that I enjoyed was the realism of the action. There was no crazy kung-fu or spectacular acrobatics involved. The fighting was kept very realistic. Actually, the way the Joker fought was just as creepy as his acting. "You've changed things... forever. There's no going back." I think when Nolan wrote that line it was more for himself. See, this movie is different. It's not a movie about superheroes fighting super villains. It's rough and gritty and you come out feeling a little disturbed. I think this movie is going to be much like Frank Miller's The Dark Knight Returns, a new age of realism and adult themes in these movies. I would like any adult friends of mine to see this film, but keep the kids out. The Dark Knight's PG-13 rating should be R. This isn't like Saturday morning cartoons.

10.title: A true masterpiece
10.content:
I'll admit, before I saw this movie, I wasn't into Batman. I'd seen Tim Burton's Batman, Batman Forever, and Batman & Robin (Ugh!). They were good, but none of them had that spark that I like. However, this film just blew me away. Firstly, the film gets to the point. There is not title sequence. All you see is the Batman symbol in blue fire, and then we get to the first scene. Thats an extra point for getting to the story straight away. Next, the Acting. Everyone in this film is at the top of their game. Christian Bale as Bruce Wayne, Aaron Eckhart at Harvey Dent, Maggie Gyllenhaal as Rachel Dawes, they were all fantastic. What of the Joker? In my opinion, the Oscar should be a certainty. Ledger gave the Joker a creepy, sadistic, almost in-human performance, and was absorbed in the role. At no point did you think "Heath Ledger is a good actor." All you can think is "The Joker is scary." When the Joker broadcast his threat video and shouted "LOOK AT ME!", the cinema went silent. Two-face was also really impressive. Aaron Eckhart was perfect for the role, and the characters gradual descent into madness felt so natural and smooth. Then the final blow comes, and we see what Dent has become. I'll have to put Makeup in for my Oscar nomination as well, because Two-Face is just...disturbing. Tommy Lee-Jones, eat your heart out. Sometimes, a script can ruin an actors performance, even if they're a great actor. However, every line in this movie has a feeling of authenticity, and relevance. There are scenes of dialogue in this scene which get you pulled into the moment. The Music in this movie is inspirational. Hans Zimmer & James-Newton Howard did a fantastic job. There is also the cinematography, which is spectacular, and gives a gritty sense of realism. All in all, I recommend this film more than any other film I have seen this year. In fact, I recommend this over any other film this decade. I would be willing to say I recommend it over any other film I have ever seen, its that perfect. As for Oscars, I genuinely hope this films gets nominations for Cinematography, Music, Makeup, Directing, screenplay and most certainly Ledger's performance. If Heath Ledger doesn't win, I guarantee there is going to be rioting.

10/10

10.title: It's one of the most fantastic scenes you've seen in film for a long, long time. And this is a fantastic film.
10.content:
Watching The Dark Knight on a big screen is an experience comparable to few other pleasures one can think of immediately. I honestly can't remember the last time I felt this satisfied coming out of a film. What's genius about director Christopher Nolan's latest Batman installment is that it's not only a spectacular comic-book movie, but also one with an intellectual heart. It's not all chases and explosions and action scenes -- although there's lots of that -- it's also a really smart film about characters with edge and a plot that actually seems to make sense.

Christian Bale slips into the batsuit once again to play the Caped Crusader who thinks of hanging up his boots when he becomes impressed with District Attorney Harvey Dent's crime-fighting resolve. But when clown-faced psychopath The Joker shows up, Batman realises retirement is a long time away.

In addition to new characters like Harvey Dent (played superbly by Aaron Eckhart, by the way), all significant characters from Nolan's previous film Batman Begins return for this new adventure. Police lieutenant Jim Gordon (played by Gary Oldman), Bruce Wayne's faithful butler Alfred (played by Michael Caine), Wayne's go-to guy for fancy gizmos Lucius Fox (played by Morgan Freeman) and assistant DA and Wayne's love interest Rachel Dawes (played this time by Maggie Gylenhaal) are all back and have respectable roles to play here, but The Dark Knight is ultimately about Batman and The Joker. It's a much darker film than any of the previous Batman movies, and it goes into directions that few comic-book films have taken before. Much of that edginess comes from The Joker and his sinister plans. Not merely content at killing his enemies, The Joker chooses to psychologically torment his rivals by forcing them to question what they stand for.

Inheriting the character completely, delivering a text-book performance that is hard to forget even days after you've watched the film, the late Heath Ledger IS The Joker. The greasy hair, the make up-smeared face, the red scar of a grin, the tongue snaking out of his lips, and that sloshy voice - not only is this Joker a complete contrast from Jack Nicholson's largely comic take on the same role in Tim Burton's 1989 Batman film, but Heath Ledger as The Joker is undoubtedly the finest, most menacing villain in any comic-book movie yet.

For those interested purely in the spectacle value of the film, there's enough to keep you excited. Cars explode, jails and hospitals are blown up, bombs are put in people's mouths, even left in their stomachs. There are some fantastic chase sequences, and there's one particularly jaw-dropping scene in which a massive truck flips in the air like an Olympic diver. There's also the Batmobile which transforms itself into an armored tank and even a turbo motorcycle.

Naturally all this means it's a long film -- 2 hours and 32 minutes to be precise -- but it's unlikely that you'll complain because you're sucked into the drama pretty early on. Allowing Ledger and The Joker to steal this film from under his nose, Christian Bale as Batman takes a backseat during this ride. But Nolan gives him that one magnificent scene which makes up for whatever complaints Batman might otherwise have. In this scene, we see Batman leaping off a Gotham skyscraper, swooping down into the night, his bat wings rustling in the air as he descends on the city he's here to protect. It's one of the most fantastic scenes you've seen in film for a long, long time. And this is a fantastic film.

I'm going with four out of five and two big thumbs up for The Dark Knight -- go with a big bucket of popcorn and prepare to have a great time. It's for the pleasure of watching films like this that reclining seats and giant screens were invented.

10.title: "You either die a hero, or you live long enough to see yourself become the villain."
10.content:
PLOT: Picking up where 'Batman Begins' left off, Batman (Christian Bale) and James Gordon (Gary Oldman) join forces with Gotham's new DA Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart), dubbed "The White Knight" by the press, to dismantle the remaining mob bosses in Gotham. But there's a new player in the game, a sadistic criminal called the Joker (the late Heath Ledger), and he's hellbent on destroying everyone and everything in his path, in one way or another.

To put it simply, this is a powerful, moving film far beyond any previous comic book adaptations. The film truly is nothing short of superb. The late Heath Ledger was undeniably creepy & terrifying as the hateful, heartless, lip-licking, cackling Joker (and trust me, he does a great job of making you hate the Joker), while Aaron Eckhart delivers a powerful performance as the doomed DA Harvey Dent/2-Face, so powerful it makes me wish Eckhart was the one up for an Oscar nomination. Christian Bale is of course perfect as Batman/Bruce Wayne with the always welcomed Gary Oldman, Michael Caine & Morgan Freeman reprising their roles as Gordon, Alfred & Fox. Maggie Gyllenhaal lends nice support in the Rachel Dawes role originated by Katie Holmes (who is sadly better known now as Mrs. Tom Cruise #3).

Can't wait for the next one... and it had better have Catwoman/Selina Kyle in it.

Heath Ledger gives a chilling, mind-bending performance that will stay with you for a while. I will be surprised if I don't go back to see it three more times. Everyone's performance made this film unarguably one of the best of the year. 10.title: One of the best films I've ever seen
10.content:
I tend not to throw around words like "best" or "ever", much less in the same sentence. In fact, I do not have a top 3, top 5, or top 10 movie list. I simply rate movies among four categories: "outstanding", "good", "okay" and "terrible".

The Dark Knight would definitely rate among the "outstanding".

Nolan's follow-up to Batman Begins exceeded the expectations of most Batman fans. Yet, it is perhaps fitting that The Dark Knight doesn't have the name "Batman" in it's title...because it is much more than a Batman movie.

The late Heath Ledger's performance as "The Joker" is so good, it's as if he was born to play the role. His portrayal of Gotham City's least favorite criminal is anything but cartoonish or comic-like. Ledger brings The Joker to a level of villain rivaled only by Anthony Hopkins' Hannibal Lecter, or Robert Deniro in "Cape Fear".

With so much hype surrounding The Joker, one would think the remaining characters suffer from lack of screen time and development (*cough* Spider-Man 3). Not true. Christopher Nolan found the right blend of face time and dialog to keep us free from disappointment and confusion. Ironically though, it's The Joker's lack of a back story that makes him all the more intriguing.

Although most "action" movies start with a little bit of drama and are mixed with a lot of action, The Dark Knight's blend consists of a great drama storyline with a decent amount of action. The result? See for yourself.

10.title: Magnificent
10.content:
I waited years for this film. I just finished watching it in IMax in the midnight premiere. Have I got some thoughts or what?

I'm not going to go into all the stuff everyone else has already said. By that, I mean I'm not going to write about how much Heath deserves that Oscar, although I think he definitely does.

Before I went into this movie, I thought that between leaked photos and video clips, I knew way too much. Boy, was I wrong. I knew nothing about what I was going to see. I made all these predictions. I was wrong about everything. There were certain things I guessed right, but in some way, I was still wrong.

The dialogue and shooting of the Dark Knight was flawless. The music was somewhat of a combination between the first film and the Prestige.

The twists were terrific. Every time I realized what was about to happen, I held my breath. The twists would be followed by straight up action. Action that Michael Bay could only dream of figuring out how to shoot. I mean, Gotham was a serious war zone. I really had that feeling that the Joker was going to strike at any minute.

I give this film a 10/10 on IMDb. Unbelievable stuff. I'm proud of you, Christopher Nolan. And Heath, you truly were a force to be reckoned with.

10.title: A Darker Sort of Magic
10.content:
It's hard to overlook Heath Ledger's death in the face of this movie. Hype for the film reached a paramount after his death was announced, The Joker's performance and the actor behind it threatening to over-blow the picture itself. The cast and crew (apart from the placid Katie Holmes, replaced comfortably by Maggie Gyllenhaal in the role of Rachel Dawes) all return for Christopher Nolan's second venture into the crime-ridden Gotham City, and quite stunningly tops their previous BATMAN BEGINS. That movie was quite excellent, portraying a dark grim world and a powerful superhero with his inner demons always haunting him. THE DARK KNIGHT manages to push the sequel into crime-epic territory, and little of the superhero grandeur expected from a comic-book adaptation can be seen. The film is all the better for it. It's absolutely stunning.

Christian Bale returns as Batman, this time as an essentially turmoil-ridden and confused hero. It's a quietly effective performance which, if attempted by an actor with less caliber than Bale, would have deflated the film. The villain, replacing Liam Neeson from BEGINS, is The Joker, in the much-hyped performance by Heath Ledger. Never has a character thrilled and scared me in the manner in which Ledger's Joker has managed to. A truly terrific turn (which certainly deserves a Supporting Actor Oscar) which startles the viewer, not letting go even after the end credits. The supporting cast, as it's predecessor, is solid from top to bottom, Michael Caine standing out as the father-figure and warm 'accomplice.' Aaron Eckhart provides an effective rival as DA Harvey Dent, the 'White Knight' who has fallen in love with Rachel Dawes, in a much more fulfilled role than what was seen in BATMAN BEGINS.

The action sequences are realistic and often brutal, occasionally pushing the boundaries of what can be shown in an unrestricted film. Nolan shoots these scenes in a much less frenetic way than with BEGINS, allowing the audience experience the scenes and the characters rather than guessing. The film is shot in a realistic manner, the stand-in for Gotham being Chicago. It's much more a crime-epic than a colourful superhero outing.

Few recent summer movies have left me as thrilled and startled as THE DARK KNIGHT. I have to back to 2003, when The Lord Of The Rings chapter closed, to find a comparable mainstream effort as absolutely stunning and effective as this movie. Epic, spiralling and ultimately unforgettable, THE DARK KNIGHT deserves all the accolades pressed upon it. It's content like this which makes this moviegoer believe again in the magic of cinema today.

10.title: Always Leave Em Smiling! HAHAHA!!
10.content:
**Just to be careful about spoilers, the only one should be if you know NOTHING about the character of Harvey Dent**

I believe "joygasim" is the word that best describes my feelings while watching this film. I got to the theater early had found the perfect seat. Right up front and center in the main aisle before you start going up so it's at the perfect height to watch it on the ultra screen. I even made sure to grab one of the comfy easy chair type cushy seats, then spent the entire movie on the edge of it! My heart was pounding, nearly jumping out of my chest throughout the entire movie. I walked out in wide-eyed amazement with a silly grin on my face, feeling somewhere between dazed and high. I ran into my friend who was in line for the next showing, and upon seeing my expression, he asked "That good huh?" I believe I garbled out something about it being the greatest movie of all time, and something about its awesomeness being boner-inducing. It's an hour later and I'm still coming down from it.

I guess i should start out with how Heath Ledger's portrayal of The Joker was one of the finest examples of acting I have EVER seen in my life, and I really hope he gets an Oscar for this. Seriously, I was one of those doubters that kind of thought "An Oscar, really? Is all this talk because he's dead?" But he REALLY stole the show and provided what I believe will go down as the quintessential, classic representation of a madman! Christian Bale was as on as ever, and did an excellent job as the Caped Crusader. I still say he is the best Batman ever. Yeah, you heard me George Clooney!! Michael Caine was again, an excellent Alfred. Playing not only Bruce's butler, but his friend, his confidante, and his mentor... as well as a terrible smart-ass. Aaron Eckhart did an awesome job as Harvey Dent, making the transition between Harvey and Two-Face very fluid and believable, even managing to be sort of likable to the very end, or at least able to be sympathized with. Even Gary Oldman did a bang-up job as Commissioner Gordon, with his role expanded greatly in this film to be a character much more central to the plot!

They say an actor is only as good as the character written and the writers here did an amazing job. Batman's lines, Dent's speeches, Alfred's little anecdotes and advice, and even Gordan's monologue at the very end, were incredibly well written and left me with goosebumps.

All in all, I really do have to say, I'm sorry Boondock Saints, The Dark Knight is now my favorite movie of all time.

In my opinion Heath Ledger has forever embodied the words "Always leave em smilin'!"

10.title: Le Dark of the fantastic Knight
10.content: Absolutely unreal. I seen the first screening in Derry yesterday and was thrust to the deepest, darkest parts of humankind. Some really scary bits in it, suspense wise, especially when the joker has the knife in that guys mouth and is explaining his scars to him. I was so intrigued and guiltily sadistic at the same time. Heath Ledger as the joker is immense. What a shame he died. I could have done with another sequel with the Joker but kudos to the man anyways. I wonder if the joker really did get to him? 10.title: "The night is always darkest just before the dawn."
10.content:
This is one of the greatest films of all time, not to mention THE GREATEST superhero film. Everything about this movie is completely stunning.

The acting is second to none, with Heath Ledger's portrayal of the Joker being the best villain of any movie in history. He truly deserves an Oscar. Christian Bale does a stunning performance as Batman, despite the Joker, in my opinion, being the main character. Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine do good performances as Bruce Wayne's assistants. Gary Oldman plays one of my favorite characters, James Gordon, and he delivers a sense of hope in all of the chaos. Lastly, Aaron Eckhart delivers an excellent performance as Harvey Dent. I thought his performance was great, and his ability to play Two-Face was good.

The story was also great. This was the first superhero movie in which I felt a real prescence of true evil. In the Spiderman films, there was never a sense of evil like this. Because of this evil, it also felt like Batman was a true hero, not some guy in tights. This film proves "The night it darkest just before the dawn." While there was never a dawn, this film proves that in darkness, there is always light.

Best movie ever, RIP Heath Ledger

10.title: The tactic
10.content: I know this is going to start some trouble,but i gotta write it.There is a tactic used in movies that does get on my nerves,but i don't get bent over it because i know that's how society can be.(Not how it always is.)What movie makers do in order to keep the audience with the story and not become upset with the death of a character,is make said character a black person.The fact of the matter is that most of the viewing public is white,and nothing is more upsetting than a white person biting it.This is not always the case,many,many movies off plenty of white people,i know.Most of the time it is within the context of the story-horror,serial killer,etc.-but during some movies it is used,and it does work.Before you fly off the handle and post some juvenile hate-filled rant my way,do some research for yourself.That being said,i loved this movie-see it in Imax please-but i was disappointed to see this tactic used so often in it.The joker killed about four black people,which didn't bother me too much,but i don't see why they couldn't have mixed it up a little.

10.title: this is a bigger blockbuster than anyone could have believed.
10.content:
The Dark Knight Rating: ***** Certificate: 12 Duration: 152 minutes Director: Christopher Nolan Starring: Christian Bale, Heath Ledger, Aaron Eckhart, Gary Oldman and Maggie Gyllenhaal Best Bit: The Joker Worst Bit: Maybe to talkative at times If you liked Batman Begins and well great films you'll love this.

Well first of all I would like to mention that me and my friend where so syked about this film we went all the way up to Birmingham to see it in IMAX!!! (It's like a HD version of the cinema). We live in Exeter. But I think was totally worth it.

The film begins with... well I really don't want to say, as its all just brilliant and I don't want to ruin it, but I will say that the story will amaze you, inspire you and captivate you in the film. This film contains everything a blockbuster needs a hero wearing a cape, a demented villain, a bad ass car, a bad ass car chase, gadgets, an all-star stellar cast, fighting and EXSPLOSIONS.

Defiantly one of the most noticeable features of this film, is the cast. Christian Bale does fantastic once again in playing a much more physical Batman in this film, Katie Holmes turned down the role of Rachel in this film so she has been replaced by Maggie Gyllenhaal who may not be as eye-catching as Katie but makes a much better performance, to be honest it appears Aaron Eckhart has been slightly overlooked in the upcoming of this film, I know he wont be now as he will be giving many people nightmares. So now I come to the late Heath Ledger, so people think that the only reason his performance is getting such good reviews is the fact that he is no longer with us, well they are mistaken, he is fantastic. OK some of the credit goes to the Nolan's for creating such a psychotic and demented villain, but they made a role that needed an actor who could pull it off, and that's just what they got, he is amazing, nearly every scene in this film is memorable.

The Director Christopher Nolan is probably my favourite director. He's not only directed the brilliance of the Prestige he's also British, which is an achievement in itself. One thing I have noticed is that he likes casting British or non-American actors in American roles. Yes Christian Bale is British.

I pretty sure that this film could be classed as a British film as many scenes where filmed in Britain, many actors are British or not American, the directors British and Michal Caine is in it.

So overall the story is top  notch, there's a stellar cast, great action, constant suspense and well this is a bigger blockbuster than anyone could have believed.

10.title: The Greatest Superhero Movie ever made. Period.
10.content:
Batman has always been my favourite comic book hero, and watching The Dark Knight makes me overwhelmed that Nolan has truly done justice himself to the Caped Crusader.

With all the summer superheroes films leading up to this one; such as Iron Man and Incredible Hulk, The Dark Knight delivers a quality feature film, that at points in the film you forget is even a Superhero flick. With outstanding performances from an All-Star cast, The Dark Knight has single handedly schooled all Superhero films ever created. I felt at the beginning that I was going to be impressed but with the Introduction alone I was blown away, Nolan keeps the film very experimental in ways, almost getting right to the point rather than these derogotory title sequences that we often have to sit through at the beginning of a Superhero film. He creates tension and gives you a slight thriller aspect to the film, causing you to feel very anxious and at times even petrified about what is taking place.

I have never really been a big fan of Heath Ledger, I have enjoyed him in films, however when I read a year and a half ago that he was to play the Joker I must admit I was disappointed, However, after seeing him portray the Joker in such a twisted and psychotic manner, I can truly say that he owns that role. Michael Caine, once again portrays and outstanding performance as Alfred as Bale does of Bruce Wayne, however Aaron Eckhart was also outstanding, an really does shine throughout this film, often stealing the spotlight from Bale, as Ledger does.

Nolan kept the film as a film, and didn't sell out for a strain to make the film 'child-friendly' which often you look around the theater and think to yourself, 'are these kids allowed to watch this?' The film is very grown up, and feels just as fresh and original as Begins, exactly what a re-boost of a franchise should be. Also the fact that he wrote alongside his brother just goes to show he had the vision for where the film should go, way before they even switched a camera on.

The action and suspense is also not solely caused by the Heroes and Villains but is also surprisingly caused by the situations, and even the pedestrians, or those with lesser roles. Gary Oldman, also really delivers as Gordon.

Where do I end? I simply can't. In simple terms, GO AND SEE THIS FILM, and if you have already, then see it again, and again, and one more time. Christopher Nolan hats off to you. You have brought us what will be the Greatest film of 2008, and the greatest Comic book adaption Superhero movie of all time.

10.title: Nolan's Masterpiece of Morality and Madness
10.content:
In 2008, director Christopher Nolan released 'The Dark Knight', the second installment in his Batman trilogy. Today, it stands as not only one of the best superhero films ever made, but also as an unparalleled masterpiece in modern cinema.

Set in the city of Gotham, 'The Dark Knight' explores the chaos that ensues when an anarchic criminal mastermind known as the Joker (Heath Ledger) begins a deadly reign of terror. Batman (Christian Bale), District Attorney Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart), and Lieutenant Jim Gordon (Gary Oldman) must work together to try and restore order.

Christian Bale's portrayal of the haunted and determined Bruce Wayne/Batman deepens the complexity of the character. Still, the film is indisputably stolen by Ledger's portrayal of the Joker. His performance is bone-chilling and mesmerizing, brilliantly capturing the essence of a character devoid of empathy and fueled by chaos. Ledger's posthumous Oscar win for Best Supporting Actor was a fitting tribute to this iconic performance.

The screenplay by Jonathan and Christopher Nolan is intricate and smart, layered with philosophical undertones. The dialogue is sharp and the plot tightly woven, ensuring the audience is riveted throughout. This film surpasses the superhero genre, delving into the realms of crime drama and psychological thriller.

Technically, 'The Dark Knight' is a marvel. Wally Pfister's cinematography beautifully captures the grit and grimness of Gotham City. The score by Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard is powerful, adding an intense aura to the film. The action sequences are choreographed and executed with precision, making for some unforgettable cinematic moments.

However, the film's greatest strength lies in its thematic depth. 'The Dark Knight' explores the dichotomy of good and evil, the nature of anarchy, and the price of heroism. It poses questions about morality and chaos, ensuring its relevance beyond the confines of the genre.

On the downside, the film is densely packed, and some viewers might find it overwhelming. However, the payoff is immensely rewarding, and repeated viewings only add to the appreciation of its complexity.

In conclusion, 'The Dark Knight' is a landmark in cinema, transcending the superhero genre to deliver a profound exploration of human nature. It is a film that is as thought-provoking as it is thrilling, driven by powerful performances and exceptional storytelling. In a genre dominated by spectacle, 'The Dark Knight' stands out as a masterwork of depth and substance.

10.title: My honest review
10.content:
This is NOT a superhero movie. it's NOT a comic book movie. this is a statement about the time which we live in, and how we want to see ourselves, what we could see ourselves as, and ultimately the dangers of what we can become... put simply: ledger does for the role of joker what Chris reeves did for superman. this is the new gold standard and could potentially forever change joker's image in pop culture. it will be almost impossible for anybody to do a plausible follow-up-- be it illustrated, live action, or animated-- that will be as effective as this one... this performance makes Nicholson's "darker" joker of 1989-- a performance raved about by bob Kane himself-- as campy-looking as Caesar Romero's joker of the 1960's TV show. ledger's character-portrayal could be called by any other name, put it in any other movie, and it would be the talk of Hollywood as one of the scariest characters in recent memory.

never mind the fact that in this movie, everything and everyone is the star getting equal screen time, including batman, joker, Harvey dent-- in a poetically brilliant portrayal by eckhardt-- Gotham city, Jim Gordon, Lucius fox, and all the tertiary characters and pyrotechnics..... never mind the basic storytelling flaws (among them characters "disappear" while other characters are still, technically, looking in their direction) and completely illogical time lines.... never mind that we still don't get an accurate explanation as to how any of batman's villains convince and recruit their hired thugs to devotedly do their bidding... never mind anything and everything that you would normally want to nit-pick. this film's main flaw is that it's TOO good. there was always a secret joy for fans in being unsatisfied, always complaining how the director never got this or that just right-- it always gave us, the audience, a reason to want and demand more attempts.... we always seemed to love the filmmakers' efforts more than the product given to us. but now that the joy of fan-kingdom complaining has been robbed from us, all i can say is: "thanks!!!!!!" go see it-- you'll be MORE than glad you did..... Must watch again

10.title: The Dark Pleasure
10.content:
I can't start talking about this movie in terms of its hype. No other movie, as far as I remember, had so many expectations from it than this one....and believe me, I have watched quite a lot of them. But somehow, only this one was able to give me goose bumps. What makes this latest installment of Batman so special for me, is the mere fact how complicated it is. And I know that for most of us, this doesn't really work for a summer block-buster. Nolan has taken a very bold and ambitious step in trying to make a beacon of hope for those of us, who want more than just another popcorn flick, just another movie based on a comic and just another action thriller with lots of explosions. Well, I, for one, really admire him for his courage. And from the reviews I have read, and the response it has received from general public (in terms of box office), I have to say......So do the many others. There isn't a lot to say, after all that has been said by everyone who was compelled to give his/her two cents. But, somehow, there is void there, which many of us have/might have failed to see. And that may be only discovered (IMHO) after multiple viewings. The very reason that makes it mammoth of a movie i.e. complicated and a long over drawn plot, is the very reason that makes it a little pedestrian. This was my opinion after I had watched it 3 times. But somehow, another viewing, all the pieces fell into their place. All I can say, is that this movie is way too layered, for a summer blockbuster. It's really a piece of art, which you can only enjoy once you have seen it miles away from the conventional bounds of a particular popcorn no-brainer movie. There are many examples, but I will state only one here. The way the movie ended, seemed like a stretch a quite unnecessary. I also thought that there was no need for batman to take the blame. But then after another viewing, I thought, I know why. This is because; he has to become more than a hero. A line that seemed like a cliché the first time. But, No..It was not. He had to change the minds of the people about him, so that he could be able to do more than what a hero does. Which other action movie has a climax based on an answer after soul searching? This may be way too much for a lot of us to understand and this should be one of the reasons for this movie to be such a big success and not just the performance by Late Heath Ledger. For me the most important thing was the dialogues. They were subtle yet eloquent. Action was better than the previous installment as well. Besides, having learnt that there were less CGI used than your average action flick, was also very good refreshing.

That said, it is not without its flaws. Some technology used, is not very plausible. The way, Two-face transforms into a villain, may seem like understandable at first..but doesn't really hold up, once you consider, why he didn't kill the joker, when he had the chance. The way, the movie stretches and keeps on going to include at least two features in one, also makes it a little over the top. But, even after all that, one has to take into account the complexity of the plot, loyalty to its source material, and the will of the Chris Nolan to make it critical study of the world we live in. No one said that art is perfect (unless, it's abstract). Things change with the seeing eyes and one cannot dismiss what they see (Unless it's criticism just for the sake of criticism). But in the end, after all is said and done, one has to seewhat I can see and that is, changing the way summer blockbusters are these days. If you have not watched this movie, and it really doesn't matter the type of movies that you like, WATCH IT (with an open mind). It transcends the genre, it represents. Lastly, what gets to me, is this talk about how good a movie it is? Does it really deserve an Oscar? Its current position on IMDb top 250? ..What is all that? Why can't we just watch a movie and not try to make another argument based on our personal likes and dislikes. I have read all the comments of the people who think, it deserves 1 out of 10. I don't agree with them, but I don't have a bone to pick with them either. What matters is that for many sensible people, it's just a movie. It's not perfect. It may have offended many batman fans, by being not the way they envisioned a batman movie. Still, it has its appeal and mostly, it is different from all the other movies based on comics. For those, who wouldn't listen; why not try to save your energy for more important issues? My opinion is, it's a great movie. It will stand the test of time, and has raised the bar for all the action, thriller and comic movies.

10.title: True Batman
10.content:
I walked out of this movie in absolute shock. It took me a few minutes before I could even speak and even then I couldn't for the life of me come up with the words powerful enough to describe what I had just experienced. Until Christopher Nolan came around and made Batman Begins I had always thought the pinnacle of the Batman Franchise was the old 90s Batman Cartoon. These new movies though have nailed it. Not just in the traditional way wither, Nolan and his brother aren't afraid to take risks and try new things with the characters and go in directions never explored before while still staying true to the Batman universe.

The entire movie was almost too intense keeping me energized and wide awake despite it being 2:00 in the morning and made me want more and more, when it ended I already wanted to see the next one (if there will be one) or at the very least watch it again, and again, and yet again still. The story arc is tragic and original throwing you curve ball after curve ball about what is going to happen next, and when it is obvious what is about to happen it left me unable to believe that someone was brave enough to actually do that. T One bit that was very impressive was that while several times in the film people suffered truly horrific deaths, but Nolan didn't show them. It is true that the sight of someone bleeding to death on the ground will make people cringe, but what is even more powerful then showing said person dying is letting the imagination of the people watching it go wild with hat happened to them.

The part the left me in awe more then any other though was the ending. It was completely unconventional, powerful, and a true showing of life in situations similar to this (if such a thing exists). Myself and everyone else in the theater stood up and clapped when the credits began to roll from the sheer power of the grand finale.

This movie is not perfect, there are flaws but thats the reality of all movies. There will always be something somewhere that can be ridiculed and used to look down on it. If you go see this movie do it with an open mind, don't go in with the mentality that its just another Batman or super hero movie. It will surprise you.

10.title: Great Movie! Heath Ledger is now larger than life!

If someone can do that, go ahead and give it to them otherwise have Heath be the second posthumous Oscar winner and give the trophy to his family! It would not be any more ridiculous than some of the other Oscars that have been given (i.e. Erin Brokovich, Three 6 Mafia, etc.) It would kind of be like Johnny Depp's Oscar nod for Pirates of the Caribbean. He should definitely be nominated for an Oscar if he doesn't win! Elsewhere, the story was good and the other performances were pretty decent. But Heath shines above them all in this film! Not even Michael Caine does as good of a job as he does! A great film. One of the best in recent memory!

10.title: Reaches new heights in superhero story-telling; phenomenal work.
10.content: A mature, layered and pacy thriller with excellent action sequences and one of the best on-screen villains of all time. What sets this apart from others in the genre is how straightforwardly gripping it is, keeping you on the edge of your seat as it races from one amazing sequence to the next, as well as the complex moral quandaries it presents to the audience without pretending they have easy answers. All this, and it still manages to keenly represent Batman in a way which will satisfy fans of comics and cinema alike. 10/10.

10.title: A dark and powerful superhero film

10.title: Masterpiece - 11 out of 10
10.content:
Surpasses Batman Begins.

Anyone who rates this under a 5 has issues. Now onto the review...

Let me begin by saying that I did not watch this movie until months after The Oscars and Heath Ledger's posthumous win which I assumed his death had been a major contributing factor. WAS I EVER WRONG - My apologies. Heath Ledger stole every scene he was in and brought depth and excitement to The Joker like none before him. Outside of the Batman universe, Heath's portrayal of the Joker is easily a top villain. As the movie credits rolled, a profound sorrow overcame me and I was ashamed of the selfishness I felt because this Joker would never again delight me. I mourned a second time.

The script is excellent and full of great character interactions. As usual, top notch acting straight across.

If I was pressed to find fault, I concur that Bale's voice change as Batman is not optimal; but this is really nit-picking because there is not much leeway as far as voice modulation goes and I'm sure he wanted to deviate from his predecessors.

The Dark Knight Rises is so wonderful that I fear for its part three sequel because I can't imagine anything better. However, if there is one person that could accomplish this, it is Christopher Nolan. I hope he makes me eat my words.

10.title: One of the most incredible cinematic experiences . . . ever!!!
10.content:
This film went beyond my expectations! The Nolans have taken the Batman story to a new level. Some won't like it because the film is EXTREMELY dark and gritty, and I highly recommend that children not see this movie, but it is a true masterpiece.

All of the acting is great, but Heath Ledger was amazing! The hype is true for once, and the man's performance as the Joker is one of the most impressive that you will ever see. I have never been a Heath Ledger fan, the guy had never been in any films of my interest, so I'm not saying this just because his recent and tragic passing. He steals the show.

The Joker is so sadistic, he manages to be both terrifying and, at times, humorous. The rest of the cast does an amazing performance, and the writing and directing are second to none.

Go and see this movie!

10.title: Batman Triumphant!! The Caped Crusader soars above and beyond all its predecessors!
10.content:
Warning!! ( Many spoilers)

First Tim Burton directed two films opening the legacy. Next, Joel Schumacher continued two more films, but for lesser quality. Now Chris Nolan has made "Batman Begins" and "The Dark Knight," something to treasure forever.

There are three things that won me over with this movie. First, this film pushes the envelope to a near R-Rating. There so much gunfire, explosions, and gruesome images that I felt tensed of what would happen next. I love movies that take risks because if more movies exercised play-safe techniques, we would be watching "Batman and Robin" all over again. Second is Heath Ledger's brilliant performance. Although less comical, ledger's character is realistic, menacing, and truly horrifying. A true psychopath, which Ledger brings so much realism.
