Even if there is no posthumous Oscar nomination, Ledger will most definitely live on as a movie legend. Not a single online hater complaining about the film's length, darkness, or complex story can take away Ledger's status. Finally the third thing is the film has first-rate storytelling. There is a surprise twist and a nail-biting action sequence at every corner. The action is also evenly balanced with the plot and characterization. Its more than just a good v.s. evil film. There is real conflict and real turmoil that plays on both sides of law enforcers and law violators.

The film concerns Batman/Bruce Wayne trying to make the city a better place. while crooks and copycat vigilantes run amok, the Joker associates himself with powerful crime bosses. Through countless terrorist attacks, the Joker commands the citizens of Gotham to do whatever he wants as long as he controls their fears and emotions. Sometimes there is no clear motive or explanation about the Joker's past, but he wants to unmask Batman and try to make him appear villainous in the face of Gotham. The Joker is anything but a two-dimensional villain. He had a conflicted childhood just like Bruce, but he uses his angst, his rage, and his emotions to hurt others rather than protect them. Bruce Wayne on the other hand soon wants to hang up his Batman suit and settle with his love Rachel Dawes, since DA Harvey Dent is leading a revolution against all citywide crime. That is until later, when Harvey Dent makes a transformation into the monstrous Two-Face. Who is just as scary and sinister as the Joker. From that moment onward its a crazy roller coaster ride of thrills, unpredictability, and tragedy.

Although the movie is long, there is sharp editing, outstanding performances, great stunt work, a superb script, and enough memorable moments to make the 2.5 hours zip by. A MOVIE MASTERPIECE.

10.title: Brilliant
10.content: This is probably the best film that I have seen in a very long time. I have been a fan of Batman ever since I picked up my first comic book many decades ago. Seeing the various portrayals of the Caped Crusader have been interesting but none have enthralled me as much as Batman Begins and The Dark Knight. But the standout performance was Heath Ledger as The Joker. His portrayal of The Thin White Duke Of Death was astounding. To be quite honest, I did not think he had it in him but happily, I was wrong. Chris Nolan has outdone himself and has finally given the comic book fans a movie worthy of the genre. The movie itself was well written, brilliantly acted and the special effects were eye popping. It is about time that we were given intelligent films like this and we have Nolan, Bale, Oldman and Ledger to thank.

10.title: One of the best movies ever
10.content: Im a huge Batman fan and this is my favorite movie. Such a pleasant surprise heath ledger was. Although Christian Bale is my 3rd on my best batman list. He did a good job. Christian mouth is what trows me off. Its so unique its hard for me to believe people couldn't tell it was him. Heath took the joker character to a different current level not to say it was better than Jack Nicholson. Gary Oldman was a great Gorden. and what a surprise in two-face, Arron Eckheart was great. I loved Tommy Lee Jones in Forever, which is my 2nd favorite Batman film and my favorite Batman Val Kilmer. lol But that could change with how good Ben Afflec dose which I'm thinking is going to be great. He knows this will make or break his career. George Clooney is dead to me.

10.title: The "knight" is darkest before the dawn
10.content:
Let me start with this statement: This is the greatest comic/superhero movie adaption ever to be achieved to date. I have been keeping up with every update on this film since is saw "Batman Begins". Let me tell you that this film was everything that I could have hope for.

"Begins" gave audiences a relatible Batman(Bruce Wayne)that everybody could understood and could cheer for. We also saw an interesting and realistic take on Gotham City and characters such as James Gordon, Alferd Pennyworth and Lucios Fox. We got to know these characters and settings to the point were audiences wanted to see more.

Director Christopher Nolan and his crew gave audiences and fans more than an excellent film but literally quite a masterpiece. "The Dark Knight" ranks with sequels such as "The Godfather: Part 2" and "Terminator 2: Judgement Day". This film contains intelligence and genus in all directions. Christorpher Nolan was born to created these two batman films; Christan Bale once again plays Batman like he actually is Bruce Wayne; but the most talked about and hyped up character of this film is of course The Joker. The late Health Leger give us a funny, evil and psychotic Joker that no one has ever scene before. Leger's performance is brilliantly played and is very Oscar worthy. Through out my viewing of this show, i was anticipating every scene that included the Joker. Health Ledger and The Joker mixed together in this film like Anthoney Hopkins and Hanibal Lector did; his performance was humorous but creepy at the same time.

The introduction of Harvey Dent(played by Aaron Echart) in this film was interesting. It shows how Dent is driven by love and compassion for helping people and how he is driven to the point were he snaps and become sometime completely different. A very pleasing performance done by Aaron Echart is believable in a every aspect.

"The Dark Knight" proves that even a Batman movie can break box office records and go down in cinematic history. I give Cristopher Nolan's "The Dark Knight" a solid 10/10

10.title: Absolutely brilliant and stunning
10.content:
The dark knight is one of the most superb and best DC comic book movies that I have seen in a while. I would say that it's probably better than all the marvel comic book movies that I have seen combined together. It has a good story which most audiences will find very moving and thrilling to watch on the big screen including great action sequences throughout the whole movie which keeps you on the edge of your seats.

I think the whole cast have done a brilliant job in the movie. Starting with Christian Bale who looked in better shape for this movie as he did in the previous one and in this one you see him as a new improved and better batman that he takes to the next level. Secondly Heath Ledger who stole almost every scene in the movie and is my favourite, did a hell of a job playing as the terrifying Joker and to be honest I couldn't possibly imagine anyone else playing the Joker more perfectly as the way he did it. It is also probably the best joker I have seen in a batman movie on the big screen so god bless you Heath Ledger, rest in peace. Also in between Aaron Eckhart did a fantastic job playing as Harvey Dent in the first half of the movie and then seeing his transformation into 2 face in the second half is brilliant to watch on the big screen because he's a very talented actor and has done a good job even though I didn't imagine him to portray this role. With introducing 2 Face this adds another mixture to the story which makes the movie work very well since its not only about the Joker and I also enjoyed watching how well Aaron and Heath work together on screen which adds another dynamic to the story and has 2 villains instead of one.

As for rest of the supporting cast including Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman, Maggie Gylenhall, Nestor Carbonell, Eric Roberts, Cillian Murphy, Michel Jai White and William Fitchner. I think they all did a phenomenal job starting with Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman who reprise their roles and both provide a bit of comic relief and sense of humour in the film which works quite well. As for Gary Oldman he gets more screen time in this movie as he did in the previous one and gets to do more things like becoming involved in some of the action sequences which is really good. Maggie Gylenhall does a great job playing Rachael Dawes even though she replaced Katie Holmes she still plays the role convincingly and in this one you see her become part of a love triangle and dilemma into choosing between Bruce Wayne or Harvey Dent which adds romance into the mix among the chaos. I also enjoyed watching Eric Roberts who played a great mob boss better than Tom Wilkinson in the first one with a bit of sense of humour. On the other side Michel Jai White also did a good job playing the gang leader role even though he had less screen time, but he did manage to have at least one or 2 funny lines in the movie which made it great to see him come face to face in 2 scenes that he has with the joker in the movie. It was also great to see Cillian Murphy back as the Scarecrow even though he did a great job in the first one, I was still disappointed that he did not get enough screen time in the movie and only appeared briefly in the beginning because it would have been great to see him team up with 2 face and joker that could have made the movie even more better with 3 villains. It is a possibility that he could come back in the 3rd batman movie as a full time villain that's if there is one. Last of all Nester Carbonell and William Fitchner did great in portraying their roles as Mayer and bank manger since they are 2 popular actors that you will probably see in Lost and Prison Break which is quite good since they are in the movie having small and big roles.

I think the crew also deserve credit for making this film and putting in a lot of hard effort to create the sound and special CGI effects including the beautiful music score for the movie and excellent directing from Christopher Nolan who deserves an Oscar award.

Above all I think this movie is awesome and defiantly worth watching. Personally I recommend it to anyone who is a batman fan or not and if you haven't seen batman begins then don't bother watching this film at all unless you have seen the first one.

10.title: The 'Darkest' of all Knights
10.content:
This is a very dark movie and Heath Ledger's Joker is the darkest it gets. The entire movie is like an eerie roller coaster ride.

There's not much CGI here, only a truly haunting score and dashes of the Joker's mesmerizing lines. The action is kept from being overblown and that's really encouraging in this era of mindless CGI-driven summer blockbusters.

More importantly, the story of Bruce Wayne is taken to new high (or low). This is unlike any comic book movie you have ever seen, one that you'll keep coming back to. All of the actors deserve their kudos, but Ledger overshadows them all.

10.title: Heath Ledger owned The Dark Knight
10.content:
Who said sequels suck? Well, The Dark Knight throws this theory on its head and shreds it to pieces with Christopher Nolan, Christian Bale and Co back for the sequel to Batman Begins.

Heath Ledger plays The Joker and he owns the role for sure, putting Jack Nicholson to shame. I wonder what Heath did to get into the head of the Joker or vice-versa.

It's a shame Katie Holmes didn't return for the sequel.

10.title: Going out in style
10.content:
The death of Heath Ledger was a terrible thing but if you were to go out at a young age as an actor at least he went out with a bang. He crafts a character with the Joker on a completely different plateau then any actor to ever play the role before. There's been tons of actors to play the Joker previously to him, most notably Jack Nicholson in Tim Burton's 1989 version of Batman. But all of their performances were too comic book like and not a realistic portrayal of a character.

Christian Bale brings another strong performance as Batman/Bruce Wayne. The rest of the cast is quite stellar also. Maggie Gyllenhaal replaces Katie Holmes in her role and doesn't miss a beat.

This movie probably went ahead of Memento as Christopher Nolan's best work so far in his career.

10.title: Top 5 film of all time
10.content: Maybe even my number one!!! I'm not a crazy Batman fan or DC enthusiast, I actually love Superman. I'm writing this review at the end of 2019 when Marvel (MCU) dominates the cinema. Having watched all the MCU movies, and many more non Superhero movies since 2008, I still can not compare Dark Knight Rises to any film made since. The cinematography, acting, score, and all Oscar categories are perfectly balanced in this movie, Christian Bale is magnificent, but somehow still in the shadow of the late Keith. All cast preformed to perfection, no disappointment at any point. Facebook and other social media outlets over the years often give short scenes from the film, and each one puts me in euphoria of motion picture. I'm no movie critic, and not a frequent review writer, but this movie deserves it. Thank you Mr Ledger, you left this world with a gift to all of us!!!!

10.title: Is it Nolan's greatest?
10.content:
I simply cannot put it into words how phenomenal this film was. I haven't had as much fun with a film like this since I watched Interstellar a few months ago. I get I'm watching this film seventeen years after its release, but it still holds up phenomenally.

The whole movie is riddled with great scenes. Starting with the opening scene of the Joker robbing the bank. It's a spectacular beginning to the film and it shows us Heath Ledger's take on the iconic villain. Ledger's Joker was a sight to see. He was sassy, funny and intimidating. Harvey Dent was also a great addition to the film. His facial CGI hasn't exactly aged well, but Nolan was able to keep the face hidden to make it easier. Dent also gave one of the best quotes of life being, "You either die a hero, or live long enough to see yourself become the villain". Very good stuff! The action in this film is turned up a ton from the previous entry. It's got loads of tension and some excellent high paced action scenes, most notably the car chase through Gotham. Seeing the Bat-mobile get turned into a motorbike was badass and Christian Bale riding his bike through the city was so cold. Finally, the ending scene is simply perfection. Seeing Batman become the villain and Gordon watching him ride off into the night whilst he says one of the best monologues ever:

"He's a silent guardian, a watchful protector. A Dark Knight..."

Before I finish off, I just have to pay tribute to Heath Ledger. It's such a shame that Ledger passed away before he could see his work in this film and he will be dearly missed by the world.

Overall, The Dark Knight is easily one of the greatest superhero films ever made. It's probably one of my favourite from Nolan and my favourite from DC as a whole. Easily one of the best recommendations I can give.

10.title: A Movie of Epic Proportions
10.content:
The Dark Knight truly exceeded all of my expectations for the film. The opening scenes involving William Fitchner and Cillian Murphy are arguably some of the best opening scenes of any film. Throughout the movie not only did the story keep a steady and interesting pace, but it also catered to the fanboy and the film-goer who is truly absorbing every nugget. The main cast was truly superb (with the possible exception of Maggie Gyllenhall), and the minor casts were just as well cast. The mayor is well-cast with the guy from Smokin Aces. Anthony Michael Hall truly seems like a reporter, and Cillian Murphy's minor cameo has the Scarecrow creates the allusion of a true universe.

This movie has a definite re-watch value. Jokes in this film are actually entertaining and do not detract from the dramatics of the more climactic scenes. At one point, a tense situation at a hospital is diffused by amusing antics from the Joker. The amount of effort put into the editing and scripting of even the most unimportant of clips allow the viewer to take in a world not our own, in a city that is understandable and very much possible. The messages in the film are obvious but not overbearing and certainly relevant.

Simply stunning.

10.title: Beautiful, chilling, and haunting... not words I usually use for a Batman Movie
10.content: I won't deny, I went to see this today with expectations of it being a great movie. The Batman series has generally been great and this one promised to be so with a fabulous cast. My expectations were blown away, this was an incredible movie. Hands down, my favorite Batman movie and within my top ten favorites of all times. Heath Ledger gave me chills as Joker, I never even thought about that I was watching him, I was merely watching Joker as never seen before. He's the ultimate in villains and will leave you thinking about the pencil trick for a while to come ;). The rest of the cast did excellent too though Joker really did steal the scenes. He's memorizing and terrifying all in one. The movie itself was unreal it was so intense. You had no idea what the next turn was and it had you on the edge of your seat in anticipation. The stunts pulled were incredible and just the whole thing had me reeling. It was far better than I had expected and not just because Heath portrayed an amazing Joker. The whole package was well worth seeing in the theater and I will be adding this to my collection as soon as it comes out. Perhaps even snagging a few as Christmas presents for the family because this movie should be seen by all.

10.title: Revolutionising the role of a Villain!
10.content: The movie was superbly directed with all the roles performing excellently, especially Heath ledger's who in my opinion has revolutionised the role of a villain! From now onwards this monumentos performance will be the cornerstone of acting.

10.title: Surpassed All Expectations!
10.content:
I was so thoroughly impressed by this movie in every way humanly possible. I never liked the Batman movies growing up, especially after the first movie with Michael Keaton. Batman Begins grabbed my attention much because of my love for Christian Bale's acting. Together, Bale and Nolan have resurrected a dead franchise.

I am surprised this movie earned a PG-13 rating. This movie was so dark and tragic, I would've guessed R-rating. I have no quarrels with the movie's darkness and am even more impressed this movie WASN'T designed with children in mind.

This movie will take you for a ride on an emotional roller coaster. After Rachel's death, I nearly cried for Harvey and his sadness. It was overwhelming. As for the next movie, I would've liked to see Nolan save two-face for the finale. He entered two-face in this movie to give the sorrow and sadness factor. I can't think of any villain who could be better than two-face and especially Joker were in this movie. Heath...you deserve an Oscar hands down.

10.title: Best example of a true villain.
10.content:
In most 'Super Hero' genre movies, it's the usual action that drives the plot, and the emotion is a reaction, rather than the force. And, up until now, very VERY predictable and formulaic.

In every movie I have ever seen featuring a villain, it has a motive, or a past, or a reason for the villainy. Animal villains don't need a reason unless it is given them by the author or writer/director, as diseased, tampered with or just plain animalistic cravings. The Joker in Dark Knight for the first time is given no back story, no reason, no excuse. He killsbecause he does. Sometimes there IS no reason. Michael Caine's character explains it succinctly when he uses a personal story of a jewel thief in a jungle that just threw away the jewels after killing many people in the attempt. No 'rational' explanation. That is what makes The Joker in Dark Knight so disturbing, and memorable in any form of media. He is just...inhuman, or non-animal. Hannibal Lecter was once 'normal', and although there is no real explaining his behavior, he had a past, and we can relate. The Joker here laughs at his own impending death, not expecting saving. Just does not care, because caring would be human, or alive. This Joker is already dead and has become something 'else'. Something not to try to figure out, reason with or investigate. Just simply needs destroying, at all costs. Because this 'bad guy' brings out the actual evil in those he comes across. Even today's terrorists have a reason for killing and destruction. The Dark Knight's Joker has no such minor flaws. He just destroys the same way a virus does. This Joker IS a virus, and just as a phage spreads destruction and chaos to everything it touches, although the death of the host will lead to it's end, so does this Joker. Christian Bale's Bat Man comes to term with this, and must accept into himself the corruption for just having come in contact with it. But survives it, irrevocably changed.

THAT..is what villainy really is. And what makes The Dark Knight stand out and above all Hero movies that came before.

10.title: Gritty & Unapologetic
10.content:
It took me until I woke up this morning to realize the awesomeness of this picture, which I saw last night at midnight. Without spoiling anything, just know that this movie is gritty and complex with a huge amount of depth in both the plot and the characters. It's extremely uncompromising as far as how one would think a major studio would handle a major comic book hero franchise. Most superhero/comic book movie plots' are set up for the sole purpose of creating a franchise and selling it to death. This is the opposite (not saying the conclusion doesn't beg for more answers, story & resolution). However, it's extremely unapologetic in the plot and characters and just goes in ways that you wouldn't expect a comic book movie to go. It's mature and adult like, you forget it is even a comic book movie. It's in your face from the moment it starts until the after the credits roll. The 2 1/2 hour runtime appears long, but the plot captivates you from the start and won't let you go. There's nothing that can be cut away from this film, as it would undermine the complexity and richness of the plot and characters.

Ledger is better than you could have imagined, as is Eckhart! Bale, Oldman, Caine, Freemon...amazing!! Go see this movie. It is the best film of the last two years and one of the best of all time!!

10.title: The Greatest Superhero Film Of All Time
10.content:
The Dark Knight is probably one of the greatest films of all time, and is undoubtedly the greatest superhero of all time WITHOUT A DOUBT. It blows any MARVEL or other DC film miles out of the water. This is mainly due to Heath Ledger's (RIP) stellar performance as The Joker, DC's most iconic villain.

Christian Bale's Batman is good, possibly a little comically voiced, and is a great counterpart to Ledger's Joker, as he embodies everything the Joker is against.

Truly an exceptional achievement by both Christopher Nolan, Hans Zimmer (music) and of course Heath Ledger. This film will go down in history.

10.title: To Date, The Best Film I've Ever Seen
10.content:
A huge fan of the Batman movies, I have been excited since the end of Batman Begins. Picturing how the Joker would be portrayed in a film directed by Christopher Nolan flat out excited me from that last scene. When Warner Bros. announced that the Joker would be played by Heath Ledger, I thought, "Heath Ledger, the guy from the cowboy movie?" I had never seen Ledger in any films before, and definitely could not see him pulling off the Joker. I mean, come on. The Joker is crazy, insane, morose, I could go on all day. Honestly, I could not see Ledger doing anything near what I expected from Nolan. Boy, was I wrong...

My friends and I had been scrambling for tickets to see The Dark Knight at the ever popular midnight showing. However, (quite embarrassingly so) none of us could drive past the PA Junior License Curfew of 11:00 PM. We thought to take the bus, go with older friends, or sheepishly ask one of our parents to come along with us. I was scared I wouldn't see it opening weekend. But what are sisters for? My sister, an intern for NBC10, had told me about a month ago that she had entered a contest to win tickets to the July 17th Philadelphia premiere of the Dark Knight. "A long shot," I recall telling her. Though she did not win the tickets, her boss had plenty of extra tickets, which he was not reluctant to give away to employees. My sister nabbed 2 tickets, each with one guest permitted. Sorry to my friends, but how many times does this happen to someone? I was nervous at first, asking people I work with what its like to see a movie on IMAX. "Can you see the whole picture?" "Am I going to be looking up the whole time?" Needless to say, I could see everything, and my neck was nice and comfortable in the bucket chairs at the Franklin Institute. Enough about my experience, let's talk about the movie.

I had already declared (without seeing it) the Dark Knight to be my favorite movie of the summer, and quite possibly the best Batman film to date. My heart was pounding in the opening minutes as a result of the overwhelmingly large screen and the excellent camera work, but it settled down throughout the two hours and thirty-two minutes. As the movie went on, I thought to myself, "This is incredible." Christian Bale has already won my vote for the best Batman since seeing his stellar performance in Batman Begins. He did not disappoint in his second showing. Charming and witty as Bruce Wayne or heroic and physical as Batman? Bale proved he can do both, and both well. Although his performance is undeniably spectacular, he does not earn the Best Performance for this film. That, my friends, would go to the late, absolutely great Mr. Heath Ledger.

As stated before, I did not see Heath Ledger as someone who could do wonders to Batman's undisputed rival. Seeing him in trailers and pictures before seeing the movie itself restored faith in Christopher Nolan. However, neither the trailers nor pictures did justice to the performance Ledger gave in the Dark Knight. His voice, his makeup, his general being on screen simply blew me away. Being able to transform himself from a character such as Brokeback Mountain's Ennis Del Mar to a corrupt, evil character such as the Joker truly showed me how versatile the man was. Now, as I had mentioned earlier, I have never seen any of his films before. The Dark Knight was probably the best way to introduce myself to Heath Ledger. This may upset whoever is kind enough to read my review, but I would like people to know what I am about to say. Quite honestly, since the day I heard Heath Ledger has passed, I hadn't really cared. But how could I be if I had never seen any of his films and knew so little about him? Thanks to his performance in the Dark Knight, I now care not only about the actor he was but also the person he was. My hat is off to you, Heath Ledger; may you rest in peace.

The Dark Knight is truly magnificent. As I'm sure anyone who has visited the IMDb page for the Dark Knight has already seen it, I recommend it to anyone and everyone. I honestly could not see how anyone could dislike this film. It is by far the best film I have ever seen, and so far, the highlight of my summer.

1 million/10

Jordan

10.title: Perfection
10.content: This film, for lack of a better word, is perfect. I never thought that anything would surpass the original Batman (1989), but Batman Begins came very close to it, if not equaling it. Then this came out. This movie is easily the best Batman movie and in my opinion, one of the greatest movies ever made. It had everything in it, absolutely everything. People say that Ledger might win an Oscar because of his death. No sir, Heath Ledger will win an Oscar because he played the most amazing villain I have EVER seen, perhaps even better than Anthony Hopkins from silence of the lambs. The entire cast was brilliant but it was Ledger's performance that topped it all. I have seen this movie twice on imax and I plan to see it again. Christopher Nolan, you have earned my respect. I hope this movie breaks all of the box office records.

10.title: Well Done Nolan and Ledger.
10.content:
All that I can say is wow. This just might be the best film I've ever seen. I saw it on the day it came out and when I checked on this web site the next day it was already a 9.6 which is needless to say very rare. Who do we have to thank for that? Health Ledger of course. The whole time he was in the film he all ways had that swagger that smooth beautiful motion acting as a lunatic comic book character brought into the flesh. He disappears into the character so good that honestly this is the first time that I've ever been in a movie theater where audience members to the right and to the left of me were like "he's crazy". They said it more than once too. Usually when I go to the theaters I can't even relate to the characters and situations much less write reviews about them.

If your going to do a remake of something that has already been done many times over such as something of the comic book genre it's important to remember a very crucial formula. The comic book is the Bible, the cartoon is the mythology, but the movie is how it actually would have happened. Christopher Nolan understood this concept perfectly. Throughout the film you get the feeling that this is a series of spectacular events dropped in an ordinary world. There's no weird filming technique that distorts color, there's not any obsession on trying to make everything look shiny like there was in Daredevil, and there's no Matrix rip offs (bullet time, dudes doing suspiciously impossible jumps in slow motion). Nolan keeps it real. Are there alterations to the original story? There probably are, the last I heard joker got his scars after Batman knocked him into a tank of acid and that he was the one who really shot Bruce Waynes parents (they created each other). This is not the only story alterations. In the comics Ras Al Gould (if I misspelled that don't trip) was an immortal who found a way to keep young. In Batman Begins it's hinted that a Ras Al Gould immortal is just a titled given to boss ranking members of the League of Shadows the same way that emperor's of Rome accepted the titled "Caesar". Little twists like that might upset comic and cartoon fans, but what they must understand is that when your making a movie adaptation it helps if you include a bit of *realism*.

Most of the time though the biggest reason people don't like works such as this isn't because people know too much of the mythology and the original story but because they know too little. Allow me to explain, (by the way I'm about to get into some spoilers so if you haven't seen this movie yet then please don't get upset if you lose a sense of drama after reading this) there is a part in this movie when it appears that Gordon has been shot and killed, now me being a fan of the cartoon knows that Gordon has always been a prolific instrumental character, in other words a *main* character, and adaptation film makers usually aren't that stupid to kill off key characters so quickly, and as it turns out they weren't Gordon comes back after playing possum just in time to rescue Batman now when they showed his face the audience was confused... no really they were. One said "What?! I thought he died." and some were snickering cause they perceived this as the film makers just doing what ever they could to bring back a character, but me knowing what was going on all I did was smile and nod in approval. Also after it was over I over heard some douche bag saying it was boring. The joker was blowing up everything in sight, shooting people here and there, backstabbing his allies with ease and this man was going to call it boring? What kind of movies does this guy watch? (People in my home town of Salinas aren't exactly known for there brains... never move here... seriously.) What I think confused those people was Batman's overly righteous persona ex. refusal to kill, willingness to take blame, the dialog revolving around concepts of hope, and heroes, and doing good in face of danger. These people are just not familiar with what Batman represents. He's a symbol, he's a symbol of being righteous fighting powerful evil obstacles with his bare hands and coming away the winner. Sometimes it seems that no matter how good a movie is there's always going to be haters out there.

10.title: MCU movies could never
10.content: There has been atleast 20 movies that the MCU has produced, and none of them has surpassed this masterpiece, and I don't even know if another Comic book movie could pass this. The Dark Knight is just special, it is it's own kind, another level, no other superheo films could reach it and it has been at least 13 years since it's release. It's definitely ahead of it's time, it's not just your ordinary "theme parks" movies, it has depth, it crossed other genres such as drama, thriller, crime and yes I know some of MCU has this but none of them really achieves the same way The Dark Knight has done. The only movies I can think of that has the biggest potential was The Winter Soldier, but still The Dark Knight remains superior and will always be.

10.title: The best batman movie to date in my opinion
10.content:
This is peak Batman for me. Christian Bale as batman and Heath Ledger as the Joker is probably as good as we are going to get.

This is far darker and grittier than I was expecting. The acting is perfect all around. The pacing is amazing as it jumps from one scene to the next and keeps things moving along.

All the characters feel tormented by their choices or past which just adds to the whole feel of the movie. By the end of it you are left feeling just emotionally tired as the tension built and you just end up feeling sad for everyone.

Any movie that can evoke an emotional response from me has done it's job. So this one goes into my top best movies of all time category.

10.title: The Godfather of Superhero comics!
10.content: Ha Ha. Chris Nolan strikes again with this Epic drama action superhero movie. Here introduces a joker who had a habit of causing trouble around until worse that Batman come and stop him. But later Joker henchmen and himself started to cause a massive disaster around Gotham City and all hell collide between hope, love, hate, and a Tragical loss. Beautifully crafted and well directed,this is a godfather that deserve many Oscars. Heath Ledger is by way, the wonderful portrayal as a sadistic, psychiatric, and a sick man who just want to torture anything that gets in his way. Heath should get an posthumous academy award nomination or win that award for his performance. Let the Academy deserves what better for the people. IF anyone of you not see it or not see it, Go watch it. It became one of my favorite films of 2008!

10.title: The Dark Knight is a masterpiece
10.content:
The Dark Knight is a masterpiece! A truly brilliant film. Epic, action-packed, intelligent, dramatic. A sensational score. A cautionary tale about morality, moral dilemmas and their consequences, and the blurred lines between good and evil. Plus an exercise in BRILLIANT Film-making AND WRITING. The direction and cinematography are graphic, Gothic, and gripping.

OH...AND GIVE HEATH LEDGER AN Oscar!!! Not because he died. Truly, I feel this Oscar hype would exist even if he were alive today. Because, from an actor's point of view, his performance is one of the FINEST CHARACTERIZATIONS I have ever seen in a film character. It was a truly iconic performance and will be remembered. It is a well-crafted, nuanced performance while simultaneously going perfectly over the top. He doesn't play a comic book character, a stock villain, or the comedic relief...but a real man, albeit an insane one...a sadomasochist who doesn't care about killing our hero, but toying with him...unafraid to die or to feel physical pain but fully cognizant that the hero will not take his life because it poses him too difficult an ethical dilemma. How do you defeat a madman with absolutely nothing to lose? It's chilling and Ledger is truly magnificent. He is a true method actor and is transformed here. In that sense, he has crafted the most iconic screen villain, I think, ever.

Not even once do you see a GLIMMER of the actor behind the face paint. Everything about him from the physical ticks, the voice, the walk, the sadomasochism, the laughter, and delivery of some TRULY BRILLIANT DIALOGUE and deliciously evil one-liners...are INCREDIBLE. The part is extremely well-written and what I love even more is that Ledger and the writers don't try to offer some pop psychology explanation for why the Joker is this way. A truly fine performance that I cannot gush about enough. Give. Him. The Oscar.

But his is not the only good performance. All the actors are excellent in the film, especially Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon. A huge debt should be paid to the script, which is so intelligent. Oldman's speech in the final minute of the film is like lyric poetry, with the emotional, dramatic score pulsing underneath him.

It needs to be seen to be believed. The Dark Knight is an amazing film. A+

10.title: Where do I begin ..........
10.content: This is one of my favourite films in the world, I know that because I can watch it over and over and never get bored. I find new aspects of Heath Ledger's performance to appreciate every time I watch and what's more the longer I watch him the more I believe that he makes every other actor seem average in his presence. The intensity, the passion, the insanity is just mind blowing ...... he is the ultimate anti-hero, you wanna hate him but you realise he kinda makes so much sense. The real genius in this film is how it becomes very little about Batman, Christian Bale has always slightly grated on me so I have to except him and move on but the casting of a new Rachel is brilliant. Overall as a film lover I take away so much from the magic Nolan creates and I for one can't wait for the next one.

10.title: I thought this film was going to be. . .
10.content:
the Greatest Movie I have saw, but i was wrong... it was BETTER.

After watching all the film specials from HBO to Reelz channel and i thought i had ruin the film for myself, but yet it was still beyond anything i had ever expected. And it seems as if the only third installment that can be made is, F. Miller's, "Batman: Return of the Dark knight." H. Ledger's performance was sinister and gruesome. And should get and Oscar nomination; this is no sympathy for his death, because he makes Jack Nickelson's version look like a Saint. Don't get me wrong, his performance was still great. But this story is more complex and just when you think it will end it'll keep going until it says the hero we need to believe in.

This film is not a superhero movie it is an Epic.

10.title: "The Dark Knight" is a first rate high-octane action film and what I expected from Christopher Nolan
10.content:
"The Dark Knight" is what every action fan is wanting from summer blockbusters, like this one. I have seen "Batman Begins" so when I heard there was a sequel to this movie, I thought for sure it would beat out the previous Batman movies, and it did! Although, when hearing that Heath Ledger would play The Joker, I was optimistic because it wouldn't seem that he could reach the standards as playing The Joker.

After seeing this AWESOME movie and Ledger's portrayal as the Joker made me a believer that he should be getting that Oscar nomination. "The Dark Knight" explodes from the screen with high-powered action, twists and turns, great story, plot, and highly engrossing characters.

This movie is the best movie I have seen this year and maybe potentially all-time. When parents take their kids to see this movie I would suggest that if they are younger and get scared easily I would recommend that they watch the film first, due to some disturbing images and/or violence.

In the end, "The Dark Knight" is a must-see for all action and comic book fans. Although, the death of Heath Ledger was sad because I believed that he could have excelled in any future films. Though, he's not, I say, RIP Heath Ledger.

I hope he gets the Oscar as the Joker and should be on the top for best action villain.

This movie will be your best bet at the theater that is, if you love action films as I do. GO SEE "The Dark Knight" YOU WILL NOT BE DISAPPOINTED!!!!

10.title: Mindblowing
10.content:
"The Dark Knight" (2008) is a cinematic masterpiece that continues to captivate audiences with its unparalleled blend of storytelling, action, and profound thematic depth. Christopher Nolan's direction is both ambitious and precise, crafting a Gotham City that feels both gritty and grandiose, a perfect backdrop for the moral dilemmas faced by its characters. Christian Bale's portrayal of Batman is compelling, delving into the complexities of a hero burdened by his own sense of justice and sacrifice. Heath Ledger's performance as the Joker is truly iconic, a chilling embodiment of chaos and unpredictability that mesmerizes and terrifies in equal measure. Ledger's interpretation remains a testament to his talent and dedication, elevating the film to legendary status.

What I find most compelling about "The Dark Knight" is its exploration of morality and the blurred lines between heroism and villainy. The film challenges us to confront difficult questions about the nature of justice, the consequences of our actions, and the masks we wear in our daily lives. Each character, from Batman to Harvey Dent to the Joker, represents a facet of these themes, offering a nuanced perspective on the human condition.

Visually stunning and emotionally resonant, "The Dark Knight" is a triumph of storytelling that leaves a lasting impression. It's a film that not only entertains but also provokes thought and reflection long after the credits roll. For me, it stands as one of the greatest achievements in modern cinema, a testament to the power of storytelling and the impact of unforgettable performances.

10.title: its a super flick, no doubt..... but
10.content: it took me a couple of viewing, paying premium ticket price to make up my mind about this movie. (by the way thats a compliment) one simple fact. its a very good movie. after tim burton's batman, nolans's batman has come much closer to the actual character of a dark knight. superman and batman are the most respected and likable superheroes from the DC stable. and my personal favorite is Batman. it was disheartening to see how his image was reduced to mere popcorn comic hero. after a decade, nolan gave me a ray of hope with his version of batman. but never had a clue about how he was going to manage another magic trick as good as the previous one. surprises are always around the corner. not only the new magic trick was better than previous one, but went beyond my expectations. the dark knight is a good movie in almost every sense. the acting - direction - story line - music - action - the theme and the ideologies that are put across by the joker are worth pondering about. philosophy and actual day reality, makes one think beyond what a man in a mask or white paste can spit out. from a mere comic strip to a thinker's movie..... very few movies does that to an audience. a rare feat. winning the common people and the critics alike speaks volumes about this movie. still the movie has few short comings... but i would be happy to let them stay in front of this spectacular work. not but the least, my tribute to an outstanding performance by heath the joker.

10.title: One of the best movies ever!!!!
10.content: Probably Nolan's best movie and one of my favourite movies of all time with a great soundtrack and excellent acting from everyone.

10.title: well worth watching.
10.content:
I was surprised by this movie greatly. I went into the cinema having not seen batman begins and was expecting a film of mediocre thrills which would entertain me but not leave me coming down from an orgasm.

Let me just say, well, tissues were needed. All jokes aside however, this film kept me transfixed for the full duration with no actor or actress performing with any degree of shoddiness. The joker was an amazing well acted character and just amplifies the tragedy of Ledger's death. I would recommend this film to all people i met and i left the theatre feeling as if i'd robbed the place, 5 quid is a bargain for the movie itself and the hours of quoting that followed.

10.title: "Do You Wanna Dance With The Devil?"
10.content:
"Do You wanna dance with the devil?" was a piece dialogue that has stuck in my mind ever since the first Batman movie was released in 1989, which starred Michael Keaton as "Batman," Jack Nicholson as "The Joker," Billy Dee Williams as "Harvey Dent," Michael Gough and Kim Basinger as "Vicky Vale." Today, Jack Nicholson's role is still remembered as it was then and since then there have been quite a few "Batman" movies but none have really matched up to it until this one.

Here, this is revived by Christian Bale as "Batman," one of the three who continues to eliminate crime in Gotham City, Aaron Eckhart as "Harvey Dent," another one of the three who also continues to eliminate crime, Sir Michael Caine as "Alfred" Batman's butler and finally the late Heath Ledger as "The Joker" who takes over organised crime and eventually wants to kill "The Dark Knight." The movie also stars Morgan Freeman.

This movie, also known as "Batman: The Dark Knight" has to be one of the best movies this year  at least for a good summer attraction. But be warned it does contain some violence and some spectacular stunts as well.

Conclusion: This movie is one of the summer blockbusters this year and is worth watching if you like "Batman." Unfortunately one of the actors was not able to see this movie being released and that how well he has performed  the late Heath Ledger, who, I felt, suited the role very well and that it can be matched to Jack Nicholson. This movie definitely surpasses the hype that has been going on.

10.title: DC Comics best known hero is battling against Joker.
10.content:
Christopher Nolan approached DC Comics most published hero Batman, after his great movie "Memento ". In 2005, Batman Begins was huge movie. Bale has ability to be both hero and millionaire. Until, in 2007, Nolan reported, that there will be second movie. I am big fan of Batman as comic book hero, so i eagerly waited this brand new franchise, of Batman-biography. The Dark Knight was so dark approach to the comic, that some of the scenes were stunning.

I wont tell anything about the movie, because it's gotta be best movie script ever. Realistic, dark and full of action. If Michael Bay made this movie, Ben Affleck would be Bruce Wayne/Batman, Alfred would be Bruce Willis and Joker would be Adam Sandler. Thank god, that Nolan took the movie seriously. Ledger's Joker was so, bad! I mean, sadistic, full of insanity, craziness and little bit of " Clockwork Orange " Alex.

Even in this movie, Michael Caine and Gary Oldman gives yet good performances, after the first. They both fit in their parts, even Caine speaks a whole line, after someone asks advice. Oldman does so perfect role. Maggie Gyllenhaal made Katie Holmes look like bad actor. Maggie fit in the part perfectly. Aaron Eckhart is amazing. Not, that he is serious actor, he does his part so good, that even Tommy Lee Jones needs to learn something. But Morgan Freeman provides truly his dull role. I know, that he has personality problems, but he does not fit in the parts, when he plays mentor or assistant.

Heath's part is best in the whole movie. Laughter is full of insanity, acting is fearless, clothing resembles part punk and part insanity. Ledger takes the role so beyond, that Jack Nicholson's part is more funnier, than scarier. Heath steals every single moment. When he speaks that tone of his voice, you actually wet your pants.

Believe me, the third one will be much more epic than this. Nolan has been known, the best Batman-movie maker. Tim Burton is absolutely fantastic and Joel Schumacher is not fantastic. Joel is just pain in the butt.

What can i say? This movie has all. Great action scenes, realistic world, funny dark humor and great musics. Opening scene is amazing and brings the point of view, that the movie goes on, like train on fire!

10.title: Way so serious !
10.content:
I am sure that "The Dark Knight" would be one of the most thrilling experiences for almost everyone out there except Batman. He had everything.. We saw how he acquired his swift moves in "Batman Begins", he got Batmobile and now he has introduced his Batpod as well. With ever reliable "Alfred Pennyworth" and techwiz "Lucius Fox" on his side he just cannot go wrong, at least we thought like that and batman must have hoped the same.

But one man had different plans. His plan was to have no plans at all. No plans and no rules.. He just wanted to increase the criminal status of Gotham city and make it darker by executing some of his cute little... did I say plans? But the real beauty of the film is when the war between the good and the evil reaches another level. The joker starts questioning Batman's ethics and his existence itself and that puts him in a deep mental dilemma.

The action was superb, no overdose of CGI, you just cannot ask for more in the acting section, great score. But really.. this film stands out for two reasons. Christopher Nolan's incredible ability to get into each of the character's mind and present each and every minute issues that are going through their mind. We saw that in insomnia, in Memento. He is able to do the same with a comic character here. Thats just unbelievable. The other factor is of course Heath Ledger. But as far as I can see there is no ledger in this film. I can see only THE JOKER !!!!

10.title: It is everything they say it is!
10.content:
Breathtaking movie! Enjoyed every minute of it.

Spoiler Alert - My favorite scene. When the joker leaves the hospital in his nurse outfit and fumbles around with detonator to finally hitting the right button, and an awesome explosion ensues, now that's filmamking at its best!! Batman's cycle is pure eye candy, and Gotham city never looked better! The key to a great super heroe movie is a super villain. Heath Ledger takes the Joker role to the peak of evil. He steals every scene in the movie and becomes the baddest of the baddies yet he has his principles.

Great job!!! A Blu-Ray must have!!

10.title: The Dark Knight Crushes!
10.content: Contradictory to endless super-hyped big budgets films with fancy trailers, this one delivers the goods promised. I have been following this film ever since Lt. Gordon pulled out that fateful card at the end of a brilliant "Batman Begins". Following this trail has been a 3 year affair and as a die hard Batman Fan(atic), I was actually more nervous than excited at the prospect of finally seeing this film. On hand I knew that Christopher Nolan and "Cast & Crew" wouldn't really muck it up but on the other, it takes one greedy studio executive with an ego to decide the fate of the product deliveredthankfully, that was not the case!! From the 1st trailer to the 2nd to the 3rd, the prospect of this film making history becomes more and more apparent. As for the marketing, to have one half of perfectly sane people paint their faces and parade around town in the guise of lunacy coupled with the other half campaigning in their city's for a non existent District Attorney is nothing short of PURE GENIUS! The Viral Campaign (which I followed closely too) made the film all the more intriguing and by the time 18th July '08 came, a final question was still lingering in my mind: Would The Dark Knight live up to the Hype? To my luck and too my wishes, The Dark Knight Crushed! The film-making was Grade "A", the story (which filmmakers have a tendency to go overboard with sequels) was the finest balance that could have been struck between comic and film, the actors were nothing short of amazing and most importantly the product on the whole delivered 100% 30 seconds (literally) into the movie, I knew I was in for the ride of my life and by the end credits, I was ready to go on this ride for the second time. Heath Ledger's Joker shone, just as Christian Bale's Batman did in Batman Begins (and in The Dark Knight for that matter) There are no words that can fully express the magnitude of his performance, but I will say this in a staunchly heterosexual way: "I couldn't get my eyes off The Joker." Aaron Eckhart was superb in portraying Harvey Dent's tragic struggle with duality. The physical scarring looks Dead On! (no pink paint this time round thankfully) Maggie Gyllenhaal made a much better Rachael Dawes the Katie Holmes, probably comes largely from the fact that the character itself is not superfluous like she was in the last one. Michael Caine & Morgan Freeman do tend to make anything look good and this was no exception .A special thanks to Gary Oldman for giving me The Commissioner I've always wanted to see done right. Watching him play Gordan page for page is nothing short of raw pleasure. To the filmmakers, rather than merely supporting their film to the hilt (which I am as you can see) I really would like to genuinely thank Christopher Nolan and Crew for giving me 2 of the greatest films I've seen and for literally bringing Batman's Universe to life. I've seen it 4 times already and am definitely going for 5. There is no guessing how many stars I'm giving this oneI just wish I could give it 11. (or more)

10.title: Brilliant
10.content: This is by far one of the best movies I've ever seen... it really is 'up there with them' (the voting figures say it all really - already no.3 in top 250 all-time-best (was no.1 for few weeks) These new Batman movies make a great change from the old ones - whilst I was a little disappointed with batman begins THIS is a massive change - not only a good storyline with good effects but HEATH LEDGER steals the show - his acting and role as The Joker is superb - his comical attributes and psychotic ongoings leave you wanting more and more - Iam absolutely gutted Heath Ledger is dead as The Joker doesn't die in this movie but is captured meaning he could have played the role again in later movie(s) perhaps :( Lots of action from the start - the ONLY thing I didn't like was Batman's voice - a bit deep (sounds stupid) Go watch at the cinema - YOU WONT BE Disappointed!!

10.title: A Superb Flick
10.content: My thanks to Christopher Nolan for not blowing it. The Dark Knight was by far the BEST movie I saw this year. I haven't yet been so pleased with a "Superhero" movie. I walked away from this one with a big smile and chills. The acting was incredible and Heath Ledger's performance was a memorable one. He is by far the best movie villain to date. I came into this movie with low expectations (we all know how sequels go) but I left very impressed overall. I'm glad they got rid of the lifeless Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes. I have been a fan of Maggie Gylenhaal since "Secretary" and "Donnie Darko". Christian Bale definitely personifies all that Bruce Wayne/Batman is. What an AMAZING movie. It's too bad it probably won't see many nods at the Golden Globes or Oscars.

10.title: See it on the big screen
10.content:
Went to see the Dark Knight today. Everything I had heard about Heath Ledgers performance, as "The Joker" was true.

As I watched him in his last role, I could utilize Caesar Romero as the 60's Joker and Jack Nicholson's performance as the 80's Joker. Then made the role his own.

Anarchy is Jokers first rule, as many know from the Comic books.

Maggie Gyllenhaal did a fine job replacing Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes Aaron Eckhart came into play Harvey Dent the coin flipping Gorham District Attorney.

Christian Bale, Gary Oldman Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman return in their roles as Bruce Wayne/Batman, James Gordon, Alfred and Mr. Fox respectively Eric Roberts role as mob boss Salvatore Maroni is okay, but he is nothing more then a set up man for Ledgers "Joker" "The Joker" is sort of a mirror of "The Batman." I enjoyed the bat cycle. Bale says there is only one man who can drive that cycle and he wasn't one of them.

There were some tense moments with the citizens of Gorham but in the end good won out over evil.

See this on the big screen it is worth the coin Now the next question is will there be a third Batman movie who would play "The Joker?" Will they bring in the Cat woman character? I am thinking a good choice would be Jessica Biel.

10.title: In Darkest Knight...A Great Movie Appears
10.content:
The Dark Knight is the follow up to Batman Begins, and was a well anticipated film. And guess what? It lived up to its standards.

A lot has improved from Batman Begins and it was a lot better too. The plot revolves around Batman still being the vigilante of Gotham, but is now more excepted. He is now teamed up with Gordon and new district attorney Harvey Dent to crack down on crime and put all the bad guys behind bars. However, there is one maniac on the loose who totally is ruling the heroes - The Joker! Manipulative, cunning, terrifying and a real basket case, the Joker brings Gotham to its knees. Things get worse when the loss of a loved one (not saying who), results in Dent getting scarred quite brutally on one side of his face and he becomes Two-Face, going on a rampage across Gotham killing all those involved with his tragedy.

Christian Bale improves his role as Batman and Bruce Wayne, particularly as Bruce. Batman still needs some work and must ditch that gravely voice. Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman and Gary Oldman return as Alfred, Lucius Fox and Commissioner Gordon and they all are brilliant. I still do not care for Rachel Dawes. My main interest in this film was the portrayal of the villains.

Scarecrow showed up for about five minutes and his role was generally pointless. Sal Maroni was introduced and his portrayal was very enjoyable to watch. Two-Face was played by Aaron Eckart who was completely different to how Tommy Lee Jones handled the character. He was very emotional before and after the transformation into a villain. His scarred face was very realistic, done through CGI.

But the main attraction was the late Heath Ledger's portrayal of the Prince Clown of Crime. Just as Jim Carrey playing the Riddler in Batman Forever ruled that film, Ledger ruled the Dark Knight as Joker. The interesting thing about this Joker, is that he was portrayed as a true homicidal maniac, using knifes and guns to kill instead of using zany weapons like previous versions did. He was terrifically maniacal in his own way and each line he says is a laugh riot. I give an applause to Mr. Ledger for his take on the Joker.

A notable absence is the Batcave and a warehouse is used instead. Aside from the Joker, the introduction of the Batpod (a motorbike) was excellent. The best moment involves a truck driven by the Joker flipping over and than Batman nearly drives the Batpod up a wall.

To parents, the film has a lot of violence, death, dark moments and a lot of scenes that may be unsuitable for children. However, it is an excellent film.

10.title: The Academy better consider this.
10.content: What can I say? This movie is almost the greatest movie ever made, just behind Indiana Jones. The story seems simple but director Christopher Nolan makes it deeper. He takes a comic book movie and makes it into a crime film that holds up with the likes of The Departed, Goodfellas, etc. The film is much faster paced than the first and the action scenes are very well done. As for the acting everyone does an amazing job. Bale does a better job here by making Batman darker. He does a very good job at selling us on how Batman may have to become something he's not just to stop the Joker and as for the Joker Heath does a phenomenal job. He has just made the Joker in my mind the greatest villain of all time and even if he was still alive he defiantly deserves the Oscar. He steals every scene he is in. If a fantasy movie like Lord of the Rings can win a best picture Oscar why can't The Dark Knight? All of the ingredients are here: great story telling, great screen play, great directing, great cinematography, great acting (especially Heath), and great editing. I say the Academy needs to really consider this as a best picture nominee.

10.title: Worth every cent, worth every second.
10.content:
IMAX movie ticket in Toronto - $15 (Daylight robbery IMHO!). Popcorn combo - $8. Experiencing a movie like The Dark Knight - Priceless!!!

Do yourself a favour and watch the movie. In the theatre, preferably. It's one of those movies that a DVD will never be able to do justice to.

I'm ever grateful to Christopher Nolan for every chill down my spine when the Joker spoke, for every rush of adrenaline when Batman jumped a building or raced his Batmobile down a street, for every grimace on my face when Two-Face appeared, and for making a movie so satisfying to all of the human senses.

Batman has always been my favourite superhero. And Nolan has made him so much more cooler and sexier. Who says action movies cater only to guys?! Here's to waiting for the next Batman movie from Nolan. And fast!!!

10.title: Truly enjoyed this flick
10.content:
I am by no means a mass fan of the Batman series but I am a true movie buff who can spot quality when I see it. This movie left me on the edge of my seat yearning for more and more. I would have liked to see some more action with the two face, but all in all we have to understand that he was not a true villain, but a depiction of man at its core.

I believe the storyline was well thought through in bringing all the characters together in a way that left you thinking, "What else could the joker possibly do?" There are many movies being made lately that are not the normal good guy bad guy, but really trying to bring you a true plot with a moral and something to learn from. Batman is a raw movie about just how corrupt the world can be and is in some sense, but it can show you hope and any movie that promotes hope among people will get a hand from me. I can appreciate a movie thats soul purpose is not to simply have you entertained, but reach down and have you thinking at the end. I think that people that are making negative comments about the movie are the people that are missing the story as a whole. Will you be willing to spend your millions on saving people that don't care to be saved? I think we all should learn a little something about this movie and stop being so critical because there were some extra-ordinary unbelievable moments reflected in the scenes that everyone at some point believes they are capable of. It is a fantasy movie so treat it like one and look deeper.

Recommended 10 from me!

10.title: Outstanding!
10.content: There are many words to describe the box office blockbuster, The Dark Knight. Commonly known by IMDb users as TDK. Some may say that the popularity was boosted by the death of Heath Ledger. It may also be that nearly every actor in the production was amazing to watch on screen. At times, I tried to picture the people behind the characters, mostly Heath Ledger behind the Joker. I could never quite do that, for he had such an amazing performance that half way through the movie, it was hard to picture the Joker as another person. Though there wasn't many laughs, there were many sharp intakes of breath. Especially during the parts that you weren't expecting it. For younger audiences, the plot might be hard to understand at some parts. TDK was very believable and the villains were sinister to the bone. Previous to this date, I have looked forward to July 18th, 2008, and the production I saw tonight did not let down any expectations. Bravo. One last thing, R.I.P. Heath Ledger, we will always remember.

10.title: One of the best of 2008. An excellent action film indeed!
10.content:
It took about two hours after this movie was over for me to understand why I felt floored upon finishing this film. I understood why the sold out IMAX audience surrounding me looked as though a sledgehammer had just him them. I understood why my legs were shaking as I left the theater, and why my best friend still felt giddy after the credits were through. Simply put, this was excellent storytelling. Pure, unadulterated, enthralling storytelling. And that's something no excess of shake-cam, ADD editing, visual effects, or that overrated 3-D stuff can ever replace.

To be fair, "The Dark Knight" does have a fair share of fast cuts and CGI. But never, NEVER, do they feel as though they interfere with the storytelling. Christopher Nolan and the cast and crew have accomplished something that few are able to achieve today; they have told a gripping story that hooks its audience from beginning to end, never letting down once during the movie. All of that visual stuff only serves the excellent story being told. This is easily one of the best movies of the year.

The ensemble cast does as impeccable of a job as with "Batman Begins." Heath Ledger gives a grand performance as the Joker, effectively showing shades of Frank Booth from "Blue Velvet" in the process. Brilliant. Christian Bale continues to toe the line well between Bruce Wayne and Batman, and in one moving scene, shows some very heartfelt emotion. Morgan Freeman shines in his expanded role as Lucius Fox, and Michael Caine is as reliable as ever as Alfred. Maggie Gyllenhaal does justice to the role of Rachel Dawes and Aaron Eckhart is superb as the conflicted Harvey Dent.

And what a job the crew does! The cinematography is top notch, the editing is perfect, the visuals and production design don't miss a beat; this is a well put together movie. Add in director Christopher Nolan, whose storytelling is uncompromising, intense, and engaging, and you have one of the best constructed movies of the year. I loved how whenever there was a closeup of the Joker, the camera would be slightly out of focus. Who does out of focus shots anymore? Or the IMAX shots; I got jitters looking down that giant building in Hong Kong. Christopher Nolan has effectively outdone himself directing "The Dark Knight." He should be nominated for an Academy Award.

This is one of the best films of this year and will go down in history as one of the best of all time. Job well done indeed!

10.title: The best crime-drama/action movie EVER made! Hats off to Mr. Nolan.
10.content:
Clever, driven, gripping, thrilling, amazing, awesome, spectacular, extraordinary...

This movie can be described as every positive thing that can be said about a movie. Christopher Nolan has given us yet another thrilling and dramatic movie for all to enjoy. I honestly can't find one negative point of this movie.

Yes, it is a staggering two and a half hour long, but let me tell you, IT IS WORTH IT. After the reboot of the Batman (Batman Begins), I was really looking forward to what happens to Batman next and 'HOW' Mr. Nolan tells the story.

This movie surpassed ALL and EVERY expectation. I didn't even expect it to be that good. When I heard that 'The Joker' was to be played by the young Heath Ledger, I honestly was confused how the blonde, show-boy would do in the role. But I was amazed at how it planned out. Heath Ledger has probably given as one of the most creepy and most loved villains ever to be appeared on screen. That has not been said since Dr. Hannibal appeared in 'Silence of the Lambs'.

The action, the humor, the drama, the special effects, the performance by the individual characters is in one word - perfect. I don't think I've seen a better movie than this one. Heath Ledger has literally stole my heart, it's a great loss to the movie world that he is no longer with us. May he rest in peace.

10/10 (Not many movies can get that!)

10.title: This Batman definitely isn't joking.
10.content:
Gotham city is alive, it's a living, breathing utopia that build on such a massive scale it almost outdoes Heaths chilling interpretation of The Joker. Boy is this one haunting experience, not only is Heath unnaturally humours but at the same time he manages to chill you down to the bone and despite is 12 certificate I do not recommend this to anybody below the age of 15 simply due to the sheer nature of Heaths character. Not only is it the performance of his life but what a stunning final bow if you will to his career. 10 years on when people are asking about him, the Dark Knight will be the film they turn to.

And while he might outshine the rest of this films outstanding cast he doesn't complete the film. Just like last time Bale seems suited to the role, as if he was born to play Bat Man. Maggie Gyllenhal, the superbly sexy and sophisticated Rachel doesn't pull any of that damsel in distress clique and last but by no means least the stunning transformation of Aaron Eckhart from Harvey Dent into the sadistic and saddening two face is Chilling to say the very least. But this is by no means a mere character film. The action seems unbeatably. When Batman soars from building to building so do the audience. When the Joker laughs his high pitch screech the audience cowers as if he were real. Are you scared yet?

Horrific as it may be, The Dark Knight is by no means rough around the edges competently soaring from Amazing set piece to the other and at an impressive 152 minutes it's a mystery on how director Christopher Nolan managed to keep the pacing in such perfect condition. Could it be that in fact we are all so captivated by the macabre brought by Ledger. The strangeness amounting from his recent passing away. Or is it the action keeping us glued to the screen unable to blink for a mere second just in case you miss one of the plenty moments that quite literally take your breath away. The truth is that its all of these, glued together and pumped with steroids. If you only go see one film this year make sure it's this one. I wouldn't be half surprised if this were to win best picture at the academy. Boy I sure hope it does. In truth we all wish for our own personal Batman. If only to add a bit of mystery back into our society. If I were to fault it in any way I would start with its inability to juggle its mass amount of characters, In retrospect you could merely see this as a justified excuse for a repeated viewing. With a tension building, spine tingling score it seems The Dark Knight is near perfect.

VERDICT: As near perfect as were ever going to get. Not only is The Dark Knight the greatest film of 2008 but it's also this decade's finest film. With its haunting performances and it's out of this world action this flies straight to the top of The Words film of the year list and nestles deep within our sole as the most powerful and disturbing superhero movie to date. The posters might say 12A but I wouldn't trust them. but be warned. The joker could stay in your nightmares for years.

10.title: Everything you've heard is true...this is a STUNNING film
10.content:
I've been visiting this site for over 10 years and this is the first movie I've ever felt compelled to post a comment about. Other folks have done a fine job describing why it's so good...just get out and see it immediately.

High points?

1. Heath Ledger is as good as you've heard and then some. I'm cynical by nature and was sure that everyone was hyping him just because of his personal tragedy. Not true - this is probably the best portrayal of a villain in the history of film. Talk about losing yourself in a part! It does NOT get any better than this. It brings a tear to my eye just thinking about the fact that this would have made him an A-list actor, no doubt. Sigh.

2. NO KATIE HOLMES! Sorry, but she can't act worth a damn and she was the only facet of the first movie which made me cringe.

3. The action scenes! You will be exhausted at the end of this film, I guarantee it. This is a non-stop thrill ride, to say the least.

4. Gary Oldman is awesome this time around - his performance in the first movie was a bit timid but this time he hits it out of the park.

5. Christian Bale finally has his Batman voice down pat - forget anyone else who ever wore the suit, he IS Batman. This point is NOT open to debate.

Low points?

1. It's only two and a half hours long. I usually start looking at my watch about halfway through a movie - but not this time.

I can not stress this enough - GO SEE THIS MOVIE!

10.title: Perfect! Nothing more, nothing less...
10.content:
Three years ago a friend of mine offered to watch Batman Begins at theater and I said OK but I didn't expect anything but overblown effects and a boring childish scenario. I'm not a fan of Batman and I usually don't like superhero movies or comic book adaptations. But it was something different than I expected. It was not built upon the simple ideas of other superhero movies and the way the movie told us the story of the protagonist was quite realistic. So it changed my prejudiced opinion on Batman.

Depending on the success of the first movie I was eager to see The Dark Knight. Especially after seeing the photos of Heath Ledger as Joker.

This time the story is darker and it exceeds the well-known Hollywood clichés. Characters are genuinely crafted and the cast is superb. Christian Bale is the best Batman ever and Heath Ledger as Joker is shocking. Script is the best I've ever seen in a this kind of movie. It shows the fight of good and evil in a quite realistic way and as it is in real life you see there's a thin line between the two. Christopher Nolan's point of view shows that things are not that easy and the good characters are not invincible. And not always there happy endings. The movie makes you feel Gotham is a city possessed by crime and it is as dark as Batman himself.

Also I was really satisfied by the ending of the movie but most of my friends said it could be better. But my opinion is the ending was great.

The last thing I couldn't control myself to tell is the tricks of Joker. They made me smile sadistically while watching them. He's completely chaotic and a real psychopath.

Go and see the movie whether you like or don't like Batman. At least you'll surely love and admire Heath's performance as Joker...

10.title: Perfect. Could not have been done any other way. Ledger is legendary.
10.content:
I was blown away by this movie. That is a first for me, of course I fell into all the hype, so I bought midnight tickets. This movie has surpassed all of the hype, Nolan directed a perfect 10. Of course Id like to know more about how Rachael and Harvey ended up where they did, but that's minor. This movie had me saying "WHAT!" "HOLY cow" NO MOVIE EVER HAS. Eckhart played a phenomenal role.. he was awesome. Every character in the movie could not have been replaced. It was amazing.. so awesome.. the F/X sound and al was just to perfection.

Perfect perfect, going to see it again in IMAX.

Ledger plays the greatest villain in any movie ever.

R.I.P Heath

10.title: Dangerous
10.content: Great movie. Safer to watch it at home and not at the cinema

10.title: "Why so serious?" - Ledger Shines, Bale outdoes himself yet again.
10.content:
I don't like to say this often: "I could not find a single flaw in this masterpiece of a movie". This is not only, by far, the best Batman movie ever created, but also the best superhero movie ever created to date! Christian Bale as Batman has returned to the big screen and really amazed us with a Batman that is both believable and absolutely amazing. His pain and sorrow are clearly evident as he tries to cope with his role as "The Dark Knight" and he just plain kicks bad guys asses throughout the entire flick! Heath Ledger will forever be known as the Joker for me. He has far outstripped veteran actor Jack Nickolson as a far far better joker. I will give no spoilers, but the line "Why So Serious?" will be with me forever. Ledger deserves a posthumous Oscar for his performance.

If you are a die hard Batman fan or a Batman newbie, there is something for everyone in this movie. None will be disappointed with the film. The atmosphere is absolutely amazing. It is both dark and brooding. It is the perfect locale for such a film, Chicago that is.

I just can't get over this movie. I think I am going to see it again in the theater later this week when the rest of my family goes, it is that great. Well worth the rising price of movie tickets!

10.title: The Dark Knight Oscar Awards
10.content: I'm not into the Batman Movies, even though I used to love the cartoon version when I was a kid - yes I'm that old. I've watched and half-watched a the previous Batman sequels and find them far too dark and repetitive. The Dark Knight can stand on it's own. It has a great story line full of action, intrigue, and plenty of thrilling interludes. I admit I watched this primarily because I was interested in seeing Heath Ledgers' last performance and the hype surrounding it, even though I've always thought he was a good actor. But in this he is superb, portraying The Joker as the insidiously evil monster that he is. He is totally psychotic. Ledger gave me the creeps. (Sorry Jack, you have nothing on him!) The other actors perform beautifully as well. Christian Bale as the cool, calm, crime fighter. Aaron Eckhart shows us our own seesaw of inner struggle with good versus evil in our own lives and how quickly a person can turn. Michael Caine, the effervescent gentleman playing the understated, wise adviser and Morgan Freeman, as a true humanitarian and closest door Robin. (As I see it). Maggie Gyllenhaal's piece de resistance has to be when The Joker drags her to face him at the function held for Harry Dent. The disgust on her face is classic. This movie would be nothing with Heath Ledger alone. Yet it would be nothing without him. He is undoubtedly the leading star. Without his amazing performance, the others would have nothing to do except read their lines. The Joker is waiting at every corner, behind every door and you never know where he's going to strike next. And He Is Crazy. The movie world has lost a great actor in Heath Ledger. It's a pity we didn't know how much we'd lost until it was too late.

10.title: The Dark Knight delivers
10.content:
well you all knew this was coming so here goes my review of The Dark Knight.

this movie is phenomenal!! you all probably figured that is what i would say but let me explain my reasoning besides the fact that its Batman. well to start it off, Batman Begins is one of my favorite movies and The Dark Knight expands on everything that was great about the first one. the acting is one of the main draws here, with Christopher Nolan expertly showcasing the scenes of dialogue between characters. Nolan manages to highlight just plain old talking into something amazing. the entire cast is superb (with Maggie Gyllenhall replacing the atrocious Katie Holmes) but the best addition is, of course, Heath Ledger. now during the course of this epic 2 and a half hour masterpiece Ledger's Joker is one of the greatest performances you will ever lay your eyes on. the things he does with this character are just mind-boggling. it blows Jack Nicholson's portrayal out of the water. he is the absolute best part of this movie. but it is just heart breaking to know once the lights come up in the theater that this is the last time you will ever see a new complete performance from the great Heath Ledger. his performance most certainly deserves a posthumous Oscar nomination for best supporting actor.
