That's what a movie's supposed to do: entertain you but make it stay with you even after you leave the theatre and on your way home.

11/10 It's that good. RIP Heath Ledger.

10.title: The best film ever made.
10.content: This is the best film ever made easy, Christian bale is the best man alive and heath hedger is also amazing. Cried at the end cos of how emotional it is and batman is just the man. Thanks

10.title: a great movie
10.content: First of all this is probably the best ever superhero movie i have ever seen in my life. The plot was out of this world, so many twists you didn't know what was going to happen next and that kept me gripped to my seat for the entire film. All the actors did a superb job (espically Heath Ledger God Bless his soul) he was one of the best on screen villains i have ever seen. But this is because he was studying very hard about being a very disturbed criminal. So he couldn't sleep at night and took anxiety pills. Also the camera work was incredible and the only continuity error was when he was on the bike and riding through the traffic and the cars where still but had their lights on. Finally i thank Christopher Nolan for producing, writing and directing this masterpiece of a film that will rank in some of the best movies of all time.

10.title: The Dark Knight experience
10.content:
The Dark Knight is no ordinary summer Hollywood flick,it is unconventional,convoluted and most precisely BRILLIANTAfter weeks & weeks of surmounting hype with the media throwing in all possible tidbits about the movie,the movie still managed to live up to the hype.This effort by a dedicated set of actors and technicians will certainly be remembered for a long long time..

I am not going to spill the beans by giving the whole movie plot,but i sure can review it The most probable question in your mind would be 'Who was the show-stealer??' .The answer to this question is a no-brainer now(Thanks to all those critics who watched this movie a week ago),it is Heath Ledger.His final performance surely does leave an impactHeath literally lived the role of The Joker and everything about him was great,be it the dialogues or the body languageOn a scale of 10,i give him 11,no villain in the recent past has been as menacing as the jokerIt is sad that he died earlier this year.He was a great talent and he would have given us more memorable roles.Big round of applause for him and i surely hope he is nominated for the Oscars next year..RIP!!

Outwardly,just like Batman Begins,the whole city of Gotham is made to tremble and joker brings the whole city to a standstill with multiple homicides,explosions and threats.The trio comprising of Batman,Lt. James Gordon and the new district attorney Harvey Dent join hands in wiping out the skum of Gotham City and they are quite successful until the city's thug mob give in to Joker's terms and what follows is sheer chaos.Joker goes on a killing spree demanding the batman to reveal his true identity and he almost succeeds!!The whole story involves a lot of sacrifices to counter Joker's moves and as an audience,we are jolted by one twist after the other.The story surpasses the mundane superhero storyline and is just inches away from realitySee it,to believe it!!

From the acting department,everybody give their best.My favorite Christian Bale delivers yet again as Batman and also as Bruce Wayne although he has very less screen time as Bruce Wayne.Bale is very much self assured but looks a tad anemic.He reprises his role just as a day at the office.Gary Oldman is given more scope this time around and he looks resolute as Lt. James Gordon.Aaron Eckhart is a new member to the cast and this is the first time i have seen him in a movie.He does well as the dedicated DA and also as the vengeful Two-Face.Maggie Gyllenhall,Micheal Caine and Morgan Freeman go about their roles with finesse and no one looks wasted at the end.The director Nolan had a clear picture of what we wanted and his ensemble deliver just the sameBravo!!

Coming to the technical department,the background music was just pulsating and concise.Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard rework on their Batman Begins theme and bring about an haunting experience which lasts the movie's length.This movie deserves it.Cinematography by Wally Pfister is top notch and is award worthy.I was dazed with the camera movements .Editing was jarring sometimes but very much acceptable.But do save your praise-points for Christopher Nolan,Jonathan Nolan and David S.Goyer.Christopher Nolan is the man who made Memento and The Prestige and he now according to me,holds the distinction of being called the most sophisticated director in Hollywood.Nolan's direction is very much in keeping the movie pacy and also elaborate at the same time.Screenplay is tight as usual.His brother Jonathan teams up with Goyer for penning the story and they sure have done their homework with the comic books .Supposedly,they have read a heck lot in bringing together a serious crime epic of a movie.Oscar worthy stuff!!

And now,my favorite moments from the film

1.) The start of the movie.a urban bank robbery which acts as a superlative intro for the Joker.

2.) The scene where Batman jumps from the top ledge of a skyscraper to gate-crash into some thugs

3.) The pre-interval chicken chase scene was just AWESOME with old fashioned stunts and gripping music.This is as good as the climax chase in Terminator 2!!

4.) All of Joker's scenes..and also his preening HEHEHE

In a nutshell,the movie was just great and it can be seen more than twice.By the end,we were left gasping for more,everybody was unwilling to move from their seats,such was the impact.It was 152 minutes of a thrill ride.Batman and Joker brawl their way into a slobberknocker and their escapades make me think by picturising the batman as a silent dark do-gooder who detests the limelight and who does everything to be within his code of ethics and the joker who is the Satan or the anti-Christ with absolute chaos as his solve motive,a person who is an crime artist with a love for the theatrics.Together,they are yin-yang but they are fun to watch So what are you waiting for,get a load of The Dark knight before your friends deliver the spoilers.

10.title: Best comic book movie
10.content: The dark knight is a great thoughtful potent movie.this was the first superhero movie that i watched seriously and believe me it really was incredible...i thought that superhero movie are only for kids...but Mr Nolan's batman movies create a lot of energetic content for adults...it really blew me...it has outdone batman begins in all aspects...i thought batman begins was best batman movie after batman returns but dark knight exceeded all my expectations and i must say it is one of the finest crime thrillers coming out from Hollywood,also what separates a good movie from a great movie is Performance...the joker has steal the acting crown of this movie,it was the best joker i have ever seen in batman movies its his best performance till date.the background score of this movie was also great. I have already watched it 30 times and i still want to see it again.

10.title: action thriller
10.content:
The Dark Knight (2008)

Christopher Nolan again blows our minds away with stunning effects, great writing, and a phenomenal cast of the most talented actors and actresses in the movie business, when he brings back Christian Bale, as Bruce Wayne, his alter-ego Batman in The Dark Knight (2008) as well as Michael Caine, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman. Some new faces are, Heath Ledger and Aaron Eckhart. There really is no better way to describe The Dark Knight (2008) than as the "Holy Grail" of all movies. The sequel to Batman Begins (2005), The Dark Knight has broken records of all sorts, such as becoming the second movie of all time to break 500 million in the Box Office, and also having the biggest weekend's total, out of any other movie made. The Dark knight brings back Christian Bale as Gotham City's billionaire man, the owner of Wayne Enterprises, Bruce Wayne.

Faced with all new problems and a new villain in the mix of thugs Batman must now deal with The Joker (Ledger). Batman (Bale), Lt. Gordon (Oldman) and new District Attorney Harvey Dent (Ekhart), set out to take out the remaining crime bosses and their pawns completely from Gotham City. While trying to put the rest of them behind bars, a new criminal mastermind sets foot in Gotham and sets out to take over. The Joker gets on a personal level with Batman, forcing him to think about what really is most important in his life.

Heath Ledger took the role of the Joker, and showed why he was the right choice for the part. This being Heath Ledger's last full movie with a main role, he definitely did not disappoint. As Batman tries to build his symbol as a hero and protector of Gotham City goons are out to destroy it and take back the city they once had. Trying to decide whether or not, being Batman is what he really wants, Bruce Wayne is also faced with the dilemma of keeping his relationship with Rachel Dawes close to him. Aaron Eckhart, plays Harvey Dent Gotham's District Attorney is also trying to fight crime and build a symbol for him while trying to avoid being assassinated and keeping a relationship with Rachel Dawes. Christopher Nolan displays Batman's power and importance by choosing to shoot a broad range of close up and low shots. Nolan also does this with Ledger's character the Joke. The Dark Knight is a movie of great darkness and that is why most of the movie's scenes are shot in dark, very dim lighted ways to make the movie have that eerie, scary feeling. Nolan shows in great detail the massive chaos and special effects, with ingenious camera shots and lighting. This movie is great for teens and adults with its riveting screenplay, brief romance and intriguing plot. Being rated PG-13, some parts and images could be too intense for some young children.

Any Batman lover or comic book enthusiast will greatly appreciate all the Christopher Nolan put into this movie. Rating this movie with five stars, it should be seen by everyone. Nolan is able to make it seem as if the viewer is right there going along with every punch, kick, and explosion that The Dark Knight has to offer.

10.title: You Changed Things Forever!
10.content:
Christopher Nolan has a vision. And whether you agree with it or not, he undeniably completes it in "The Dark Knight"--a vicious, engrossing, overwhelming, intelligent event- film that re-defines 'comic-book-flicks'. In Nolan's grim, dark-depiction of Gotham-City (the crime-ridden hell protected by legendary superhero Batman), the director strives to make everything real (something he began in the well-received "Batman Begins"). He makes it plausible, possible. And yet there's more to it: just as 'Begins' was a dissection of myth, the nature of symbols and heroes, 'Knight' is the escalation of that notion. It's a biblical- confrontation of 'good-and-evil', yet as 'good-and-evil' really exist: a conflict of ideals, something that can't be purely-defined but that is relative to a viewpoint. In Nolan's world, the line of villainy and heroism isn't crossed... it's non-existent. The bad-guys don't see themselves as bad-guys, and as such something so unnervingly-real comes across it might fly past some people's minds (no insult to anybody, it's just common that people don't look deep into 'popcorn-flicks'): the battle is a complete ambiguity.

The film runs at nearly 2.5-hours, yet never ceases to lose interest or momentum. It doesn't waste a scene or moment; every event is utilized and necessary. 'The Dark Knight' tells a story worth telling and it takes the proper amount of time to tell it. Action-sequences are frantic, old-school, eye-grabbing stunts (vastly superior to 'Begins') and in their chaotic intensity we see that they serve purpose to the story, yet more interesting are not played for pure entertainment-value: we are meant to watch, petrified, simply hoping that the outcome will go the hero's way. Attention is never lost because we are immersed in a breathtaking, almost completely-unpredictable story (it packs many a shock), that makes us think and more importantly gains our emotional-investment. We come to care for the characters, because they are believable, developed, and personified fully.

Everyone has great-chemistry together. Maggie Gyllenhal is a more mature Rachel Dawes than Katie Holmes. Morgan Freeman provides his authoritative presence to the role of bad- gadget-inventor/Wayne-Enterprise CEO Lucius Fox, and under anyone else's portrayal, the part would be less-memorable. Gary Oldman underplays his world-wearied lawman with such honest-nobility, you never feel for a second any of its forced-acting. The irreplaceable Michael Caine makes a gentle, reassuring, father-like presence as Alfred, and the movie would surely fail without his strong-presence and interjected-moments of light-humor.

And while everyone (rightfully) pours the praise unto Bale and Ledger, I think most are glancing-over Knight's breakout-performance. As Harvey Dent, Aaron Eckhart does more than hold himself in the company of such a renowned-cast. He makes his presence known, whether he's playing on the easy-going charisma of Gotham's 'White-Knight' or the broken and damaged, twisted-soul of Two-Face. He achieves a full-impact with the tragedy that comes unto his character, and so closely connects with Dent, that he makes his pain tangible for us: we sympathize even as we become terrified. He captures both facets of each personality flawlessly.

Now, some people cite that 'Knight' has a potential fatal-flaw in the supposedly wooden- acting of Christian Bale. Admittedly, his development is not as grand as in 'Begins' (yet that film gave us such a good psychoanalysis of Wayne, we hardly need more), yet what Bale pulls off is admirable. Wayne is not an eccentric personality. He is a disillusioned man who can hardly find any joy in having no family, giving up his love-interest and spending his life fighting a battle that may never end. He's dark and conflicted, and Bale plays up on that brooding-mood by making Wayne look as though a thousand dark-things were on his mind. He's not wooden...he's a humorless, quiet individual. Even when Wayne is acting as a frivolous playboy for the public, every now and then Bale offers us a powerful glance that reminds us its all a façade; that deep down, something more disturbed irks him. Occasionally he offers a broken-smile when exchanging banter with Alfred, letting us know that beyond the dour depression of the Caped-Crusader lies a damaged human-being. It is only in the guise of a growling masked-man, that he can unleash his true, ferocious personality.

Finally, who could forget Heath Ledger. Now, when he was first-announced for the part, I was (along with many other people) asking myself: "Why?". Mr. Ledger had proved with 'Brokeback Mountain' he could deliver a potent performance. But he hadn't before. It is only, after seeing this film, that I know the answer to 'why?': I see the significance of his loss.

When Heath appears in this movie, he is completely unrecognizable. His voice is distinctly-altered; a near-whiny, pedophile-like tone that sends shivers down the spine. His face is completely splattered with makeup that renders him both freakishly-nightmarish and strangely-funny. And when you see him, you don't think it's him. In this, his final performance, Ledger proved he was a chameleon. His two iconic performances in this, and 'Brokeback', could not be more different. I am convinced he could have been anything in his career. He commits so intensely to character that the line of actor/portrayal dies. His every tick and gesture only further-enhances his character. Heath never hams the role up or goes for something cheap: he delivers a fully-immersed display of psychotic madness...or do we just label him that to feel safer? The movie writes the character brilliantly; blending terrifying truth into his every social-accusation, and making us question why we laugh at his sick-jokes.

'The Dark Knight' has had an incredible-amount of hype running for it, from the get-go, mounting ever-higher, until Heath Ledger's too-soon death. And the finished-product does more than exceed all of the near-impossible expectations placed on it. It becomes something much richer than a super-hero-franchise-saga. Christopher Nolan has opened a new door in cinema: allowing action-flicks to become more serious, capable of intelligence. He has transformed this into a piece of artwork, full of beauty, terror, moral-conundrums. This movie has changed things...forever.

10.title: Proper Execution
10.content: What makes any movie get to the Top 1 spot in the All time greatest list? Is it because of a super hero? Is it because of psycho maniac? or Is it because of good script/direction/execution etc? I guess not to the fullest... All these things comes with a proper PLAN...and yes plan is something which makes things routine and more importantly push things towards getting ordinary. The movie however is not about any super hero or a super villain, nor is interested in showcasing some heroics. Its more about showcasing what humans do and how humans do...although its more about taking those things to an extreme but there is nothing "SUPER" in this movie and thats what brings it to the top spot. It deserves to be there where it is.

10.title: One of the Absolute Greatest Films i've EVER seen!
10.content:
AT 12:00 am on July 18th in my local movie theater, I saw what may possibly be(at least in my opinion) to be one of the greatest movies ever made, "The Dark Knight". I know, I know i'm just another person drooling over a super hero on the big screen and you think in a few weeks or months i'll forget all about this film, but no thats not it at all.

What I experienced in those two and a half hours, sitting in my seat, just gazing at the big screen, was probably the best movie experience i've ever had(next to probably my first time seeing 'The Godfather'). When I tell you that this isn't your ordinary "superhero movie", this isn't your quintessential big budget, high grossing, star studded action/adventure movie, I mean it. This is art, this is poetry, this is cinema. This is how movies should be made, this is how movies used to be made(aside from the special effects and CGI of course).

Let me cut as much to the chase as I can, Heath Ledger gives what I consider, one of the better supporting performances in the last twenty years. ACtually, scratch that, OF ALL TIME! Ledger was absolutely captivating as the Joker and(no offense to Jack Nicholson, he's one of my favorite actors) kicks the crap out of Nicholson's performance twenty years earlier. Ledger without a doubt, not out of sympathy at all but out of pure talent, deserves the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.

Another awesome performance which will probably go unnoticed is Gary Oldman's for playing LT. Gordon. Oldman is a very good and very underrated actor(also one of my favorites). Christian Bale is amazing once again as Batman.Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, and Maggie Gylenhal all give excellent supporting performance as well.

While this film may or may not entice you to go see it, while most people might consider it "just another superhero movie", take it from someone who's seen thousands of films, old and new, this is one of the greatest movies i've ever seen.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. AN ABSOLUTE MUST SEE! 11/10

10.title: Believe the hype!!!!!!!!!!!!
10.content:
I don't even know where to begin with this movie. I have never been more excited to see a movie more than Iwas excited to see The Dark Knight. As soon as I saw Memento, I knew that Christopher Nolan was what all directors in Hollywood should aspire to. Batman Begins was incredible and who could forget the intricacies of The Prestige. Christopher Nolan, Peter Jackson, Guillermo del Toro and Ridley Scott are the class of Hollywood right now. Now for The Dark Knight

I was absolutely ecstatic when I heard Heath Ledger was going to portray The Joker. Heath's death was tragic in every way possible. We lost a true talent who would have captured the big screen for many many years to come. Early marketing was all hype for Ledger's Joker performance and rightly so. In all of the comic book world there is no more important hero/villain relationship than Batman/Joker. It's better than Superman/Lex Luthor, better than X-Men/Magneto, better than Fantastic 4/Dr. Doom, better than Spider-Man/Venom. You DO NOT have Batman without the Joker. With all the hype leading up to Ledger's Joker the question is raised: is it worth the hype? The answer, in a word is ABSOLUTELY. Jack Nicholson has nothing on Heath Ledger. The Joker steals the screen in every scene he is in. He also has the greatest entrance of any character possibly ever with his "disappearing pencil trick." It sets the tone for his character as dark, twisted, demented, sadistic and strangely funny. It is a OMG scene but you will have a very hard time not laughing. Ledger steals the movie, but in a very good way. He is over-the-top but you never ask him to apologize for it, in fact, you'll be thanking him for it. The Joker sums it up in one line when he says to Batman "you and I could do this forever." If the Acadamy does not recognize Heath Ledger posthumously for his role in The Dark Knight, then I vow to never watch the Oscars ever again.

Now for Christian Bale. After watching the '89 and 90's Batmans I always thought that if you could take Michael Keaton's Bruce Wayne character and mix it with Val Kilmer's Batman character that you'd have the perfect Batman/Bruce Wayne. Ladies and gentleman, I give you Christian Bale. He is the fun loving and smart Bruce Wayne that Micheal Keaton gave us and the brooding and unrelenting Batman that Val Kilmer gave us. Batman has always been my favorite hero because he has no superhuman powers. He is a vigilante but never crosses the dark line. However, at the same time he is angry with how his beloved Gotham City has been taken over by crime. I have always liked Christian Bale. In The Dark Knight we see Batman struggling with how the morals and ethics of being a hero, but not crossing the moral line and becoming a criminal himself. Much like in Batman Forever we see Bruce Wayne considering hanging up the mask forever. Batman goes from being the Caped Crusader to the title character of The Dark Knight. Bale pulls this role off flawlessly and you really start to feel for his struggle with donning the mask and cape.

Michael Caine is always brilliant, and he gives the role of Alfred Pennyworth his due course and adds in some humility, direction and even a little humor. I am glad Nolan gave him this role.

Aaron Eckhart as Harvey Dent is awesome. This was another casting that I was very excited for. Dent's character is perfect. If Batman is the Dark Knight, then Dent is Gotham's White Knight so to speak. Dent ruthlessly hunts down, in the legal realm, Gotham's criminals in an effort to clean the streets of crime and corruption. However, as we all know, Harvey Dent must eventually become Two-Face and you see his struggle with morality. Dent himself has a dark side that he must confront on several occasions. SPOILER HERE!!!!!!!!!!!!! Dent does become Two-Face about 3/4ths of the way through the movie. It is not the cartoon-like Two-Face that Tommy Lee Jones gives us. Like the rest of the movie, it is dark and evil and when you see his face you might look away at first. It's not for the feint of heart. END SPOILER!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Maggie Gyllenhaal is perfectly re-cast as Rachel Dawes. She seems to connect better with Bale than Holmes did. However, Nolan does not give her character much to do in the movie. She does have a cool encounter with The Joker, but overall her character is not extremely important to the movie as a whole.

Gary Oldman is another character that deserves an award for his role in The Dark Knight. His portrayal of Jim Gordon is awesome. For moments in the movie you actually forget that he's acting. He must find his own place in a corrupt police force that struggles with deciding to capture or honor Batman. Nolan hit the nail on the head again with this casting choice.

Overall, the story is a little convoluted, but it doesn't matter because once the Joker hits the scene, that's all you care about. The fights between Batman and Joker are epic. This is the blueprint of how all comic book/superhero movies must be made. Iron Man was cool, but I left this movie thinking to myself, "who's Iron Man?" This movie lives up to every hype possible and is required viewing for everyone and anyone who likes movies at all. This is one of the few movies I've seen that I cannot point out any flaws in the film-making.

A resounding 10/10

Heath Ledger 1979-2008 RIP

10.title: This movie was a good movie.
10.content:
I didn't like it as much as I liked it though. But the first ten minutes or so was rly good. Batman is introduced as he says with a confident and badass "I'm Batman" and then he jumps and glides straight towards the camera. He almost seems to fly out of the screen. It was amazing. The only way it could have been better is if he flew out of the screen and gave me a handjob, which was OK that he didn't but it would have saved me the effort. Batman then meets up with Commissioner Gordon on the top of the police station, because Gordon used the bat-signal again because he can't afford a phone. Batman gets there and is all like "I'm Batman". Gordon replies with an entirely expected "I know. Lol. Will you please sleep with my wife?" Batman agrees and then he goes to beat up the bad guys. The score during all of this is incredible. I threw away almost all of my CDs and stuff I stole off the internet and now I only listen to the soundtrack. Later on, because Batman is so badass, awesome, and badass, he says randomly at one point "Fuck." just to push the PG-13 rating as far as possible. Lol. He is so cool.

Great camera work, a perfect score, great acting, near-perfect editing, but then it all seemed to go downhill from there. It seems like 99.99% of the budget was used on that first ten minutes. After that, the entire atmosphere seems so cheap and rushed. Part of the rest of the film was in black and white and other parts there was no sound. The camera work was even more ridiculous. During a scene in Bruce's room when he's looking in the mirror, the camera and crew are all entirely visible in the reflection. If you look closely you can even see Chris Nolan smacking around his assistant. The score goes from being awesomely good classical music to being a bunch of random twee indie pop songs from the late 90s. At a certain point, the screen goes blank for seven minutes and is followed by a scrolling message that describes what supposedly happened while the screen was blank. At another point, Batman becomes a piece of paper with a wire attached to it that says "Batman" on it, and it flies around a cardboard cutout Gotham miniature model. I was also a bit disappointed by The Joker's role. He was in the background for a few minutes and just looked like a regular clown. It was hella creepy though. Clowns shouldn't just be "around". But what the hell was with the entire hour of rescuing orphans that seemed to pop out of nowhere? Where are their god damn parents? Talk about your cliché filler.

Despite all of these ridiculous flaws, it still had Batman in it, which makes any movie a 10/10 automatically.

10.title: Great if you don't mind messages, Hype=10, Movie=7.5-8
10.content: Yes, it is everything everyone is saying about the movie almost. . . Great directions first off. Great acting secondly, especially Ledger, and lastly a great score. With Nolan and this cast these things were expected. So here are the the drawbacks. Too long. Why not end with the birth of Two-face and let that carry over to a possible sequel? That would have saved us at least 30 minutes. All the messages in the movie!!!!!! This is the biggest flaw. I come for enjoyment, not to be taught a lesson. So it was good, but after all the lessons and the length I had to give it an 8 (really a 7.5). But let me go back to the direction, the biggest talent here is Nolan (and the cinematographer). The pace of the action, and the dialogue is masterful. The art direction is masterful. And that bike! That was too cool. If you were half asleep before the emergence of the bike, you were wide awake from that point onward. The stunts and the bike alone were enough.

10.title: Better than the first
10.content: This movie was outstanding in every way possible, of course my words cant describe how good it was, see for your self. Acting was very good, Heath Ledgher R.I.P, was outstanding, it was Oscar worthy, Christian bale was good as well. It was misleading at times, like where Gordon was shot, and how he came back. The score for the movie was OK, could of been better. Visual effects were awesome, i was surprised about two-face, i heard their were thinking baout making another movie with Jamie Foxx as two-face, which probably wont happen. OUtstanding movie, i loved it, its better than the first one. Im not surprised if this movie wins a few Oscars. 10 out of 10, great movie, SEE IT.

10.title: A masterpiece and the best movie of 2008 hand's down!
10.content:
What can I say about The Dark Knight that hasn't already been said? It's already rated as the 3rd best film of all time on IMDb. Believe me, it deserves that spot in the top 10, easily.

But let me just warn you, this is not a movie meant to be pure "fun". It is not a pure adrenaline ride, with no purpose but to give you explosions and punches. This is meant to be taken seriously, in every single aspect. Where as some people may want movies only to be fun, and those movies are good sometimes, this movie does not even try that. This movie is a balance of drama, sheer creepiness, and action. The action is pretty damn good, very exciting (especially the chase sequences), but it's not the focal point. It's not gonna be the type of movie you should watch if you just want action. I would say this is an epic crime drama more than anything, with a theme of good vs evil. Anyone who knows some of Cristopher Nolan's work knows his films have thought put behind them.

Speaking of which, Nolan is a great director, one of the best in recent years I now believe. During action sequences the camera work is frenetic, but you can see what you need to. Every punch and kick has a sense of power behind it. On the other hand during the flights of Batman the city seems large and expansive, and even Batman seems minor in comparison. In my opinion Nolan knows how to make a good movie.

Nolan's brother Jonathan has co-written a great screenplay with his brother, and I think I must say something. Half of the brilliance of the Joker and Batman/Wayne is definitely due to the writing. Their respective actors just happen to be almost perfect, but you must give points to Jonathan Nolan. Never once does a line seem truly unnatural. Even the one liners have a natural wit, as if someone really could say something of that sort on the spot.

As far as acting goes, everyone is pitch perfect. Not one person really seems fake, save for a few civilians who say lines a little forced once in a while. Still, all characters with names in the movie are played very well, which should tell others who make movies that casting is very important, even for minor characters. From Caine as Alfred, Freeman as Lucius Fox, Oldman as Lt. Gordon, Gyllenhall as Rachel Dawes (much better than Holmes), everybody does well.

Bale is very good as Batman- dark and gruff voiced- but more importantly, he is able to switch characters to be Bruce Wayne, the playboy show off type at ease. He will hopefully get recognition with even more people now because he is a great actor. Eckhart is pretty good as Dent as well, and we see a gradual change in his character emotionally and on his thoughts of heroism.

And Ledger, what can I say? If Joker appears in the next movie, I doubt anyone can play him as well. Every action, lip smack, word, everything that he does or says is the definitive Joker. Before this movie I always wondered what makes him Batman's most popular enemy. Now I understand: Joker is downright evil and psychotic and he seems to be a mastermind of planning, thinking about everything before it happens. He has the exact opposite ideals (trying to bring down Gotham to the criminals) of Batman, who wants to bring peace. Once again, credit must be given to both Ledger and Jonathan Nolan's writing.

The music (Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard) is brilliant at setting the mood for everything and often makes scenes super tense. There are some moments in the movie where there's just a dull vibrating bell thing sound (the scene where Joker sticks his head out the car window that is in the trailer), and it was actually mesmerizing. The sounds of guns and punches feel very solid and heavy, just like they should.

Joker once tells Batman he doesn't want to kill him, saying "you complete me". Now others in the theater started laughing, thinking that he meant it as a joke (which was one meaning possibly). But it is more than that- Batman completes the Joker, because no matter how much good there is in Gotham, there must be someone like the Joker to counter that with evil. In a way Gotham represents the whole world's struggle between evil and good. And in the end, Batman and Joker are simply two faces of a coin- They have different faces and ideals on the outside, but in many ways, they are made of the same stuff inside, and are necessary to each other.

10.title: an epic movie leaves you speechless it is that brilliant best film of the decade by far
10.content: this film is simply the greatest superhero film ever in my mind it will never be beaten it was just off the charts leaves you so amazed i thought batman returns was dark but this is far darker Christoper Nolan has taken batman to a new level he's taken it way further than Burton or Schumacher ever did he's gone into the soul of batman and i like it Christan bale has done it again just brilliant as batman Aaron eckhart just superb a million times better than tommy lee Jones as two face appearance bloody awesome but the man of the hour was heath ledger as the joker in my view the greatest villain of all time so cold, so dark so bloody serious went so deep into the joker showed us why he is a total psychopath jack Nicholson didn't even scratch the service with his version of the joker this film is the best of the decade you want to find an icon of this decade than look no further than heath ledger rest in peace you put a smile on my face for sure again this film is totally epic go and see it now you hear me NOW!!!!

10.title: A perfect score for the perfect cast!
10.content:
Little really can need to be said about this movie that has not been already said before.

Bale as Batman is exceptional as we all knew he was going to be (again!). He not only plays the side of Batman quite darkly and mysterious but also give Bruce Wayne that slightly arrogant charm which is originally the way Bruce was said to be. Heath Ledger pretty much did as everyone said he would and stole the show in his deranged, psychotic and immensely breathtaking performance as the joker. Slight touches such as the dryness of his mouth when talking and also the constant licking of the lips along with slight twitches of the head just made you want to see more and more of him through out the film. Aaron Eckhart and Maggie Gylenhall are excellent together and Im looking forward to seeing more from Eckhart, he puts in a solid performance as Harvey Dent and really shows his acting capabilities in the last half hour of the movie! All in all This is a must see for everyone, not just Batman fans and I can certainly promise you will not be disappointed, well I'm off to see it again for the 3rd time in 2 days. :P

10.title: The Dark Knight one of the true masterpiece of all time
10.content: Theirs no doubt that the dark knight doesn't deserve an important place with other masterpieces.This is the only film in years to have such an interesting match of action,thriller,good literature,superb direction and of course it has portrayed the common people as heroes. This movie on my perspective is truly inspirational and the other critics should not just see it as a comic character portrayal, rather they should respect this icon and learn how a normal person through strong determination stand up for good.I have watched it hundreds of times and each time i feel rejuvenated to see the interesting contrast of good & the evil which has been brilliantly showcased by bale and late heath ledger. I wish the whole group of Christopher Nolan all the best and hope his direction will surprise everyone of us creating the sequel and break all box office records one again.I do hope the dark knight character will stand tall and deliver what his audiences expect of him.

10.title: Not as great as Batman Begins, but still great....
10.content:
This review has been swirling in my mind for ages, I watched it at the Cinemas and didn't know quite what to make of it...I was a big comic book fan, a great lover of Batman Begins, so when the trailer arrived I was in awe of Heath Ledger as the Joker and impressed by Christian's development of the Batman.....

Gotham City is in turmoil as the events of Batman Begins have thrown everything into chaos, people are dressing up as Batman and fighting crime with guns, while some of Arkham's inmates are still on the loose, and the leading criminals in the City are terrified of the thing that lurks in the shadows. Until a man arrives who doesn't seem to be afraid of the Batman, a man who dresses up as a clown...a man who calls himself the, Joker.

Joker unleashes hell on Gotham City torturing and killing people, blowing up buildings all in the hope of catching Batmans attention and he does, as well as Harvey Dent's, the new DA.

I felt that there was too much hype building up towards this film and there were so many non-fans suddenly jumping on the band-waggon that it made it hard to distinguish if this film was truly great....

Heath Ledger's portrayal was truly magnificent, he went out as a great Hollywood actor, he portrays a man truly lost to madness, a man who wants to understand why Gotham celebrates another maniac? While Aaron Eckhart plays a satisfactory Harvey Dent, he is a man who is truly trying to change things. Gary Oldman is as fine as the first, Michael Caine takes a backseat in this film but hopefully he will return in the third with a bigger part. Morgan Freeman becomes a more pivotal place within Batman's side, and does justice toward the end. Maggie Gylenhaal was okay...I felt the role needed Katie Holmes.... And finally Erice Roberts as Sal Maroni, Eric did a tremendous job playing the mobster; he oozes with charm out of every pore...

And finally I come to Christian Bale. Bale takes his character to a new level, his Bruce Wayne, is broken up into two people, the brooding 'Wayne' who spends his days stitching himself back up, and staring into space with the pain he constantly feels and the Bachelor 'Bruce', a man totally ignorant of the things that are happening around him...

This Batman is much more violent then the last, he's had enough and will throw you off a building if he has to...A creature that is losing the fear that he instilled in the hearts of his victims to the popularity.....

And finally Christopher Nolan, Nolan focuses on the action a little more and create breathtaking sequences like the Bat-pod chase, the truck flip, Batman standing on top of a huge building and then leaping off... Nolan shows Gotham in a more brighter role, as the City gleams with happiness, almost happy at what has happened in the previous film.....I leaped out of my seat towards the end when Batman takes on the SWAT team and the criminals in order to save the innocent, absolutely beautifully choreographed.

All in all, a great sequel...but hopefully will return to the roots in the third...

10.title: The movie is probably the best you will have witnessed in ages.
10.content:
This movie contains one of the most balanced plots i have ever saw. It has the right amount of action, drama, suspense and features that will make you leap out of seat and say, "damn". After watching the movie by myself the first time, me, my mother and father went to go see it the second time. I plan on seeing again about 2 or 3 more times. The movie is just that great. I'm finally growing on Christian Bale as Batman, his haughty nature and cockiness is something i actually enjoy from Batman. It kind of set's him apart from the previous Batmans.

Out of all the characters, The Joker ( Heath Ledger ) stole the show. I'm pretty sure, most, if not all you have heard about his dazzling performance. Heath did an excellent portraying The Joker, he actually got it down to the "t". So for everyone wondering, " Is the movie really this good?" Yes, it really is this good, go see it as soon as you can.

10.title: Dark, funny, intense, and a masterpiece!
10.content:
It seems to me that this film is the best of 2008. And many years to come. It is simply a masterpiece! The entire time, from the first take, to the breathtaking last, I was on the edge of my seat.

The acting, well what can I say about it. WONDERFUL! Christian Bale does a great job as Batman the second time. Aaron Echkart does a great, but disgusting Harvey Dent outlook. Morgan Freeman is always funny, along with Michal Caine. Gary Oldman does an awesome job as Gordon. Maggie G did a good job. (I'm glad they didn't bring back Katie Holmes.) But now the highlight.......THE JOKER. Heath Ledger's incredible job as the joker brought out the characters dark side, with a few funny stuff thrown in! I would take Heath Ledger's Joker over Jack's any day! Jack's Joker has the funny clown side with his white face. While Heath's brings the dark creepy side with his angry face paint covering up his violent scars.

The Joker is the best part of the entire film, his evil dark character is deliciously great. The way he stands, looks, how he kills people, and of course, the smacking of the lips. In every scene with him in it, my hands shook. I noticed a few rows down, the first time you see the joker, a woman began to cry. The film made me sad as well to.

The action was one of the greatest i've seen in a while. Nolan brings things out I have not seen in a film before. So many cool and disturbing action scenes. Nolan I think is one of the new visionary directors. This movie brought out an intense side of the story of batman. The entire film is intense. That's why I liked it.

The film in incredible. Heath Ledger would deserve an Oscar dead or not. I will see this a lot in the theater,and will be added to my DVD collection.

The film will make you laugh, jump, cry, and applaud at the end. I know I was.

10.title: A Short Review
10.content:
The Dark Knight presents a riveting and enthralling film-going experience that has topped any previous super hero films of any era. This ground-breaking masterpiece slices any reputation of 'another poor batman film' it destroys any stigma from the last batman disasters like Tim Burtons catastrophe. It reinvents, revitalises and reinvigorates the superhero genre.

The Gothic themes continue from the last film, and are used to fantastic proportions in illustrating a crime ridden evil society that the joker has plagued Gotham with. the Joker played magnificently by heath ledger brings a further element of fear and a sinister nature to the film.

Plot twists and turns, developments of characters and their emotions (particularly Harvey Dent's), mind blowing special effects, an enthralling story and Heath Ledger's portrayal of the The menacing joker, ensures that this film excels beyond any other superhero movie made before or since. this is proved by knocking out spider man 3's box office record in the opening weekend.

You'd have to be a joker to miss it!

10.title: The Knight Beckons!
10.content:
Last night was the biggest night of the summer. The closest place to park was 8 buildings away from the theatre and all 10 screenings of "The Dark Knight" were completely filled. My friends and I were lucky to see this film at midnight and I will say right now; it is worth every penny. "The Dark Knight", the newest addition to the Batman series has it all. The action, the chaos, the heroes, the villains, and most importantly BATMAN!

Christian Bale never ceases to amaze me. He still has the same elements he did in the first one and does so much more with his abilities, whether it's kicking ass or rolling around as smooth-talking billionaire Bruce Wayne. However the biggest reason why I wanted to see this film was because of the legendary performance of Heath Ledger as the infamous "Joker" (God rest his soul). Every time he was on that screen, everybody just went wild, cheering him on and waiting to see what he does next. He was absolutely flawless as the villain and "The Joker" character is the greatest villain imaginable. The fights that Batman and the Joker have are amazing. Also I was happy of how much the comic book was seen in the movie. "The Joker" is not only a member of the mob who has a taste for the theatrics and performs a couple of deadly gags, but he is also a crazy guy who just kills people. Believe me; Heath Ledger does it all.

Michael Cain is always great in everything he does, Maggie Gyllenhaal was so much better than Katie Holmes (She is not the typical damsel in distress), Gary Oldman is untouchable as newly appointed Commissioner Gordon, and Aaron Eckhart does a great job as well, playing the roll of District Attorney Harvey Dent and his alter-ego as the infamous Two-Face. This is one of those films that has an all-star cast and a great story that keeps you on the edge of your seat. Christopher Nolan has done it again and it would be great if he could make another Batman film in the next few years. But I was so happy that they dedicated the film to the memory of Heath Ledger during the credits. Everyone applauded, including me. Rest in peace Heath Ledger. Your fans will miss you. I will miss you. But in your honor, The Knight Beckons!

10.title: Not just a superhero action film,an absolute classic of a film is The Dark Knight
10.content:
I have waited for this film for so long and now I have had the privilege of watching it.Most of this movie came to me as a surprise.The Dark Knight is one of,if not,the best film of the year and probably ever made.It is one of my favorite films.It was more than a action film to me,it was an epic like Heat,The Godfather saga and Scarface among others.Christopher Nolan was brilliant at directing this so in my view,he should be nominated for an Academy Award for Best Director as well as the film as a whole being nominated for the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay as well as the Academy Award for Best Picture.

Christian Bale stars as Batman/Bruce Wayne who proves that he is just as good as he was in Batman Begins,if not better.The cast also includes Gary Oldman(Jim Gordon),Michael Caine(Alfred),Morgan Freeman(Lucius) as well as William Fichtner,Eric Roberts,Aaron Eckhart(Harvey Dent),Maggie Gyllenhaal(Rachel Dawes) and the late,great Heath Ledger as the Joker.

The cast was magnificent but I think it was Heath Ledger who made me feel proud to watch this film.His performance is worthy of an Academy Award win for Best Actor as he gave it his all and more than 100% of an effort for his role as The Joker.We will all miss you,Heath and your character who you made iconic.Rest in Peace.Heath Ledger-1979-2008.

10.title: I can't stop talking about this film...
10.content:
Mark my words, the Nolans brothers will be on the same level as the Coens shortly. Their films provide a dark and disturbing world into Batman's persona and the illusion of the life he desires, Bruce Wayne.

Simply put, this film possesses every attribute a viewer looks for in a film. It has tremendous writing, directing, acting, scenery and plot. How can you go wrong with Oldman, Eckhart, Caine, Gyllenhaal, Ledger, Freeman and Bale. A superstar cast that doesn't disappoint.

I won't spoil the film for anyone, but I urge all to see it. It is my own selfish need, but I feel robbed that cinema will never again see such a disturbing and entertaining character personified in Ledgers performance. RIP...

10.title: The Best Batman Movie of ALL Time!
10.content:
I love it. I love it more than my croissant. I love it more than my silk bathrobe. I love it more than Audrey Hepburn.

Batman faces the man who would ultimately be his greatest nemesis and finds himself in a position he's never been in. The Joker keeps him and the rest of Gotham on their toes with his random videos and attacks.

I must say The Dark Knight surpasses all Batman films due to the plot, acting, music, artistic direction...

Christian Bale - excellent.

Heath Ledger made this movie. Simple. He was awesome and it was because of him I went to watch it thrice.

Watch The Dark Knight. You will LOVE it!!!!

10.title: Dark, different and twisted (review, no spoilers)
10.content:
Top notch and superb, The Dark Knight delivers all the goods. I particularly enjoyed the way the film transfered from scene to scene as it could satisfy a wide audience base by giving lots of story and information, without having to drag on and explain everything for half an hour at a time (This despite the fact that the movie surpassed the two hour mark). The way it is filmed reminds me of reading a comic book. As each new scene came about I found myself almost feeling like I was flipping the pages of a video comic.

Heath Ledger is superb, and the Oscar hype he has received is well deserved. However, I hope those who give him that consideration truly feel that way. His performance as the Joker, as expected, is truly nothing like anything we have seen before. I fear that some may not see this performance for what it truly is, as Ledger's untimely death brought about a lot of attention. Hopefully people truly do feel that his performance is Oscar worthy, and aren't just blinded by the idea that this is his last film. The way he portrayed the Joker was twisted, funny, scary and unreal. Truly Oscar worthy material by Ledger if this movie gets the type of attention it deserves.

All and all, The Dark Knight is a very new and refreshing take on the super hero movie. It offers a host of brilliant characters, twists and surprises, and a whole new look on filming styles for the super hero genre. All I can say is that I just can't wait to watch it again.

10.title: Exquisite!
10.content:
I have long awaited this movie and it has finally come! I just got home from the first showing in the theater and I'm very enthusiastic! I really enjoyed Batman Begins and ever since I have been overly excited. Especially after I found out who was cast for this movie.

The Dark Knight is flawless! There's no doubt it will pick up some awards on the red carpet. The plot is dark and twisted with splashes of humor along the way.

Christian Bale rejuvenated his role as Batman and portrays the Caped Crusader in a heroic way bringing a thrilling performance.

I'll be honest in saying I was glad there would be someone new to pick up the role of Rachel Dawes. Katie Holmes just didn't seem to fit. But Maggie Gyllenhaal is lovely as the Gotham City DA.

Harvey Dent was a key protagonist in the film to tie it all together. Aaron Eckhart is very talented! I was surprised in the way he took over his role and shined.

And, of course, the true star is Heath Ledger who is rendering The Joker. He doesn't hold back in anyway! Bold and fearless, Heath deserves a posthumous Oscar for his brilliant acting. Truthfully I wish he would have had more screen-time because he plays the Killing Clown in a way that makes you want to see more. You lose site of the supposedly "painfully shy" actor.

Heath steals the scenes, but certainly doesn't put the other actors to shame.

Overall The Dark Knight is thrilling, sinister, suspenseful and deserving of all the hype and publicity. For those of us who were a fan of Heath Ledger, it's hard to watch his final complete film without feeling a little down that there's no more exciting (complete) portrayals.

I'm keeping my fingers crossed that TDK will break Spiderman 3's weekend box office record! This movie isn't to be missed! 10/10

Rest in peace, Heath Ledger- 1979-2008. ♥

10.title: Batman's Back!
10.content:
I never saw Batman Begins, but I didn't have to when I saw it today. The Dark Knight is crammed with action in every corner of Gotham City. Batman's back with Christian Bale as the caped vigilante. But there're two new villains. There's the sadistic Joker (Heath Ledger) and Two-Face (Aaron Eckhart), but they're not the Jack Nicholson and Tommy Lee Jones you saw back about twenty years ago. Nope. The villains are violent, corrupted, and not by just on the outside. If you haven't seen this movie, and you do, you'll definitely seen what I mean.

Anyway, I enjoyed this movie a lot! A lot of action, a lot of unsuspecting things will happen, I guarantee it. Good, good, good movie that deserves and Oscar this year.

Total 10 out of 10

10.title: Best Movie Ever!
10.content:
For the faint of heart be warned--Here be spoilers.

Let me start off with, Yes; I have been looking up every small piece of info about this movie for a year, Yes; I ordered my tickets 12 years in advance, Yes; I counted down the hours and minutes till the movie opened and Yes; I stood at the theater 2 hours early to make sure I got a really good seat. I'm a fan of Batman, always have been always will be, through the good and Batman and Robin.

But this Bat movie had so much hype that even if you're not a fan you are drawn to see it, if only to see Heath Ledgers last movie. And after seeing it I can only say one word....Holy Crap. Take everything you know about movies and throw it out the window people, this movie is so full of twist and turns that the 2 hour 45 min run time seems like 10 minutes and once the last frame of the movie is over, you'll find yourself asking "When is the third one now?"

The Dark Knight picks up right where Batman Begins left off, and the caped crusader could not be in better form. New gizmo's and gadgets make the capture of the joker look good.

Which brings me to, the Joker. I personally have never been a fan of Heath Ledger (My daughter thinks hes dreamy) but this role made me a fan at once. THIS IS THE JOKER! Forget Cesar Romero and Jack Nicholson, while good versions, they fell far from who the Joker really was, a sadistic serial killer with no morals or guilt. This Joker is scary, and believe me, you would not want him at your birthday party. My wife (who is a shrink) is watching this trying to diagnose his mental illnesses, and I'm laughing because I'm watching a comic book literally come to life. We've come a long way from the 60's batman series and its about time we saw the characters for who they really are.

We have the usual players: Bale, Caine, Freeman, Oldman (Except Katie Holmes, but oh well, her loss) Two Face even makes an appearance here, and he reminds me of Shadow of the Bat comics, a very good look for him, way way better than Tommy Lee Jones' Two Face.

However, a few things did Bother me, and I thought I'd share them with you, Like:

1: Gordons wife, her name is Barbara....You mean like Batgirl? Isn't Barbara Gordon commissioner Gordons DAUGHTER? Ewwww.

2: Two Faces 'transformation'. It seemed really rushed, a big lead up just to have a small 'poof' and hes TwoFace. Seemed a silly way to have it happen if you ask me, which no one did.

3: With Two Face, the eye on his scarred side, how does it stay moist? He has no eye lids to blink with. Does he use special eye drops or something?

4: OK, so some dweeb guy at Wayne Enterprises discovers 'Hmmm, a lot of stuff is missing', why did it take so long for this to be discovered? You'd think with a huge business like that there would be more checks and balances.

5: On the same note with the dweeb guy, how did the guy decide 'Bruce Wayne is Batman' why not Fox? Fox had access to all that stuff and was obviously the one who lied about the stuff going missing? Why would he go after Wayne of all people first?

6: Maggie Gyllenhaal....What is the deal? Every line she had seemed like she was whining through it. Thank god we didn't have to put up with much of her in this role.

7: What is with Batmans voice? Take a cough drop already.

But even with my nonsense complaining, this is the best I have seen in a LONG time. Best film I have seen ever if I may be so bold. The hype was well met and this one is even better than the first. If this is any indication of what to expect from this new Batman franchise, we are in good hands.

Long Live Batman!

10.title: The New Benchmark Of Comic-Based Movies!
10.content:
Kudos to Christopher Nolan for directing such an intense two and half hour thrill ride which pushes the benchmark of the comic series to a whole new level! And one of those few movies which not only lives up to the hype, but even surpasses it! Truly remarkable feat of performance by Heath Ledger which further defines the character Joker more than ever! And in my opinion; even surpasses the equally matched counterpart Jack Nicholson's portrayal of the same character in the decade old Batman Movie.

The tension portrayed in being a Batman and also at same time being Bruce Wayne is truly fine work done by Christian Bale. Also worth mentioning. Aaron Eckhart pulls off an remarkably performed transformation from an Attorney to 2-face. And the rest of the cast have done a pretty good job too. All in all the Dark Knight is one those few movies where its really difficult to pin point any weak aspects at all! So to conclude The Dark Knight has become the "Godfather" of comic-based movies and easily one of the best films ever made!

10.title: Absolutely Incredible
10.content:
I saw this movie opening night and once again two nights later. The first time I saw it, I was like, "Yeah, that was good, not as good as 'Batman Begins.'" Then I saw it again. And I absolutely loved it the second time. Now, I just want to see it again, too bad I don't have enough money to see a movie 3,4,5 or more times.

Heath Ledger was absolutely impeccable in his role of the Joker. If I were a 13 year old kid watching this movie, I'd have nightmares. Christian Bale improved his Batman character which I didn't think was possible. And Eckhart played Harvey Dent so well that he even confused me that I couldn't tell if he was good or bad, although I knew the story.

It's really sad that Bale, Ledger and Eckhart can't play together again because they made this movie what it was. I HOPE they decide to go for another one, it will be tough to top this...If it's possible at all. I am begging the makers of this movie to make another one. Christian Bale has proved to me once again that he is the GREATEST superhero actor, ever. And I'm a Superman fan.

Please lets see the next edition to this terrific duo of movies. "Why so serious?"

10.title: Magnificent
10.content:
I had been looking forward to The Dark Knight since the middle of 2007, and the death of Heath Ledger increased the already growing hype surrounding the film. Approaching the cinema, I decided to forget the hype, forget my own desire to watch, so I could do the film justice in my own way. I'm glad I did, as I think this is the 21st Century's best film so far, it surpasses the hype magnificently.

The film centres around Batman, James Gordon and Harvey Dent's struggle against the Joker, a new criminal in Gotham City who is running riot. As the city begins to descend into chaos, our heroes begin to see what they must become in order to stop him.

From the opening scene, it is clear that The Dark Knight is more about the villain than the hero. Heath Ledger is simply unbelievable as the Joker, he bristles with psychotic energy in every scene. His body language and vocal range are an inspiration and he is a truly terrifying character. As a Heath Ledger fan, my expectations were exceeded beyond belief. The real surprise was Aaron Eckheart, who was at times even more chilling as Two-Face than Ledger. Watching him slowly turn from Gotham City's white knight into an evil, vengeful monster is brilliant. Christian Bale is as good as he was in Batman Begins, and it was nice to see Maggie Gyllenhall surpass Katie Holmes. Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman's performances were several levels above what they were in Batman Begins. Each actor complemented each other, and shares a common plus point with Anchorman in that it was as near as can be to perfectly cast.

I think this film's main strength is it's writing. The script delivers constant high quality dialogue and some of the best twists and turns since Fight Club, and I love Fight Club. I love how Nolan adapted the characters into what worked the best, in particular the villains. The campness of the Joker and Two-Face's previous incarnations is non-existent, and would be out of place in this version of Gotham City. The Two-Face character is visceral and graphic, and Harvey Dent's fall from grace is handled brilliantly. The origins of the Joker are not shown, merely referenced by the Joker himself in some horrifyingly genius dialogue.

I was blown away by The Dark Knight, it was almost perfect. The only niggle I had was that I would have liked to have seen more of Cillian Murphy as Scarecrow. This film was a fitting end to Heath Ledger's career, and the Joker is definitely the role he will be most remembered for. The must-see film of 2008.

10.title: One of the Year's Best Films
10.content: I was completely stunned by the ferocity of "The Dark Knight". I've yet to wrap my head around it all. Christopher Nolan has upped the ante in every possible way. The muscular storytelling, intense action, impeccable production, direction, and the ensemble cast, are all on their best game. Ledger is a revelation. Arguably, it's his best performance, and the performance of the year. His Joker will live on as the most vital villain to hit the big screen in years and for many, many more years to come. The magnitude of the finale in 'Knight' is emotionally deep, haunting and inspiring. "The Dark Knight" will rattle the senses and linger in your thoughts long after.

10.title: Not just a great Batman movie, but a great movie period.
10.content:
So, it's finally here. After seeing the Joker playing card at the end of Batman Begins, we've been waiting for this day. I've finally seen it. I've let it resonate in my mind for a while. I've gone over the good and the bad, and yes, there are some things I was not a fan of. I'll get to those first.

There are only a few things that bothered me.

1) The sonar. It seems so weird compared to the rest of the film.

2) Sometimes Batman's voice gets dangerously close to laughable.

3) I wish the Joker had gotten a last scene in Arkham. He's just left there literally hanging, and that is the last time we see him in the film. No final shot.

4) Michael Caine had so little to do in the film. Compared to how much he did in BB, he is just a bit player here.

That's really it. So now the good stuff...

What can I say that hasn't been said already? It's just a great movie. After thinking about this a while, I've realized just how different BB and TDK are. Despite the same director, they are completely different in their style and presentation. If anyone has seen the Prestige, also written by the Nolan brothers, it's very evident that Jonah Nolan helped write TDK. Like the Prestige, the story gets going and never stops. It never allows for a breather. Stop paying attention for even a minute, and you can get lost. It's that quick. I expected a film like BB, and instead I got something else. Notice how this isn't listed as a negative. It's just not what I expected.

The Joker is exactly how Nolan said he would be. He has no real storyline. He exists just to push people to their breaking point. He is a terrorist in ways no other villain has been. Hell, he out terrorizes real terrorists! He is a real enigma, and you always know when he is approaching because of his theme. I loved this. Whenever the Joker's presence is imminent, the "Why So Serious" theme starts. It sounds literally like a tornado siren. Every time that started, I was thinking, "Oh crap, he's coming!" It's exactly what Nolan intended, and it works beautifully, building tension to his appearance. And the Joker is not really in the film that much. Like I said, he is more of an enigma. He's even doing things when he is not on screen, putting his plot in motion. His presence is felt, but not seen. He's also insanely (literally) funny. The way he moves, talks, and acts is funny. Even when giving his speeches about his philosophy on life, he is still funny. However, this does not lessen his impact. It heightens it even more. It's great stuff.

Also, there are some incredibly tension inducing, nail biting scenes. One is where the Joker simultaneously murders both Loeb and the judge prosecuting the mob, while also attacking Bruce's fund raiser for Harvey Dent. As this happens, the theme starts kicking in. You know he is coming. Something is going to happen, and when it does, it does not disappoint. Another great sequence is when this guy (can't remember his name) knows Bruce's secret, and is about to reveal it to Mike Engel on GCN. But before he can, Joker calls in and says that if he is not dead in one hour, a hospital will blow up. Total city-wide panic. What hospital could it be? No one knows, but because people want to save their loved ones, the man is constantly being targeted for assassination. This whole sequence leading up to Joker and Harvey's confrontation is without a doubt my favorite part of the film. And that nurse scene is hilarious.

Despite Two-face's end, I didn't feel cheated like some people. Ya, it's surprising he was killed off, but in that short time we got a Two-face that delivers in what we want. Also, Harvey Dent is a great character. Dent is a little psycho before he becomes Two-face. The whole scene where he interrogates one of Joker's henchmen really shows you the path he is destined for. Like the Joker says, "Madness is like gravity, all you need is a little push." And a little push is all Harvey needs to become a madman. It feels totally plausible too, and this is because of the madness Harvey had before he becomes Two-face.

Ultimately, I would not say it is better than BB. I like them both. They are both so different. Everyone did a great job. And after the film ended, my father, who loved Batman89 and Jack Nicholson, turned to me and said, "That probably will win an Oscar." Enough said...

10.title: A Spectacle
10.content: The Dark Knight is a superb movie. The best Batman film ever made and the best Christopher Nolan film ever made with Memento following close behind. Tonight I will be going to see Inception to see if it beats these other two films out. I will write a review later today for that film. The Dark Knight has everything needed for a summer blockbuster but also for a great epic movie. It stands alone outside of all the other Batman films and does not feel at all like a sequel. The acting all around in this film is great, the best performance being Heath Ledger for his insane interpretation of everyone's favorite Batman villain. The screenplay and story is compelling with many subplots going on all at the same time with all of them being equally entrancing. Another great actor to mention is Aaron Eckhart making us love his character and care for him despite what he turns into. The special effects are nothing short of amazing and the replay value in this film is never ending. One of the best movies of the decade. I hope this helped keep checking to see what I think of Inception.

10.title: "The Dark Knight" is a shining and moving piece of cinema!
10.content:
Let me begin by saying that what I expected to see was another super-hero movie with a clichéd storyline  the good vs. evil thread, the megalomaniac who turns evil with excessive power, the humble common-man who becomes the hero, etc. I expected to see the quintessential super-hero movie with oodles of patriotism and boisterous bravado, none of which I thought would justify the 200 bucks I spent on the ticket.

What I saw instead was a grim tale of a city going through dark times, besieged by crime and corruption, further exacerbated by a maniacal madman whose primary objective is the spread of absolute anarchy. A movie which transcended the level of all other super-hero movies by providing not only a scintillating visual spectacle, but more importantly also a deep psychological treatise on the best and the worst amongst us and the factors that motivate us to be either supremely good or maniacally bad. And let me say that it was worth the 200 bucks!

Plot-Summary: The story begins with a violent bank robbery orchestrated by a masked man who calls himself the "Joker". We are given an indication of his ruthlessness, when he double-crosses his accomplices, killing them mercilessly. Then, we are introduced to "The Mob", whose wings have been clipped by Batman's heroics (Christian Bale). The Mob's operations are shut-down and its members indicted by the legal acumen of Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart), the newly appointed crime-intolerant District Attorney (D.A.), with the help of a beautiful assistant Rachel Dawes (Maggie Gyllenhaal). The Joker suggests that in return for half their financial assets, he neutralizes Batman, to which the Mob reluctantly complies. The rest of the movie chronicles the war between The Batman and the D.A. Harvey Dent on one side and the Joker on the other. As the war progresses, we see the balance constantly tilt in favor of the evil, helping to maintain the overpowering sense of gloom, which serves as harbinger of a dark future.

It might not be completely "new", but it is the manner the story unfolds that leaves you spellbound and deeply unsettled. There is a careful examination of the moral conundrum that Batman and Harvey Dent face as they go about dealing with crime in the city. Harvey Dent is the kind of hero that Gotham City deserves: fighting crime with legal recourse, but the vigilante Batman is the one that it needs currently. The Batman feels that Dent's methodologies are more suitable for a civilized society, but is forced to don the mantle of an outlawed vigilante. Both of these men face tough choices when they are confronted by an evil madman who is not motivated by money, but by the pure black desire for absolute chaos. The Joker threatens the city with increasing violence as a bait for Batman to reveal his true identity. The troubling conundrum comes up: should Batman give himself up to prevent bloodshed and cause a moral victory for the anarchist ideology or should he risk it in order to subdue the Joker?

On the performance front: Christian Bale as the Batman/Bruce Wayne manages to switch rather effortlessly in the two persona: being the persistent Batman, while also being the flamboyant millionaire. Aaron Eckhart as Harvey Dent, the crime-tough D.A. gives a moving performance as a good, earnest man who is befallen by tragedy. Maggie Gyllenhaal plays Rachel Dawes as a mixture of toughness and tenderness. The rest of the cast is also spot-on.

But the one that beats 'em all, is the portrayal of the Joker by the Late Heath Ledger, whose performance is stellar and superlative. It is not everyday that one gets to experience evil in its purest form. Throughout the movie, I found myself spell-bound by this Joker, grudgingly admiring his capacity at evil! I couldn't help finding him more dynamic than the "good" but rather rigid Batman. This ambivalence of feelings is a testament of Ledger's portrayal of the Joker: he manages to make a character whom you should despise into a character whom you are mildly amused with! His is truly a spine-chilling performance!

At 2hours 45mins, this movie is indeed unusually long, but there was never a dull moment in the movie and the screenplay kept things tight. The direction and cinematography is spot on, managing to capture a range of emotions on different characters, all from the most strategic angles. The special effects were spectacular and complemented the stylish action on screen.

There are a lot of moments in this movie that gives you goose-bumps. Most of them have the Joker and Harvey featured prominently. These two characters steal the show from the Batman. Particularly memorable is the moment when the Joker tells Batman that "when the chips fall down, these so-called 'civilized' people will become wolves and chaos would ensue". Later on, when such a 'chip-falling' situation occurs (not revealed because it would be a plot-spoiler), in a spine-chilling moment, we realize that the Joker's prediction might come true. In that moment of epiphany, you realize that The Joker is simply a doppelganger of the Batman  the evil complementary alter-ego which completes the whole.

Its already on the Top 250 list within the top 10. Whether it is worthy of such a spot shall no doubt kick a storm in IMDb's message boards. What is more relevant as the troubling questions it raises (which have tremendous parallels to the real world). This movie is indeed an unusual entrant  a super-hero movie which crosses its genre and becomes a poetically grim dissertation on the dilemma that we all face: whether it is prudent to become evil in order to fight evil. And yes, Heath Ledger deserves to be at least nominated (if not win) for the Oscars for his haunting performance  it was his parting shot which deserves to be honored.

Bottom-line: A fantastic masterpiece!

10.title: The Dark Knight - A Masterpiece of a film
10.content: The Dark Knight is the best comic book film and one of the best films ever made. It is a dark, and gripping tale of Crime, psychopaths, and the city of Gotham. It can't be said enough that Heath Ledger's performance as the Joker is stunning. His last role will be known as his best and is Oscar worthy. This Joker is a terrifying sociopath which will be remembered for years to come. Christin Bale is once again a great Bruce Wayne/ Batman. The viewer really feels for his character and his struggles. Michael Caine, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freemen are also great as usual. Maggie Glyhanall adds depth to the character of Rachael Dawes and is much better than Katie Holmes. Aaron Eckhart is a fantastic Harvey Dent and has an impressive and gruesome alter ego. The action scenes are spectacular especially since there was little CGI. The villains and mob bosses are all greatly casted and used. The music and score are great especially Joker's theme song. The Dark Knight has broken several box office records and currently is rated #1 on IMDb. it truly deserves all the honors.

10.title: Astounding (Perfect)
10.content:
The Dark Knight was 100% astounding. The first time I think I've ever walked out of a theater and not had a least one complaint. The perfect superhero movie. I'll remember the movie for its top notch performances. Every scene Ledger is in is pure magic. He doesn't steal the scenes hes in, he takes them. Eckhart is absolutely insane as Dent. You really feel for this guy. He is completely controlled throughout the entire movie. Even as Two-Face. Nolan took the screen time to make us believe in Dent and at the end it shows. Bale is perfect as Batman again. Alfred, Fox, Gordon, etc all get there due. I will remember this film mainly for how spread out everything is. Every character is used. The story is complex, but perfect for the particular movie. Visuals are also excellent. I really can't think of one thing I disliked about the film.

I'll remember this film for Ledger's and Eckhart's performances, the character development, and the overall fantastic directing on the part of Nolan. The perfect superhero movie. 10 out of a possible 10.

10.title: In Brightest Day, In Darkest Night........
10.content:
Where to begin? Well probably with Batman Begins' last scene and a Joker playing card. From this moment on, most fanboys (and I include myself amongst this number) have been frothing at the mouth at the prospect of a sequel. Three years later, Christopher Nolan and his brother, have delivered a script, and Nolan has helmed a film which transcends the limitations of the genre that it is nominally in.

From the opening scene of a daring bank robbery executed in broad daylight, introducing us to the Joker, which was obviously inspired by Michael Mann's Heat, to the unexpected and dark ending, the film is relentlessly paced and never lets up. Whilst there are small touched of humour here and there in the film, primarily supplied by Alfred (played with a deft touch by Michael Caine) and the Joker (in an iconic performance by Heath Ledger, more of which later).

For those wanting nothing more than a rattling good "superhero movie", there are more than enough action set pieces, as Nolan has become more assured behind the camera shooting action, but there is so much more here than simple action.

The main story arc of the film is Harvey Dent's (played by a very good Aaron Eckhart), whose descend from grace informs the action. Gary Oldman is wonderful as "everyman" Jim Gordon, one of the few good policemen in a corrupt force, and the rest of the cast is very good, including Maggie Gyllenhall as Rachel Dawes.

But the strength of the film is carried on the backs of the two primary characters, Heath Ledger's Joker, a sado-masochistic, psychotic, sociopathic killer with no limits, no boundaries, no rules and Christian Bale's Batman for whom structure and order are all.

Its a huge shame that Ledger will never get a chance to reprise the role, since in my opinion it is destined to become iconic, like Vader or Lector. But Bale's turn as both Bruce Wayne and Batman is excellent as well, and he fully makes us believe in Batman.

The dialogue is often witty and intelligent, and always serves to drive the plot forward, without sacrificing character development for any of the major characters along the way. So far I have only seen the film once, but am planning to go again today.

Its difficult to call a film a classic of its type or a masterpiece so quickly after the film's original release. However, if I was tempted to do so, this would be one of the very very few films I would consider calling a classic, and perhaps even a masterpiece....

10.title: Best Comic Book Movie Ever
10.content:
Of course I have not seen every comic book movie. I know that but of all the movies I have seen, this is by far the best. The dark side of this movie is so deep that at times it is hard to believe parents would take their 13-year-old kids to see this movie. Personally I would have nightmares if I was 13.

Christian Bale pulls the batman role off perfectly. The joker leaves me speechless in every scene. There are no corny one-liners like you expect from a comic book movie: this is not Iron Man or Spider Man (although I did enjoy Iron Man). This series is so much more serious and creepier than the previous batman movies. Just looking at the Joker puts a chill down your spine.

Seeing the events in the movie are enjoyable for everyone, you don't have to be a fan of the batman comics or comic books to include this movie in your all time favorites.
