7.content: I'm probably one of the biggest Batman fans. Even though I enjoy most things about the movie, I strongly believe Ben Affleck makes a far better Batman. I believe his body type best resembles Batman is the comics.

7.title: Missing Something
7.content:
Dark Knight has been highly hyped. Superhero is not my preferred genre, but I had to check this one out. Unfortunately, it didn't have much of an effect on me. Some things were interesting, like (a) the dilemmas that Joker put Batman into and (b) the idea that people need a hero whose face they can see, but that was about it.

The main characters were too simplistic. I got no feel for what made the Joker tick. And, Batman's slick world was just too slick. When he suddenly re-jiggered 30 million cell phones to create a SONAR tracking device...that's when the movie jumped the shark, IMO.

Credit where credit is due: 2-Face's make-up was amazing. SFX dept earns a point.

Christopher Nolan's pacing is so fast that viewers have little time to notice how implausible things are. For example, the police chief (Gary Oldman) gets shot in an assassination attempt on the mayor. Later it's revealed that he's alive and that getting shot was the plan. Huh? What if the shooter had aimed six inches higher? Chief's head would've been blown off. Not a great plan.

Also, I grew tired of Joker's (Heath Ledger) speechifying. Basically, every scene he appears in features him stepping forward to orate.

Finally, what's with the mob bosses of Gotham? They were a bunch of paper mache losers. The movie spends quite a bit of time with Lao, but in the end I'm not even sure what happened to him.

P.s., Hilarious that there was an incinerator in the super high tech Batcave. WTH?

7.title: THE DARK KNIGHT (Christopher Nolan, 2008) ***
7.content:
Apart from the usual summer blockbuster expectations, this film acquired an instant mythical aura all its own following Heath Ledger's untimely demise (which inevitably borders on overhype). As long-rumored, Ledger's portrayal of The Joker is electrifying and leaves one in no doubt of the late actor's talent and versatility; still, though undeniably creepy – especially given his penchant for macabre TV appearances – he lacks the flamboyance (even if he does get to appear in drag!) and sense of fun that The Joker of Cesar Romero, Jack Nicholson and even the animated series possessed! Besides, I don't understand why he's seen constantly recruiting henchmen from the other Gotham gangs when the film-makers chose to depict him as such a manic, trigger-happy thug that he does practically all of the shooting himself – with his anonymous lackeys being there merely to get treacherously shot in the back or hand him weapons! And what's up with leaving him dangling from a stairwell? It's not like he's coming back in the inevitable third entry, no? Incidentally, I feel that all the ongoing talk of posthumously awarding Ledger an Oscar in tribute is premature. By the way, the fact that the film is currently topping the all-time 250 list on IMDb – not that I ever cared for that particular list myself, mind you – is, quite frankly, ridiculous!

While I can't really complain of it ever being slow, the film's 152-minute running-time is definitely excessive and could easily have been thinned down by as much as 45 minutes if some of the less interesting vignettes were dropped altogether: among the many needlessly intricate subplots, the chief offenders were the whole Asian financier segment, the dead-end assault on the Japanese skyscraper full of hostages and the climactic 'confrontation' between the two respective shiploads of evacuated citizens and jailbirds. Personally, I don't understand why the film-makers chose to divide the time between the Scarecrow (albeit a mere cameo from Cillian Murphy but welcome nonetheless), the mobsters, The Joker and Two-Face rather than devote a leaner (if consequently less ambitious) narrative to the most famous of Batman's opponents – as indeed Tim Burton's 1989 revival of the caped crusader had itself done. At the very end, I also didn't get why tolerated vigilante Batman must suddenly become a hunted fugitive from the law for the good of Gotham – what for and on whose authority? Gary Oldman's final monologue was supposed to shed some light on this, I guess, but I didn't catch some of it because of the music drowning out the dialogue!

The returning actors from the first film of this new franchise (Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman) have all grown nicely into their roles – especially Caine and Oldman (so much so that I was disappointed to see him get 'bumped off' half-way through); that said, Batman himself seemed to be merely engaged in action sequences or else make split-second appearances to make his latest report to Gordon; by the way, I too found his scowling demeanor irritating – which his raspy voice sometimes rendered inaudible! On the other hand, the new additions to the fold – Aaron Eckhart (as unlucky D.A. Harvey 'Two-Face' Dent) and his gushing secretary Maggie Gyllenhaal (replacing Katie Holmes) – were less impressive (and their relationship equally dreary and time-consuming), which is just as well since both their characters lose their lives by the end of it (or so we are led to believe); Two-Face was supposed to be another criminal mastermind but, here, all he seems to care about is avenge his lover's death! Incidentally, I never thought I'd say this, but I enjoyed seeing Eric Roberts playing the meaty supporting role of one of Gotham's leading mobsters.

Where special effects are concerned, the spectacular capsizing of the trailer was the film's most breath-taking moment and Two-Face's CGI-animated facial decomposition was not too distracting under the circumstances (reminding one of Griffin Dunne from AN American WEREWOLF IN London [1981]). Those of you who've read thus far may be questioning my eventual *** rating but, seriously, I did enjoy the film and there were certainly several good sequences and performances in it but, overall, in the words of George Harrison, "it's all too much"

7.title: Best Batman
7.content:
The Dark Knight is a thrilling and visually stunning superhero film that raises the bar for the genre. Christian Bale delivers a powerful performance as Batman, and Heath Ledger's portrayal of the Joker is nothing short of legendary. The film's dark and gritty tone adds a level of realism to the story, and the action sequences are expertly choreographed and intense.

However, the film does have its flaws. The pacing can be a bit slow at times, and some of the supporting characters are not fleshed out as well as they could have been.

Overall, The Dark Knight is a must-see for fans of superhero films and is a strong addition to the Batman franchise. I would give it a 7 out of 10.

7.title: Overrated but enjoyable!
7.content:
Now, let me start by saying that I have, and always will think The Dark Knight is overrated. I think the only reason it got so much attention was because of the whole publicity around Heath Ledger etc. Let me say, if Ledger were still alive, I feel the film would probably perform well, but really not as much as it did. So yeah, with this in mind I sat down this afternoon to watch it. It's grown on me a bit since last viewing, but I still think it's very overrated. I've said this a lot in the past, but Nolans trilogy just isn't Batman to me. I see them as very well written action movies. I just don't feel he's captured the look and feel of what Batman is supposed to be (For me anyway, this is my opinion). It's very strange though, since I prefer Batman Begins, to something that can be considered more traditional Batman (Joker etc), but anyway, I find The Dark Knight to be a very well written, and entertaining film. Heath Ledger is, one of the strongest aspects of the movie, and even though he's not my favourite Joker (I have to say that I prefer Jack Nicholsen and Mark Hammil), he put forward a very good performance. Gary Oldman is fantastic once again as Commissioner Gordon, and Michael Caine delivers a rather small, but unforgettable role as Alfred.

Overall, The Dark Knight is very enjoyable, the action set pieces are stunning, and the dialogue is beautifully delivered (Except "WHEREE ISS HEEE!?!?!?! and "I'M NOT WEARINGG HOCKKEYYY PANNNNTTTSS! and "THEN YOU'RE GONNA LOVE ME!", but we'll get to that later) Despite how much I enjoyed it though, I still think the movie is just a bit too long and has a few pacing issues. I think the pacing of Batman Begins was pitch perfect, and I feel that The Dark Knight dragged quite a bit in places, especially the Hong Kong scene, which i didn't think added anything to the final film, and a totally forgettable sequence. I thought Two Face, even though a good villain, was un-needed. His scenes could've easily been cut, and made his reveal into some kind of cliffhanger for The Dark Knight Rises. I just don't think his character was that well developed to be honest. I wasn't that much of a fan of him, but it was a nice performance all the same. I also don't know the reason as to why Katie Holmes didn't return to the part of Rachel Dawes, but I felt that Maggie Gyllenhaal was a very worthy replacement, ALTHOUGH it would've had a lot more emotional impact to have the same actress in both parts considering what happens.

It's very strange actually, because I thought that Christian Bale was the strongest aspect of Batman Begins, and here I feel he is one of the weakest. I don't really care for Bruce Wayne that much, maybe that's intentional. I know he's an international playboy type character, but I'm just not a fan. I really enjoyed his performance in Batman Begins a lot, and I thought his performance in The Dark Knight was a bit disappointing. I also spent the entire movie getting constantly more and more annoyed at his Batman voice. It's completely unnecessary and there's no reason why he just couldn't speak normally, he did in Batman Begins. Although. I'm not going to blame Bale for this, because apparently it was an editing decision made in post production.

The Dark Knight is littered with beautiful scenes and lovely dialogue. It's definitely a strong film in it's own right, despite it's flaws, and it has managed (Along with Batman Begins) to heighten my excitement for The Dark Knight Rises (Which I really wasn't that interested in seeing).

7.title: I don't get why people loved this movie so much
7.content:
Saw The Dark Knight on opening night and to be truthful, I thought it was just an OK movie. Yes, maybe the best movie of 2008 so far (haven't seen a lot of movies this year however). How it's number one on IMDb is beyond belief. To say that this movie is better than The Godfather, The Shawshank Redemption or even Lord of the Rings is a mystery. Probable the best comic book movie, but that's not saying much since all the others are pretty average.

The movie was good, not great. Wasn't Joker supposed to be the one that murdered Bruce Wayne's parents? Heath Ledger was great as the Joker. But to be honest, Jack Nicholson was better and more of a "joker". Maggie Gyllenhal was boring and there were times where I just wanted to close my eyes and sleep. Also, why bring the Scarecrow for like just 2 minutes??? Batman doing his stuff from underneath a cargo freight??? That Batpod looked corny and really looks like it should be impossible to drive. And why does Christian Bale talk so "horrible" as Batman?

The movie did have its moments, but overall, I give it a 7 out of 10. Ya, I'm sure I'll get a lot of people hating this, but truth is, this movie just didn't wow me.

7.title: It's good. Very good. Not brilliant, but good.
7.content:
Could this be the film of 2008? Perhaps so. Perhaps again the benchmark isn't very high. Is this the best superhero film of 2008? I would have thought clearly so. Even allowing for Hancock as the same type ;-).

There is more than superhero here and it's a beautifully produced movie. There's some clever stuff, there's some excellent sub-plots but ultimately it's position as a great movie is compromised by the subject matter. Much as it attempts to lay in the human condition and the dilemmas of man it ultimately reverts to action status to get its kicks and that will forever compromise it.

The cigar remains in the humidor.

7.title: Over rated
7.content: This movie isn't that great in my opinion. The only reason why this movie has such a high rating is because the performance by Heath Ledger. Which in my opinion is incredible, but that shouldn't make up for the whole movie as a whole. I personally thought the dark knight rises was better

7.title: Nolan creates brilliant multi-colored film and yet it all seems so familiar...
7.content: Well, I must say that the imagery in this movie is fantastic. I love the directing. Very symbolic. The acting is truly brilliant. Heath Ledger is most definitely a fine actor and very impressive. However, this movie was not so outstanding and I was not awe-stricken. The plots were very repetitive. It was as if I had seen it all before. Granted, the joker was extremely malevolent but that scene where he tells Batman that the city will turn on him and they will not love him anymore--all I could see was that scene from Spider-Man. Goblin speaks almost the exact same words. The only difference is that Spider-Man was made six years earlier. Also, the mind games that Two-Face plays with his victims reminded me of the horrifying games of Russian roulette during The Deer Hunter. Or quite possibly the game of life and death that Anton Chigurh plays with his victims in No Country for Old Men. Life is depended upon a single flip of the coin. Besides this movie not being very original, it was overall pretty good. The Spider-Man 3-like structure of bringing in a second villain halfway through and carrying on several subplots worked out for Dark Knight, I guess. I would recommend it if you have not seen any of the following movies. Otherwise, it is like watching a brilliantly directed sum-up of so many other better movies before The Dark Knight's time.

7.title: Not a Masterpiece, not even close. Batman Begins reigns.
7.content:
The following includes spoilers of the movie in order to review some of the aspects that stand out and those that are ludicrous.

In the past month, I've grown accustomed to changing the channels during TV commercial breaks and walking out on the previews at the movie theater, just to miss the trailers and TV spots of The Dark Knight. The goal was to watch this film as my parents and many people approached "Jaws" in the 70's: clueless regarding what the movie is about. I was somewhat successful. As a fan of Batman and Christopher Nolan, I was very convinced this movie would turn out to be a very good so if I would look for the clips of the usual summer propaganda, my rewarding experience would not be as great. Impatience lead me to buy a ticket for the premiere of The Dark Knight, but I left the theater only knowing that this wasn't no Jaws and certainly no masterpiece.

I liked that the movie is around 150 minutes and I could have stayed 6 hours if it were the case because the movie is visually stunning. The problem consists in the story of Batman as real person with the agility, money and technology. The adaptation of the renewal of the franchise was based on this "real" concept and it is the reason why special effects were totally minimized. But what happened when we got to see Batman with white eyes interlaced with shots of 3d modeling and the voice-over of Morgan Freeman like the super cliché that that is. The idea of the bat sonar might have been an innovative concept but the way that it is explained to us does not work. You can even project that the Batman with white eyes is part of a marketing decision: the toy action figure. I would hope that the reason for it pertains only the conscious decision of the character Morgan Freeman plays, Lucius Fox. The ethical portrayal of Fox is key to the bat sonar, not the cool 3d vision of Batman.

The Dark Knight has skipped practical approaches that were presented to us in the first film. This one presents the Batman Headquarters, an underground one floor slick and clean space where the Batmobile has no parking except the dead center and where other peripherals are just an accessory to the huge space with fluorescent lamps as a roof. In no way this one- dimensional "replacement" place, where a fireplace is installed, represents the technological edge of the bat cave. Also, I felt the spirit of a really mindless blockbuster summer movie when I first saw the Bat motorcycle: pulled out from an engineering-impossible nowhere and turning against a brick wall as if it the proper way to turn the thing.

Where is the "real" concept in the third act of the film when the Joker somehow got to put a bomb, and a cell phone might I add, inside the stomach of a human being without anyone witnessing it? And didn't the Nolans and Goyer learn of the effects of multi villains from Batman Returns and Spiderman 3? Sure Batman is more than a good guy and the Joker more than a bad guy but then there is the development of Maroni, whose role seems to be to get bullied and tortured by everybody. Regarding Two Face, I interpret that Nolan attempts to make the same bridge "Empire Strikes back" made to tie the first and plausible third movie of his adaptation, but the development of Two Face in the third act was way unnecessary. I argument this by saying that at the ending of Batman Begins, Commissioner Gordon states that The Joker is a criminal that had committed a robbery and double homicide (check your Batman Begins DVD) and already in the beginning of The Dark Knight, the Joker is an unknown.

Speaking of the Joker, he is the real reason to go see The Dark Knight but not the only. Many people have dwelled on his posture and unique tone of voice, which by comparison makes Batman's voice an annoying and nagging shout that dropped the fear effect it had on the first film. Heath Ledger satisfied my expectations and he steals the movie because I couldn't wait for him to be back on screen when he is off. It's speculative that we say he will win an Oscar but certain he should deserve his nomination.

By the end of the film, I felt that after the hospital scene where the Joker walks away, they should have called it a movie. The philosophical aspects presented afterwards are redundant and should have been left for interpretation. That shot of Ledger in the nurse suit is so remarkable and powerful that would have been appropriate for remembering him, if the intention was to keep the Joker alive for another movie. Lastly, I emphasized on the "real" concept because after all Batman, is the only superhero in comics that a human being can possibly be if it were for the money and the desire.

7.title: solid entertainment, verging on art in certain ways, but 9.6 rating is completely ridiculous
7.content:
First the good: Heath Ledger is mesmerizing, as is Gary Oldman. Many of the images are spellbinding. The basic mythology of Batman is fleshed out thoughtfully and well.

But 9.6? 3/4 of people giving it a 10/10? That's crazy. This just isn't a perfect movie, by any stretch. The plot is convoluted and sometimes muddy, and makes certain leaps that aren't well-earned. For instance, 1) Harvey Dent's transformation into Two-Face (supposedly based on his profound love for Rachel, which we hear about but don't really witness for most of the movie.) 2)Batman's decision to turn himself in: it's not clear whether all along he's calculated that Harvey will pretend to be Batman, or if he just adjusted his plans based on Harvey's move and Alfred's pep-talk. Also the action, and the cuts from scene to scene, are sometimes cluttered, repetitive, and confusing.

Hopefully the IMDb rating gods will step in and make sure The Dark Knight doesn't end up rated the #3 movie of all time, which would be a travesty. It's a worthy effort, but one of the best movies of all time? Please.

p.s. Too bad Heath Ledger is gone: a fantastic young actor.

7.title: The car is the star
7.content: I used to think that what Batman really needed was a racy chick. He must go green with envy every time he runs (or flies) into James Bond at a party. With the exception of Uma Thurman as Poison Ivy, Batman's female sidekicks form a long line of partly classy, but notoriously boring blondes: Kim Basinger, Michelle Pfeiffer, Nicole Kidman, Alicia Silverstone. Katie Holmes and Maggie Gyllenhaal may be minor improvements, but Bondgirls of the Andress-Auger-Bisset-Bach-Ekland-Janssen-Hatcher-Marceau-Richards variety are obviously entirely out of the Bat's reach. Maybe it's the suit. He may want to trade his Batgear for Brioni. Anyway, I used to think that what Batman really needed was a racy chick. Now I'm not so sure. With a car like that? He may not need other people anymore, at all. Small surprise Robin's part is past and gone. Other than the Batmobile, there are two stars in this movie. One is Eric Roberts, fashionably fattened and so tan it must hurt, in the part of smug mafia sleaze-ball Sally Maroni. The other is Heath Ledger as the Joker. It's a grateful part, but he does it justice. I must confess all the pre-release praise annoyed me, so I tried hard to not like his performance, but to no avail. He really is that good. My favorite scene is the one in which there seems to be something wrong with his remote as he tries to blow up Gotham General Hospital.

7.title: " You're Gonna Blackmail a man who pummels his enemies to death "
7.content: When Bob Kane created The Batman in the early 30's he had no idea he would become world wide popular. Yet here he is with a plethora of films, plays, books and action figures and many other venues are continuing to expand. Yet it is the newest film which had the attention of the audience today. The newest movie is called " The Dark Knight " and it stars Christian Bale as Bruce Wayne / Batman. When you sit and watch the movie, be prepared for a launching into action and dark drama. The ride of total action is what gives this offering it's appeal. From one explosive scene to the next, an audience member encounters nothing short of a 'run-on' roller-coaster ride movie. So much action is given, it becomes nearly impossible to say when the sequence begins and where the dramatic event ends. Heath Ledger, plays 'The Joker' a homicidal maniac who takes pleasure in saying, he doesn't want money or fame, just the knowledge that no one can understand why he is so crazy. Aaron Eckhart plays Harvey Dent / Two-Face, a good guy who slips into the dark side. Michael Caine, reprises his role as loyal Alfred Pennyworth. Gary Oldman as James Gordon and Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox return as stanch supporters of the Batman. If there was a single aspect which I would critique about this movie, I would point out that the facial make-up of the Joker, is to say the least, haphazard and sloppy. He looks like he put his make up on with a large wide paint brush. Other than that, the film is so loaded with action, it's difficult to ignore the length it will go to keep the audience's attention. Great Movie though. ****

7.title: Can one character make a good movie?
7.content:
I didn't think so before I went to the cinema to watch the dark knight. Since the Joker was Heath Ledgers last part before his tragic death I thought it was a hype just to honor him. I was wrong. Back in 1989 and Tim Burtons Batman I thought Jack Nicholson was excellent. I never expected anyone to beat his appearance as the insane criminal Joker. I was wrong. Ledger is outstanding and he alone saves what otherwise should be a pretty standard comic book superhero movie. Sure, the dark knight has one bad guy too much (Twoface) and the action sequences with the batpod is so-so. But when the joker enters the plot everything gets interesting in a twisted sort of way.

Bale does once again a good part as the dark knight as well as he did in Batman begins. Cain, Freeman is back as well. Gyllenhaal known from "the secretary" replaces Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes.

Now lets hope they are going to film Frank Millers "the dark knight returns"!

7.title: Good - but not great
7.content:
**spoiler alert** I watched this tonight and had very high expectations for it - I watched Batman Begins and expected more of the same. Unfortunately I cannot say this movie delivered (sorry, with all the hype I expected a lot more!).

I should start off by saying that I do think that Heath Ledger did a phenomenal job. As to who was the better Joker, Ledger or Jack Nicholson, all I can say is that they were played differently - Nicholson was great in a over-the-top comic book way and Ledger played it more menacingly "real" (what you would think a real serial killer might be like). Of the two, if I had to take my chances in a dark alley, I'd more likely survive if I met Nicholson's character.

I found the movie far too long and there are entire scenes that were unnecessary (Hong Kong, the long Dent transport/carnival truck chase...). Personally, I didn't mind Katie Holmes in the role of Rachel and I just didn't think replacing her with Maggie Gyllenhaal was worth the disruption to the character. For consistency, I thought it would have been better to keep Holmes. If they had to change who plays Rachel, which really is just a screen "fluff" role, it might as well have been stunning "fluff" (let's not forget Rachel attracts not just one powerful man, but two and her death drives one of them to turn to crime - takes a smart AND stunning woman to do that - sorry Maggie fans).

As for Christian Bale, I really liked him in Batman Begins and think he is great as Batman. He is quite possibly the best Batman to date, but his role in this one was mediocre at times. I found it laughable and annoying when he tried to disguise his voice and the lack of any real emotion when the love of his life died left me a bit baffled. I found it odd that he who supposedly grew up with Rachel was not an emotional wreck and Dent, who didn't know the real Rachel at all (hey she was supposedly in love with two men and he never clued in???) changed everything about himself and turned into a (not so believable) monster within hours of her death, even going to the extent of trying to murder a child to get revenge for her...

Aaron Eckhart, who I loved in Thank You for Smoking, was good but I felt his whole performance began to slide once he had to start playing Two Faced. His anguish over Rachel's death was passable, but not totally believable and it should have been considering that was supposedly the catalyst for change. Quite possibly the whole Rachel role could have been removed altogether from the film and they could have used another causal event - why not stick to the original acid/bad guy thing or if they had to, why not use something even more traumatic and character changing, like killing off his wife (Rachel?)/kids? Would have been more believable. I don't know if introducing two evil characters in one film was even necessary. He could have been introduced here and explored more fully in another movie, at least it would have kept this one shorter! I loved Michael Caine as Alfred and thought he suited the role superbly and I also thought Morgan Freeman was great. Neither really had big roles in this film.

Even though I have a whole lot to criticize, the special effects were superb and overall the movie was well acted, especially by Ledger. Definitely worth going to watch, but come on people, it is not the best movie ever and personally I do not think it is the best Batman!

7.title: Why So Overrated?
7.content: This is a great movie. Just great. There are some problems though, and it doesn't deserve a 9/10 and sure doesn't deserve to be the 4th best movie ever made! Of course IMDb's top 250 isn't too accurate and is different then other people's opinions. So basically, this movie should probably get a 7.5 or 8 but I believe it's too overrated in IMDb and by most people. It isn't the best movie ever made, not even on the top 10. The action scenes are good and they have pretty good actors. The voice acting of Bat man is awkward and he is kind of a side kick in the movie; a side character. I know the movie is called "The Dark Knight", not Batman, but it's a sequel to Batman. Great movie, but overrated. That's all I'll say

7.title: Dark Knight-Joker and Others Go Wild ***
7.content:
The film is good but is very much over-rated. The Daily News rated this movie *****. It is rather a *** as I shall try to explain.

The acting is top-notch, especially Heath Ledger as the Joker and Aaron Eckhart, amazingly good as Harvey Dent, D.A.

This is one film that is rare since good does not triumph over evil. Dent's transformation is magnificently realized. It just shows us what situations can lead someone so pious to go so wrong.

The film is action packed. The special effects are marvelously arranged.

As far as the Oscars for this year go, an argument can be made that Ledger's performance should be in the supporting category as well as Eckhart. Gary Oldham,as Gordon, should also be in the running for a supporting Oscar as well as Maggie Gyllenhaal, who has really shown a depth of maturity here in a breakout performance.

My lone argument with this film is the last-half hour. Once the Gyllenhaal character is killed off, the film does go a bit down-hill. It becomes confusing at this point. Confusion we don't need as we wish to study the change in dimension depicted by Dent. That being said, the picture is one of a rare quality. A thin line is drawn between good and evil here and we wonder where we can go from here as the credits roll.

7.title: great film ,but get rid of Bale!!!

7.title: The image mirrors life...
7.content:
It's a too close approximation to life... it's very dark, and shows how easily one can become corrupted, regardless of the good that they do in this world. The League of Shadows had a point. And the Joker was right on many occasions... not the in the "stories" he told, but in how humanity is easy to control. He burned the money because he saw no value. I was a bit disappointed. The Joker represented futility and apathy. Two-Face represented the corruption in us all. Batman represented the fear in which we must all face in life. 10 years ago, I thought that this movie would have been good. But as I see life in it's whimsical evils... the movie was no more than an overly-expressive image of life. In terms of artistic prowess and ingenuity, it's an excellent movie. But in terms of the entertainment experience... it was depressing.

It was balance... either side of the balance was far too extreme. This is what the League of Shadows was trying to reset. Bringing Gotham back to neutrality and order. But, when you have two extreme opposites opposing each other, you create chaos. The Joker wanted it this way. It entertained him. The harder Batman fought to bring justice, the harder the Joker came back with more evil schemes. It didn't phase him at all to get punched or hit or fall down to his impending doom. Chaos was the Joker.

Batman's symbol... the mask. It's as if he's hiding behind something. But it wasn't that. The symbol, the one thing that was incorruptible... the moment Batman let his humanity out, it hurt him.

7.title: Overrated
7.content: Bloated, overly-long, too many sub plots. Still a really good movie but hold back on the accolades people

7.title: Many actions, good story and great selection of characters

Batman, even as super hero, is not always in top situation. we can see difficulties in this movie, where he is weaker than his enemies. I find the adaptation of the initial story is successful. 7.title: Joker??? I think not
7.content:
Having grown up watching Bill Dozier's TV homage to the comic book hero, maybe I went into this with an unfair expectation of the principal villain in TDK. I wasn't looking for the howling Cesar Romero necessarily, but there was nothing even remotely wry about this film's Joker. Are we to believe this character is named the Joker simply because of the angle of his facial scars? I guess that might be enough for some, but I wanted the Joker to wield a devilish sense of humor as part of his arsenal of terror. Heath Ledger delivers a terrific psychopath, but a Joker he's not.

Relationships seemed amiss in TDK. Where was the genuine if frequently sarcastic warmth shared between Alfred and Bruce in Batman Begins? Did anyone really believe there was much passion between Rachel and Bruce in this version, despite a much better performance from Gyllenhaal than Holmes? Even the wonderful Morgan Freeman had little to do in TDK, other than monitor the preposterous-even-by-comic-book-cinema-standards wall of cell phone data from what... 30-million Gothamites? Yeah. That could work. Lt./Commish Gordon's interplay with Batman misses the mark as well, and I felt the Gordon family anguish was forced.

I've read some unflattering comments about Bale's performance. For me, he wasn't given much material with which to work. In Batman Begins, his character has far more dynamic range. TDK further quashes Bale's work by over-graveling his Batman voice to the point that only constipated anger can be effectively emoted.

At least Eckhart and Gyllenhaal were given some latitude to develop their characters, though I never fully surrendered my heart to their oft-stated love.

Complaints aside, for theater thrills TDK brings it home... outstanding production design, great effects, superb sound, and another great collaborative effort between JNH and Zimmer on the soundtrack.

7.title: Should have been called "The White Knight"
7.content:
As I sat through this movie I thought that the Joker was the real star in this film. Heath Ledger was brilliant, far better than Jack Nicholson and all others. The movie comes to life every time he appears on screen. I do think Christian Bale is the best Batman, but what's with his voice? I was also glad to see Gary Oldman get a bigger role. Michael Caine as always was low-key and does his usual good work, as does Morgan Freeman. Having those reliable actors adds to the film. I wish they had a bigger role in this film. Instead they give a larger role to actor Aaron Eckhart as Harvey Dent, and this is where I think the movie starts to suck.

I can't believe this is being called the movie of the year. But everyone I talked to thought it was so great. So my opinion doesn't reflect the majority. But the popcorn was better than I have had in the past. Would I see it again? No.

Time for the real review because everyone of the reviews above is unrealistic.

The Movie is a lot of fun to watch. Heath Ledger's Joker !!!

7.title: A hodge-podge of mainstream actors competing for each scene.
7.content:
Don't get me wrong, this movie is above average. But not in my top 10 list. I am going to predict, as time goes on, this movie will slowly drop down to maybe in 30th place in the IMDb ranking.

First off, I am impressed with all the details that Dark Knight embedded me. I appreciate the well developed characters of Joker, Two-Face, Alfred, Rachel, Commissioner Gordon and Lucius. All the actors are stunning in their performances. Christian Bale was good as Bruce Wayne, but whenever he turned into Batman, it's that same annoying raspy voice that comes from him. Half the time, I just wish Batman would stop talking. Heath Ledger, rest his soul, did a good job at reinventing Joker and his performance is Oscar worthy but it wasn't the real Joker. But he should have been a different character. Joker was a more comical giddy trickster, not a depressive washed up alcoholic version. I liked Aaron Eckhart's portrayal of Two-Face, it was right on the money.

Maybe I am applying my personal taste in movies whenever I write about them. I am just not a big fan of comic book movies though I did like Batman Begins. The major flaw of this movie was that it just felt a little too much to take in one sitting. There is such thing as overabundance in movie making. The running time felt a little too long for my attention span, it had that same effect on me like Transformers did. Dark Knight was that temporary rush I had at the beginning up until the Two Face scenario, but I just started getting a headache afterwards. The fact that I know that in every Comic hero movie, the good guy wins and the bad guy loses or dies. It's inevitable and by knowing this, I often wished that this movie would be over soon while sitting 3 quarters of the way.

Nonetheless I still give props to this movie for being well produced and took a shot at human psychology on what people would really do. There is a notable scene which the two boats were forced to make a life or death decision. I guess direction wanted us to see that the city of Gotham has good people despite of the high crime rate.

7/10, I'll watch again on DVD knowing I can pause and take a breather.
