8.title: The last laugh
8.content:
An engaging and psychologically rewarding character study that paints the word 'dichotomy' across the screen in blood red lipstick and forces you to reflect on it over two and half bleak but for the most part well judged hours. Why so serious? Because Joel Schumacher is always watching that's why.

If characterisation is the yardstick, The Dark Knight is the most dense and finely drawn Batman movie yet made - interweaving the motivations and moral complications of its cast with a magician's slight of hand and a calculating intelligence. The ambiguities thrown up by the plot aren't subtle by any means but that it feels less signposted than we've come to expect in comic book fare is attributable to Nolan's deft handling of the material and his refusal to over egg the pudding with laden dialogue or simplistic conceptions of good and evil.

As entertainment it fares less well. One of the sublime pleasures of Tim Burton's 1989 Batman movie was your total immersion in a hyperreal Gothic dystopia, augmented with a score that perfectly partnered the aesthetic.

Nolan's Batpics have one dirty foot in the real world making them less cartoons than Film Noirs with costumes but there are times during this 150 minutes when the lack of stylized backdrop or sweeping score make it a relatively still and cold experience.

Nolan takes his directorial cues from the likes of Johnathan Demme and Michael Mann but doesn't frame action or build suspense with their assured touch. That isn't to say that TDK isn't involving but there's a workmanlike quality to some of the spectacle here and nothing to wrongfoot the audience with the same verve as say Silence of the Lambs did 20 years ago.

An occasionally elliptical narrative and confused framing in fight scenes sometimes suggests that Nolan's realisation of his script was more sure footed than his choices in the editing suite but where he scores major hits is in his handling of tone and the drawing out of the comic book's more challenging themes. This is a Batman movie that has been futureproofed in being aimed at Adults and consequently it should have a long and respected self-life when the likes of Spider-man are filling space on charity shop shelves marked up for 75 pence.

One disappointment with this Batflick, particularly given the prominence he was afforded in 'Begins' is that Christian Bale gets somewhat lost amongst a large cast with character trajectories more integral to the plot. The deceased Heath Ledger is very good, giving a creepy, dread soaked performance. He's the bastard child of Seth Brundle in mid-transformation and Hannibal Lecter with all the discomfort that implies while Aaron Eckhart's Harvey Dent/Two Face is less involving but well handled and performs a public service in permanently wiping all memory of Tommy Lee Jones horrific turn in Batman Forever. God Bless you Aaron.

Ultimately its easier to admire than to love but TDK is superior, involving fare which talks up to it's audience without ever really getting their pulse racing. The storytelling values displayed bode well for the series but if this can married with a little more care in constructing setpieces and please please please a proper score rather than this ambient mood music (two composers and not a single, memorable note), the next film might be a real treasure. As it stands this is just very good but with the likes of Michael Bay forever circling I'll take that with thanks.

8.title: Go see it!!!
8.content:
I have always been a sceptic as far as films based on comic books go - some up and coming (or established and lazy) director comes along, has "a vision" and summarily ruins it for everyone and anyone with the audacity not to share it.

But not Mr Nolan.

This film is everything an action film should be and everything a Batman film should be. Highly recommended, it doesn't skimp on special effects nor compromise on story. The casting, on the whole, was inspired (R.I.P Mr Ledger). There may be a few die-hards out there who will disagree but on the whole, Dark Knight shows Batman as he should be and I think the portrayal of the people around him is great because lets face it, people are flawed.

In conclusion, well executed, cinematography is amazing and the gadgets! Oh the gadgets! Satisfactory for any geek worth his salt! Well worth paying to see (and there's not many films you can say that about anymore).

Enjoy (^_^)

8.title: In 'The Dark Knight', Christopher Nolan finds light among the shadows
8.content:
In his successful reboot of the Batman franchise, Christopher Nolan has accomplished an admirable feat: he has taken a scorned, ridiculed series and transformed it into a near-masterpiece of modern crime noir that feels frighteningly close to home. Since its widely publicized release in July 2008, The Dark Knight has almost universally become known as the best adaptation of a superhero comic book in history, and while the film is not by all means perfect, this status is hard to debate.

From the very first opening shot of Gotham City, Nolan enthralls his audience in the movie. Especially when viewed in IMAX, one cannot help but gape with awe at the film's spectacular visuals, from the opening bank robbery - an ingenious imitation of the famous heist in Michael Mann's 1995 crime drama Heat - to the thrilling Batpod chase scene (enhanced by the fact that, like most of the film's special effects, the flipped truck was real, not CGI). The masterful cinematography helps generate a bleak, murky atmosphere that not only increases the suspense, but also reflects the ambiguous principles of the movie's protagonist. Almost instantly, it becomes clear that The Dark Knight is not just another mindless action blockbuster; in actuality, it is more of a crime drama, a gritty meditation on corruption, honor and morality. Ultimately, it is not cheap explosions and elaborate action set pieces that captivate the viewer, but instead the film's underlying themes and, above all, the epic battle of wills between Christian Bale's Batman and Heath Ledger's Joker.

And it cannot be denied that this eternal struggle is arguably one of the most engrossing conflicts presented in recent cinema. Christian Bale imbues his iconic antihero with a sense of grim, pensive dignity, making the audience alternately admire his courageous determination and abhor his ruthless ambition. Unlike most superheroes, Batman feels less like a glorified deity and more like a complex, three-dimensional human being. Screenwriters Christopher and Jonathan Nolan must be commended for effectively breathing life into this character that could easily have become little more than a caricature, providing him with secrets, desires, hopes, motivations and fears, all the while maintaining his mysterious temperament. On the flip side, Heath Ledger's Joker has quickly evolved into one of the most famed screen villains of all-time along with the likes of Anthony Hopkins's Hannibal Lecter and James Earl Jones's Darth Vader. Ledger's performance is nothing short of superlative. The young, amiable actor - otherwise known mostly for his heartrending portrayal of the forlorn cowboy Ennis Del Mar in 2005's Brokeback Mountain - completely vanishes behind the Joker's creepy, haphazard mask of make-up, expertly crafting a character that is both sinister and haunting, a twisted, merciless psychopath who somehow manages to feel believable and down-to-earth. The shadow of Heath Ledger's tragic, untimely death lingers throughout, adding an eerily poignant layer to his performance, yet it never overwhelms the malicious, tormented persona he has created. Perhaps more than anything else, the passionate, tumultuous friction between Christian Bale and Heath Ledger - epitomized in the now-famous interrogation scene - helped elevate The Dark Knight above the normal confines of its genre and into the realm of classic cinema.

The rest of the cast does a bravura job of supporting the two leads. Most notable is Aaron Eckhart, who is equally convincing as the noble, saintly D.A. Harvey Dent and as the bitter, anguished Two-Face; he provides a steady, levelheaded foil to rival Christian Bale's haughty Bruce Wayne. In addition, Gary Oldman lends an emotional nuance to James Gordon not evident in the previous installment, and Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman are always reliable as Alfred the butler and Lucius Fox, respectively. The only questionable performance comes from Maggie Gyllenhaal as the idealistic Rachel Dawes. Her chemistry with Christian Bale does not match the restrained tenderness that Bale shared with Katie Holmes in Batman Begins, and her matter-of-fact attitude does not seem to suit her more quixotic character. Still, Gyllenhaal makes an honest effort and over time, the viewer comes to appreciate the candid prudence she brings to the screen.

Much of The Dark Knight revolves around the Freudian idea that evil resides within the heart of all humans. While in Batman Begins, Bruce Wayne/Batman was portrayed mostly as an honorable guardian of integrity, this time, he is constantly characterized as an obsessive, even deranged vigilante. The film-makers take care to emphasize the thin line between defender and criminal that Batman treads so closely, utilizing dark lighting and a dynamic score, mostly forsaking the heroic theme melody in favor of a more chilling arrangement. Also, many people have noticed that The Dark Knight focuses much more on Batman as opposed to Bruce Wayne. While the fact that he spends a great deal of his screen time behind a mask could easily detract from Christian Bale's performance or diminish his character's personality, this oddly clever move shows how Bruce Wayne himself is slowly being consumed by his alter ego, evolving into a faceless, coldblooded icon, his energy and life bent toward fulfilling a single unattainable goal: to rid Gotham of evil. At some point or another, each character is forced to flirt with the gray area between right and wrong, and the audience watches as one by one, they find either salvation or oblivion.

Remarkably, however, Christopher Nolan manages to stop the film from becoming nothing more than a cynical diatribe on the flaws of humanity. Sparks of humor are sprinkled throughout the movie, such as the time when Bruce Wayne and Harvey Dent dine together or the many wry conversations between Bruce and Alfred, to contrast the otherwise relentless solemnity. In the end, the audience emerges from the gloom and sorrow to discover hope - the fervent belief in man's ability to improve himself and the world around him - because above all, The Dark Knight is a movie about redemption and the promise of rebirth after devastation.

8.title: Overrated but good.
8.content:
I'm shocked how high "The Dark Knight" has been rated on this site, currently at #1 with a 9.5 rating. It must come down. But what if it doesn't? Below is my Onion-esque take as one future possibility:

Warner Brothers Announces: No More New Movies

Hollywood, CA -- Warner Brothers announced today they will not be making new movies, and those that are currently in production are going to be shut down. As CEO Barry M. Meyer explains, "What's the point in making new movies? 'The Dark Knight' is a perfect picture that can't be topped, so we're simply going to re-release it at regular intervals and save a bundle on production costs." Other studios expect to follow suit after "The Dark Knight" overtook the number one spot on IMDb.com's top 250 Films List within a record-breaking four days after its release, usurping longtime #1 film, "The Godfather." Talk has already begun between Warner Brothers and rival studios to license out distribution rights to "The Dark Knight" so that competing studios can also stop producing new films and simply re-release "The Dark Knight." As Steven Spielberg noted, "It makes total sense. 'The Dark Knight' has been instantly recognized by the public as the pinnacle of movie making, far surpassing the critical acclaim of films such as 'Casablanca,' 'Lawrence of Arabia,' 'Star Wars,' and even 'Schindler's List,' so there's little incentive for studios and filmmakers to move forward on product that we know beforehand will be vastly inferior." Rumors that the major broadcast and cable networks are trying to obtain the rights to replace all of their current programming with 24/7 showings of "The Dark Knight" have not yet been confirmed.

8.title: We Take It So Serious!
8.content:

Burton successfully provides a new acceptable point of view for thiz kind of genre. The tone is dark, mysterious, and full of believable characters and environments.

8.title: Good movie but feel a little let down
8.content:
I guess it was my own fault. I really, REALLY wanted this movie to blow my socks off, but after all the hype, it really didn't. I came away knowing I'd seen something good, but best movie ever? Come on, Batman Begins was on a par with this. And as for saying it's better than The Godfather. Please.

For me the movie was a little too long. I don't mind long films but this didn't keep me on the edge of my seat.

Much is made of Heath Ledger's performance and he does an excellent job, but I just worry that much of the clamour for this film is related to his untimely death rather than the actual content of the film.

Don't get me wrong, there are some fantastic bits in this movie and all the actors put in solid performances, just as a whole this didn't have enough of a wow factor after all the reviews I'd read on here and elsewhere.

Still give it a benefit of the doubt 8 though. 7.5 would be a more realistic mark for me.

8.title: Great Batman Finally
8.content:
Finally we get to watch a Batman the way it was meant to be. This film has an amazing script and amazing special effects. Although, Christian Bale while in his Batman suit, has an extremely deep voice. Almost to the point that you cannot understand what he is saying.

Ledger plays the Joker in the dark way that I always envisioned him. This was by far the best performance of his career.

This movie was the only Batman that I personally enjoyed watching.

I don't think this is the 4th greatest movie ever, but it was an amazing movie. Great special effects, clever script, good actors, this movie almost convinced me to be a DC comic fan.

8.title: A good film but not the best
8.content:
I think the Dark Knight is a good film but not the greatest film ever made. It has some good action scenes and the stunts are amazing but the film it is also over long, the story and dialogue droops and maybe the film could have lost action sequences. The acting is good all round. I think Heath Ledger was very clever in the way he performed the Joker. Bale is great when he is Bruce Wayne but when he becomes batman his performance becomes a bit force, I think I probably find the way he talks when he is batman a bit over the top. For me my favourite performance and the hardest to pull off by far was Aaron Eckhart who was great in the role of Harvey Dent and Two Face.

The cinematography is very good and most of the time the editing worked. I was not a huge fan of the score in the original film and I can't really say that I found it that great this time.

Over all I think that Christopher Nolan has done a good job with the sequel with some great touches. The film isn't perfect but is a general success.

8.title: Better than the first, Heath Ledger performance
8.content:
Everybody knows about Heath Ledger's death and how it affected other movies, including this one.

But I must say that when I watched this film, I wasn't thinking about that, I had my mind focused on the film, performances and story. And I have to say, that it turned out better than I had expected, this is a definite improvement over Batman Begins and I lot more interesting. Ledger's performance in this film was incredible, his take on the Joker cannot be compared to previous Joker incarnations because it is unique and very intense.

There were a couple of things on this film that I didn't quite get and maybe were a little loose, but overall, this film great in action, drama and probably the best tribute to Ledger.

8.title: I can't keep silent on this one
8.content:
Hi there.

I'm usually a silent IMDb viewer. I log on and read the positive and negative comments about films to get an objective feel for the film . I don't usually respond or comment on films as I feel there are enough people throwing their opinions around. After reading the 'hated it' reviews for this film i have to get a few things off my chest. Please take what I'm about to say as relevant to every film, as well as this one.

First my thoughts on the film:

The Dark Knight was a great film. I say this- and I stress the difference here- not only because I really enjoyed it, but also because it was very well made. As a studier of film and a potential maker (fingers crossed) it is hard not to sit in the cinema and pull a film apart. The great thing is you know you really like a film when you are so engrossed in the story that this doesn't happen.

The script was great. Definitely the backbone of the two films. The character development of Batman extended far beyond the other films as it delved deep into the consequences of his actions and their effects on his alter-ego and the people he loves. The Joker's character was also well developed despite there being no back story to him, apart from some minor references to his father. The randomness of his character makes him more creepy, less understandable and very effective which is the essence of his character, "Do I look like a guy with a plan?" This in turn makes him a more formidable opponent for Batman than we've seen in the past and therefore makes the darkness of the film feel greater.

The best thing about The Dark Knight and its predecessor is that they strive for realism as much as possible for a super-hero film. The visuals are great as the shots flow seamlessly and bring the action forward to make Batman, the Joker and the battles more intense.

The performances are as solid as Batman Begins thanks to the great supporting cast. They are all believable characters in an imagined world, especially the Joker. Heath embodies the character to perfection; his laugh, his expressions, his walk, everything down to little idiosyncrasies like his sense of humor and the way he licks his lips. It is the attention to detail, the subtleties of character that make this performance memorable. The Joker is pure menace with homicidal charm and sense of humor to match.

The Oscar debate for Heath is unfortunate given the circumstances. Hopefully people will base their opinion/ nomination on his performance, not because it's his last.

On another note:

It is frustrating to see people rating films poorly just because they don't want it to be at the top of the all-time-greats list, just as it is annoying that the opposite occurs. This seems to have happened frequently for the Dark Knight. The people that have done this obviously don't realize that the scores for each film are averaged over time and according to dedicated reviews for the site. Films are like a good wine... I don't drink it, but everyone knows the cliché I'm getting at.

The negative comments for this film (read the 'hated it' section) amount to just over 1400 compared to over 124000 in total -so far- and most of these lack insight or objectivity. They spout phrases of condemnation for the film, yet provide no evidence to support their claims. for example, one critique said:

..."So why, therefore, did this movie suck? Because it was created more for shock value than for actual entertainment."

Were they referring to the violence committed in some scenes by the joker? Or where they considering to something else? Apparently they haven't considered anything because looking at this comment we can see there is nothing constructive about their criticism; no trail of thought to follow and respect. This appears to be because they don't show any respect for the opinions of others, thinking in terms of right and wrong rather than simply disagreeing. Check this comment out:

"C'mon folks, you call this a masterpiece? The greatest movie of all-time? Seriously, I thought people had better tastes than this. The main reason why people went to see it is because it was Heath Ledger's last performance."

How completely arrogant to speak as though you know the minds and motivations the millions who went to see the film. I was looking forward to this film long before Heath passed and I would've been at it's first screening regardless.

I have written this, not because I take so much notice of poor reviewers that it offends me, but because it's sad to think that someone else might and make a judgment based on a badly formed opinion. However, I feel I have been slightly biased so it is important to note that it is not only the negative reviews that do this but also the positive ones.

The thing that makes this site great is that you can come on and get some really constructive and objective thought happening. The reviews that I am referring to, both positive and negative ones, put this in jeopardy and make IMDb more like a blogspot for over opinionated, self-important film buff wannabes. If you have an opinion express it without fear of any intelligent bias- Being brilliant is not a requirement- just do it constructively and objectively, not like a pi@#ed-off adolescent who hates everything for the sake of hating it.

Thanks for reading my rant.

Cheers

8.title: Batman Begins was better than this but still worth watching
8.content:
This sequel didn't achieve the same rating I gave for the first Batman Begins. The movie is in my opinion too long but still a must see. One or two parts could have been cut easily here. I mean all the countdown to combat Joker takes too much time and loses definitely the dynamic. The many action scenes or car chases were okay so far. I missed the funny situations as in Batman Begins except the only one with Joker dressed as a nurse. Then the color wasn't so clear as in the last one. Joker played by Heath Ledger and Christian Bale as Batman delivered another convincing performance as all the rest of actors here. Christian Bale has got one of my favorite actor of nowadays. Director Christopher Nolan created another masterpiece. My family enjoyed it and the vote is 8/10.

If you are a fan of Bale don't miss Prestige.

8.title: Excellent. But Not The Best Movie Of All Time....
8.content:
Christopher Nolan's dark masterpiece is clearly one of the highlights of Hollywood's 2008.

We all know why we love it; the spectacular action, the seminal ensemble & the hype.

But really...the No. 1 film of all time? The film is at least 15 minutes too long, it's saturated with so many themes and morals that it gets lost. Don't get me wrong, it's spectacular but it's not perfect.

Please stop voting ''10/10'' just because Heath Ledger gives a sublime performance. Think about it, and hopefully in a few months it will rest at about no. 150 where it belongs.

8.title: The best Batman movie too date...until next one--hopefully,
8.content:
I saw this flick twice in the theaters and managed to snag an early copy of the DVD last Thursday. Since then, I have watched the film four times and have yet to grow sick of it. So, where do I begin with a review of the Dark Knight? There really isn't anyway I could describe how good this movie is that hasn't already been stated 10,000 times. So this is why I'm going to take a different route and vent a little over four minor snags I noticed with repeated viewings of this stellar production.

I've been following Christian Bales' career since American Psycho, and I knew he would be the perfect Batman once I saw him in 2002's Equilibrium. However, there is a problemhis Batman voice. Towards the end of the film, when Batman has the Joker trussed up and ready to go, the dialogue was laughable. The Joker's voice, as provided by Heath Ledger, was different, yet cool and authentic. Batman's voice, as provided by Bale, felt strained and absurdalmost too the point of comedy. Maybe Bale should take a cue from veteran voice actor Kevin Conroy, who has voiced Batman/Bruce Wayne for sixteen years. Bruce Wayne's voice should be upbeat, perky, and conversant. However, when he is alone, talking shop with either Alfred or Lucius, or in costume, his voice should be lower, driving, and powerful. Batman doesn't scream at people, because he's the best at what he does and is fully aware of this. He simply tells folks the way it's going to be, and they have no choice in the matter but to comply or suffer.

In Batman Begins, the fight scenes were hard too make out. You could see a fist there, a foot here, but I was never able to discern more than that. The Dark Knight rectified this and has much steadier and greatly appreciated camera work for the fight scenes. However, after seeing it multiple times on DVD, Batman's fighting style is all wrong. He comes off like a blunt instrument that depends too heavily on his suit and on the fact that no one is bigger or physically stronger than he is. In short, this Batman possesses none of the precision, speed, or agility his four color counterpart does. Bruce Wayne is supposed to be a peak level, multi disciplined martial artistthink Chuck Norris crossed with Frank Dux. This is a character that has no problem snap kicking one guy in the chest, while elbowing another guy in the jaw. The Keysi fighting method, while distinctive, holds the flow of combat back by limiting his range of motion. In a future film, I'd very much like to see an agile and fast on his feet Dark Knight who just cannot be touched in a fight.

But, standing in the way of this is the costume he wears. More so than any other actor to portray the character thus far, Christian Bale's physique is dead on for Bruce Wayne's. Despite this, he's kept in a suit that seriously hinders his mobility. I like how this film acknowledged the shortcomings of the first costume, but the second one doesn't seem to be all too much of an improvement. Since Wayne is a billionaire, can't he afford a more streamlined disguise that has Kevlar sewn right into the material, instead of relying so heavily on armor? Yeah, he could still have the armor over his chest, his forearms, and his shins, but that should pretty much be it. Since the police are now going to be on Batman's butt 24/7, it only makes sense for him, in a future film, to adapt a lighter and more flexible suit of arms to move around in.

Finally, there is the score. I remember Danny Elfman's score for both Batman (1989) and Batman Returns (1992). His themes for Batman, the Joker, the Penguin, and Catwoman are all so distinctive that, to this day, if I hear them on the tube, I know what movie it is without having to see or hear anything else. That being said, this score is woefully unremarkable. The only track that comes close to competing against any of Elfman's is "Like a Dog Chasing Cars". Warner Bros. knows this. That is why this one track is used to advertise the DVD and is also looped over the main menu. The rest of the tracks, literally, aren't worth mentioning. Never mind the fact that, two movies in, we still don't have a defining theme for the title character. This needs to be changed, especially if the studio insists on making such a big deal over the soundtrack. Hey, maybe one composer is better than two? Then again, maybe both Zimmer and Howard need to go so that another composer can be brought in who will hopefully make some real headway with this powerful medium that can either heighten or trash a scene.

Besides these four issues, the Dark Knight is highly watchable. The action is compelling. The acting, all across the board, is superb. The cinematography allows you to take in far more of this interpretation of Gotham City and it's nocturnal guardian than the previous effort. The writing is tight, moving, dark, and will make you forget all about the two and a half hour run time. I say buy the DVD, turn the lights off, kick your feet up, and prepare to lose 154 minutes of your life over and over.

8.title: Overrated
8.content:
Let's be real - this is a GREAT action movie, i'd surely put it in the top 10 action movies of all time, the acting is superb, photography is outstanding and it has a great story - but honestly i think this title has received too much hype after Ledger's death. I'll say it again:great action movie, great movie overall, but IMHO it does not deserve to be the nr.1 movie in all cinema history. It lacks the depth of a movie like the Godfather or the Shawshank Redemption; Batman is a great fictional character but i still rank it behind a story like the Lord of the rings; nor it puts you on an emotional roller-coaster like Schindler's List or New Cinema Paradiso; as a police movie i still prefer The Departed or The Usual Suspects; also i didn't get the overall feeling i got from movies like The Sixth Sense or Crash.

8.5 out of 10

8.title: They better not make another movie with the Joker...
8.content:
...because I won't see it unless Heath Ledger plays him again (which might be difficult).

I did like the movie a lot, but for me, Heath Ledger playing the Joker is what set the movie apart from other action flicks. Christian Bale definitely plays Batman well, and the other acting in the movie was not disappointing. The special effects and intense action sequences were obviously spectacular, but I've got to say that there are other movies that have done it better.

For me, the villain in the story is what makes it or breaks it, and I think Heath should definitely get at LEAST and Oscar nomination for this. I can't think of any other acting performance by a male that I've liked better this year. The Joker was extremely well played, and his grotesque appearance (no prosthetics like Jack had) only heightened the excellence of the character in this movie. He made me laugh (dark humor, mind you) and made me realize that there are truly no limits to the art of villainy.

8.title: (K)night and the city...
8.content:
Having just watched for the first time "Batman Begins" (guess who got the double DVD set for Christmas!), I was keenly anticipating my viewing of the almost universally praised sequel, the record-breaking "The Dark Knight".

I was not disappointed. Unlike its predecessor, there's no "origin" sequence to slow down the "clobberin' time" (to mix up my comic-book metaphors!) and while I would recommend any comic-lovers to read the superb "Killing Joke" graphic novel which does just that, we're here presented with The Joker full-on from the outset, of course tying in with the continuity from the end of the first film.

Much has been said about the performance of the late Heath Ledger in the Clown of Crime role and I was naturally curious to see if it lived up to the hype. Again, I have to say, believe it. This is a truly superb performance, endowing what is after all a comic-book creation with psychological and psychopathic depths. While not conforming physically to the idealised image of The Joker as painted up beanpole in a purple dress-coat, Ledger's commitment to the role knocks aside any reservations on that score. You almost believe that the scars which grotesquely extend his manic grin are real (a brilliant attribute which I never picked up from the comics), so deep does he reach into the role.

Almost as good is Aaron Eckhart as nemesis number two on show, namely Harvey Dent D.A. who metamorphoses into the twisted "Two-Face". His ghastly fate is set-up with a number of premonitory phrases if you listen closely enough to the soundtrack and as well as sporting the best make-up effect in the whole film, Eckhart too makes the pulp villain into something believable.

This is where the film is most successful, with its concentration on characterisation heightened sufficiently above the norm against a similarly exaggerated, but still grounded in reality, cityscape which any urban dweller can imagine all too easily. The duality of pretty much all the characters is brought to the forefront, particularly the central premise that the Batman and Joker justify each other's existence which is why the half-way house character of Two-Face alongside them (in the previous Batman series he was paired off with "The Riddler"), is so right with all the maxims about two sides of the one coin etc absolutely manifest, particularly the celebrated scene where Batman indulges in straightforward interrogation brutality as he's brought to the edge of his reason that The Joker voluntarily and Dent, involuntarily actually cross.

Which brings me to The Batman, almost third-string in his own movie. Perhaps it's just that old song about the devil having all the best tunes but certainly while a complex character in his own right, Batman here pales in significance beside The Joker and Two-Face and seems in fact to get roughly the same screen-time to almost tacitly acknowledge this fact.

Onto other facets of the film and praise must also go the cinematographers, stunt organisers, special effects technicians and Messrs Zimmer and Newton Howard's atmospheric soundtrack. The only debits for me were the casting of Maggie Gylenhaal as the new Rachel Dawes. I actually quite liked Katie Holmes in "Batman Begins" and found the less glamorous Gylenhaal too jarringly different in the part. Continuity counts for a lot in a series like this, less so oddly enough for the costumed characters than the flesh and blood everyday parts and I found her performance wanting.

Also the plot-dense narrative lost me from time to time and I really just didn't get what The Joker was planning with the ferries' stand-off at the conclusion. With a bit of imagination, I'm sure the writers could have given us a big, certainly more memorable three-way confrontation between the main protagonists, say, at Arkham.

So whither now for the franchise? The producers mustn't weaken the vision here by allowing key-players like Nolan or Bale to move on and the introduction of new characters from the comics (Robin? The Riddler? - arguably the two campest characters in Batman's cast) must be done sympathetically to what has gone before. This series is too good to stop now and shouldn't be allowed to deteriorate as the 80's first reinvention by Tim Burton was sadly allowed to. I caught the reference to cats which makes me think that Catwoman might take a bow next time. Whoever gets her part however will certainly be up against it as comparisons to Ledger's performance, at one stroke trashing the memory of Jack Nicholson, will require not only a similarly dramatic revision of the part but also a performance of similar dare and imagination.

Until then, I'll be there for the next one, same Bat time, same Bat - channel...

8.title: Great but 9.5 and 10? Na...
8.content:
I saw the movie today... The movie is Great, But I wonder did it really deserve 9.4 or 10 as some people are so excited to rate it with the later value... It has some realistic Action Sequences like there wasn't any music during that chase scene with great sound mixing and brings you the holly wood feel within... I would rate the entire chase scene were Joker chases Harvey a Grand 10.... But rest of it?? 7.5+ && 8.0-

8.title: A great but flawed masterpiece
8.content: I saw the movie with my wife and interestingly while she is the comic book buff, I thought it was a great movie and she hated it. When I asked her why, she felt the movie Batman was not true to the character of the comic book Batman. Her example was in the simultaneous capture of the DA and girlfriend. The comic Batman would have managed to somehow save both of them but in the movie, one dies and perhaps the other should have died. I attributed that to perhaps a more true-to-life situation of not being able to save everyone, every time, but her comments did make me rethink some of the movie. The parts I found unbelievable is how the Joker could manage to surreptitiously plant a ton of explosives not only throughout a major medical center but also in two large ferries. And I am the only one who thinks Gotham City should be New York, not Chicago? The other irritating thing was - at least in my theater - the music drowned out the dialog. I had a very hard time hearing critical parts of what the characters were saying. So, in summary, while it was a great movie and I recommend it highly, I also wish there could have been less explosions and less background music.

8.title: Nolan does it again
8.content:
After the brilliant " The Prestige " and a very good "Batman Begins", Nolan passes another test with "The Dark Knight" The film starts with a bank robbery by some people with clowns masks, who end up shooting each other. Gotham City is frightened by the first act of the Joker out of many. The joker will kill influential people until Batman shows up. And he does..

The film clocks in about 2,5 hours, but it feels like 90 minutes. This is the strength of the "Dark Knight". The story is strong, although there are some minor plot holes here and there, and some parts of the plot (the courtroom scene, and the mafia influence in general)are unnecessary complicated and overdone.

The acting is good, with Ledger stealing the show, because of his good performance, but also because Bale's role and dialog is fairly flat, so it is hard for him to stand out.

Overall a good summer blockbuster, which is terribly over-hyped, presumably because of the death of Ledger. Worth seeing!

8/10 (77/100)

8.title: Awesome movie---but Number 1 of all time?!?!
8.content: I loved this movie. It is by far the best superhero/comic book character movie ever. I just can't believe that it has surpassed Shawshank and The Godfather on here. My guess is that it's a lot of young kids who haven't even seen these movies. This movie doesn't even compare. When saying that it is the best movie of all time, it's hard to ignore that there isn't really an in-depth story line; it is a superhero movie after all. And all this hype of Heath Ledger winning an Oscar for this? It's sad to say but if he had not perished so young and tragically, it's hard to imagine this would be even a thought, albeit it has been a weak year for movies overall. And was anyone else annoyed by Christian Bale's voice change as Batman; it wasn't that pronounced in Batman Begins, which was awesome also, so why change it? That being said, what a great movie. Very unfortunate that Heath won't be around to be in the next one, because to be honest, I did not think that anyone could out do Jack as the Joker, but he did.

8.title: This IS NOT the Greatest Film Ever.
8.content:
The Dark Knight was the most hyped movie that I have ever gone to see. While I thought it was good, it was nowhere near the hyped that it received and I doubt any movie ever could be.

Basically a new villain is around, the Joker. Also a new district attourney named Harvey Dent is helping to end crime in Gotham. Batman also is beginning to have his image tainted and hopes that he will not be needed one day.

I once again liked the overall serious tone in this film. That helps to make the conflict seem more real and problamatic. It is great for these new Batman Films to have this tone and hopefully they stick with it.

Loved the new character of Harvey Dent. He is great both as Harvey Dent the District Attorney and later as Two Face the coin flipping killer.

I think Christian Bale is great as Batman once again. Bale is good at playing Batman and I look forward to seeing him in future films.

Heath Ledger plays the Joker. While an interesting performance and one that is memorable, I think that his performance is completely over rated due to his death. If he had not died I do not know how much credit he would have gotten or how much hype the film would have gotten. I do feel bad that he died, but this performance is not as great as people say and somewhat disturbing at times.

Scarecrow gets to show up for a little, which is interesting.

I think this film dragged at times. It seemed like there are too many things going on and stuff that should have been cut out.

Also Batman could have been in this film more. This film is somewhat similar to Spiderman 2 in that Spiderman is absent for much of the film as Batman is absent from this film for a while as well. But when Batman is on screen he is great. I really like Batman.

Also I hate the new actress that played Rachel. Why did they change actresses? Katie Holmes was way better and it would have helped if they had found an actress who LOOKED LIKE KATIE HOLMES AT LEAST! Idiots.

The action is pretty good. Batman gets to fight dogs, the Joker, and some thugs. Also the effects and music were phenomenal.

So I think this film was over hyped more than any film I have ever seen. It was very good, but not a masterpiece. Still, I recommend it.

8.title: Wow, I couldn't agree with edmundgrieg more
8.content: When I saw Batman Begins in IMAX back in June of 2005, the first thing I noticed immediately when the camera raced through the garden at Wayne Manor was how fast that scene had happened. And the entire movie moved at that pace. A lot of people's complaints about the first movie were the action scenes being edited too quickly, and the camera being too close in on the action. I felt like EVERY scene,even dialogue scenes, were edited too quickly. Basically, before a character can even get to the fourth word in a five word sentence, the movie already cuts to another shot of something. And basically 5 seconds maximum on that next shot, and five or so seconds on the next, and so on and so forth. The editing in these movies reminds me a lot of Dark City. Supremely, quickly edited. Great movie, but I saw NO one comment on that, the editing, and when I saw your post just now I just HAD to comment about it.

8.title: Solid but completely over-hyped
8.content: This is a solid movie folks, but terribly over-hyped so be ready for it. Excellent directing and a great cast. The one thing I will comment on right away is that the movie was at least 30 minutes too long and they kept putting in silly plot after silly plot with respect to the joker. Mr. Ledger's performance, while certainly solid, was not at all worthy of an Oscar. He had said that the role was so disturbing and troubling that it caused his insomnia, depression etc. If that is the case then he obviously had some serious emotional problems already, because the joker was downright tame from what I was expecting. Jack Nickolson offered up a much better version in 1989.

8.title: Two thumbs up!
8.content:
Wow! i saw movie after hearing about Heath Ledgers sad death, man i wish he was still alive, he stole the show completely, he rocked as the Joker, Christain Bale was great though he was almost pushed as a secondary actor behind Heath, Gary oldman became a bigger character and really stood out as Commissioner Gordon, Aaron Eckhart co-starred as Harvey Dent, he did great through the two hours that he was normal, than after he was turned into Two-Face it seemed as though he was partially out of body, i was so mad to see that they replaced Katie Holmes with Maggie Gyllenhaal, she did good as her own Rachel Dawes, but she just didn't match up to Katie Holmes' portrayal of Rachel. but still i thoroughly enjoy this film (mostly because of Heath Ledger) so i recommend this film to anyone who loved the predecessor.

I give this film 8/10 *'s.

8.title: One of the best productions ever - but not the greatest film
8.content:
I saw The Dark Knight at the IMAX. The first shot, as the camera zooms over the city scape and the whole audience gasped. The amazing visual effects, towering eight storeys around you, wowed us all as we set off on the roller-coaster ride through Gotham's darkest times.

That gasp from the audience really wasn't the last gasp either. The IMAX enhanced effects, Heath Ledger's JOKE, some pretty stunning direction and all round good acting made this one of the best productions I've ever seen. But when I saw this clinch the number one spot at IMDb, I worried for it.

No one could expect a DC Comics film not be American through and through. However, even the most hardened comic fan couldn't help but wince at the references to terrorism, the blatant advocacy of invading the privacy of citizens and torturing prisoners (though only when necessary, of course), and the amazing idea that the people will unite, through democracy, to defeat the evil that is chaos and replace it with the good that is conformity.

The corny lines are, generally, within the acceptable limit (you need some in a Batman film for goodness sake) and a plot would stand up to a fair amount of scrutiny, something few comic book films deliver. That said, the film constantly seems to be ending, then a new twist takes in forward. When it does end, we suffer the monologue summary that now seems compulsory in any blockbuster, presumably so that the increasing number of effect-seeking media-illiterates can still understand what the point of the past two hours was.

if, however, these comments are starting to give you a negative vibe, please stop reading. This film is good and should be seen, if nothing else for Ledger's Joker. The effects and the pace eclipse Batman Begins, rival Burton and, coupled with a storyline as dark as the original comics, this has got to be a contender for film of the year. Just not for all time.

8.title: superb
8.content:
I'm near speechless when it comes to describing this movie. Saw it opening weekend (regular sized screen as my local IMAX was sold out for DAYS.) And the pleasure to see the re release on IMAX (finally!)

The cinematography is astounding. Especially in IMAX). Nolan does an excellent job directing. The score is exquisite and powerful in supporting the actions and emotions. The CGI is kept to a minimum and supports the story and scenes instead of overpowering them. (Take a lesson Lucas!!!)

Bale is hands down the best Batman of the "Batman" franchise. He captures the emotions and conflicts of Bruce Wayne perfectly and that of his alter ego Batman. I'll be disappointed if they make another Batman movie in this series and start replacing Batmans. And no, the "growley" Batman voice didn't bother me.

Eckhart was a good choice for Gotham's white knight. He's convincing and easily able to make a believable transition from city hero to the bitter, disfigured twisted psyche required for Two Face.

The support cast as always is excellent. Freeman & Cain return, as does Oldman, who as always disappears into his role. Gyllenhaal is an awesome replacement for Katie Holmes. She gives the character of Rachel Dawes some dimension, emotion, and life, unlike Holmes's wooden, shallow portrayal.

And last but not least. Heath Ledger. There's not a word that exists that could adequately describe his performance as the Joker. Superb? Mind Blowing? Excellent? Chilling? Astounding? All these words don't even seem to measure up to level of performance that is given. As the Joker, he's frightening, psychotic, chaotic, twisted, evil, chilling. Ledger doesn't just play the Joker, he disappears into his character as "an agent of chaos." Ledger IS the joker. To say the least, I was absolutely blown away. As far as i'm concerned, there is nobody else even in that Oscar Cattegory. The void left behind by Ledger's tragic death is still felt, and will be for a long time to come. (Especially after viewing the Dark Knight.) Just Excellent. 10/10

8.title: The dark knight just got darker
8.content:
It's dark times in Gotham city. A new villain is sowing chaos and reaping despair. Mad as a hat this villain gives evil a new name: the Joker. And once again the Batman comes out of hiding to save the city.

The original Batman tales never had too much around them. Flimsy little comics never could have after all. The main story line backing this film isn't much different: criminal is on the loose, superhero goes after him. But luckily for this film there is more. There is the background of the main characters, there's a nice suspense story and there is great action.

And not to forget, there is great acting. Bale is doing a wonderful job as the Batman, but it has to be said that it is Ledger that is stealing the show. His rendition of the Joker is downright brilliant, the character coming to life as mad as it can and every little move and sound he makes fitting into the character and the story.

So, all in all, well played, well written, and good looking. Leaving only some small space for improvement here and there.

8 out of 10 bats out of Hell

8.title: Not perfect, but a really good, high octane action film
8.content:
"The Dark Knight" has been the cinema sensation of 2008. It has been, very nearly, universally acclaimed by the critics. It is the biggest film of the year so far, by far, and is unlikely to be overtaken by anything else released during 2008. For weeks "The Dark Knight" was the #1 film on IMDb's top 250 films list (which surprised me a little bit, as it was a very new film), although it is down to #3 this week. It has endured unprecedented levels of hype and has come through unhindered as a big, solid hit movie. A perfect Summer blockbuster.

I don't think that "The Dark Knight" is a perfect film, but it is a really good film, if not a great film. Certainly it is the best high octane, high weaponry action film released in many a year (for high octane, high weaponry, I think "Heat" or "Die Hard") and would still have worked even if it had not been a Batman movie. It has great set pieces, a huge scale (I saw it on an IMAX screen - Good Lord! - highly recommended) and had good performances by the whole cast, but especially by Heath Ledger, Gary Oldman and Aaron Eckhart. Particularly Aaron Eckhart. He had the most difficult character arc to follow during the course of the film.

I said that "The Dark Knight" is not a perfect film. It isn't. Let me elaborate.

1. It is too long. Sorry, but it is. Sometimes you can have too much of a good thing. The first half of the film could have definitely been trimmed.

2. Bale's Batman voice sometimes verged on the ridiculous. I kept thinking of The Kurgan from "Highlander".

3. Michael Caine's screen time as Alfred was little more than an extended cameo. I seem to remember he had more screen time in "Batman Begins".

4. Ditto Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox.

5. Maggie Gylenhaal's Rachel Dawes really had nothing to do. True, I will admit that her final scenes were crucial to the motivation of Harvey Dent in the latter part of the movie.

6. Unlike in "Batman Begins", this time around Batman/Bruce Wayne was not nearly as interesting as the villains. The typical curse of any Batman film.

I am being picky. Sure I am. Minor issues.

I really enjoyed "The Dark Knight". I definitely recommend it, even if you cannot stand superhero movies.

8.title: Perfect.--so long as you're not a Batman fan.
8.content:
Almost every aspect of this movie was great. The action was brilliant. Unlike Batman Begins you can clearly see what's happening in each and every action scene. Plus the truck flipping? Holy crap! Awesome! The acting: brilliant. And not JUST Heath Ledger was great. There's probably to much focus on him, seeing as how everyone else was just as brilliant. Christian Bale- Still great. Aaron Eckhart, whom I wasn't expecting much out of- AMAZING. The directing, perfect. The scenery, pretty good.

All in all, I would've thought this movie was probably the best movie I've seen in a long time...if I hadn't read the Batman graphic novels and seen Batman Begins first. In comparison to them, The Dark Knight seems to be missing something. In the graphic novels and Begins, the scenes are darker, Batman's character is more conflicted, and Alfred is funnier. Knowing this was supposed to be based off of Batman, I was impressed at first, until I thought it through. Some major parts of Batman's character is lost.

Batman's always been the character stuck between his morals and what's necessary. In the comic books he knows he should have and still should kill The Joker because The Joker's a serial killer, but he thinks of killing someone as a line he just shouldn't cross. In The Dark Knight, I don't even think Batman thought about killing The Joker. I guess he was too busy dealing with people dieing to think about saving them? It just doesn't seem to be a problem for him.

Batman's also always been the character fighting in the shadows, so that both his audiences and the villains are left in suspense as to where he is. As I said earlier, in The Dark Knight you can see everything at all points in time during action scenes.

8.title: It could have been as good as everybody's pretending it is, if only...........
8.content:
Nolan had the dialogue written by a professional in that particular area, not him and his brother. The movie had in its favor rock-solid acting (particularly in the case of Heath Ledger, who pretty much lives up to the staggering hype), a great director, a wonderful plot with wonderful nuances and a wonderful way of ending with a beginning. But the dialogue....the dialogue, my God the dialogue. It was pathetic. Abysmally bad. So overwrought. Almost everyone speaks in what sounds like carefully prepared prose. I kept thinking 'People don't talk like that!' It ruins the continuity of scenes and makes them unrealistic. It reminds you you're watching a movie. More than anything though, it doesn't afford the characters relationships with each other. They're never talking to one another, never reacting to one another, they're just saying in-character things kind of in each other's general directions. Nobody had a rapport with anybody. Even the dynamic between Bale's Batman and Caine's Alfred that the 'Batman Begins' so lovingly established, seems falsified and staged, and I imagine it's hard to screw something up so bad that even the joint ministrations of Christian Bale and Michael Caine can't save it.

However, in spite of all that, this is still such a good movie that it couldn't effectively ruin itself. It just breaks my heart how much better it could have been.

Certainly not lacking in the action department, and unique in that the action never feels separate from the plot, like a pee break from the drama of the story, like a lot of these movies end up. Everything is woven together quite masterfully. Beautifully choreographed action scenes, with lots of brutal beatdowns, car/truck/wheeled bat-gadget chases, and an appropriate amount of stuff blowing up all awesome-like.

Worth seeing, but could have truly great with different writing. =(

8/10

8.title: Modern Enough...Stylish Enough...It is......Batman
8.content:
Immensely Popular and a Mega-Money-Maker (over $1 Billion worldwide and still counting) this is a very Ambitious Batman Movie and as always it is the Character Batman and, in this case, The Joker and to a lesser extent Two-Face that are the Soul of any Series with such Iconic, Indelible, Artful, Mythological Personas.

It can be Hyped and Hyper-Financed with all the Technological and Creative Spirit Available in any Time period, but it is the Manifestational Psychology and Surreal Images of the Fictional Representations of Humanity that are at the Core.

Here Heath Ledger's Legendary and Academy Award Winning Performance is helped by the Great Psychotic Clown's Character. He is Batman's Arch Nemesis and it just begs for Over the Top takes on His Disturbed Mentality and His Psychotic Glee, and a Look that is Archetypal and the Anarchy Abounds.

The Film is not without some Missteps and up front Disappointments. Like the Ending that is Overwritten to make Batman "the Hero that we deserve". That bit of Nonsensical Overkill is too Pretentious to be Profound and is the Filmmaker Reaching too far.

The Cast, including Christian Bale as Batman, are pretty much in the Spirit of Things as usual. The Look is Great, except the City that is Nothing More Now than just a City. Gotham's Dark Architecture is Gone and Gleaming Skyscrapers and Clean Streets are an Antithesis to the Milieu of a Dark Time and a Cynical Society that usually Surrounds Batman.

Overall, a slightly Overrated but Excellent Entertainment that is Dark enough and Disturbing enough and Modern enough to be a Respectable and Rewarding Second Act to Director Christopher Nolan's Trilogy.

8.title: Very good and enjoyable but not a Masterpiece
8.content:
I saw this movie a few days after it came out because all my friends saw it and said it was great and they loved it. The hype for the movie was crazy. However, the movie wasn't an all around masterpiece. I have read some reviews saying it belongs up there with movies like Goodfellas, The Godfather, and many many other greats. Not even close in my opinion. The ending wasn't really great in my eyes with the joker not dying. I know Ledger died and he played the joker but its not like everyone on set knew he was going to die.

As for the positives, I enjoyed the movie. Ledger's performance was outstanding as was the rest of the supporting cast. Eckhart, Caine, Oldman, and all others were superb in their respective supporting roles. Ledger's performance is Oscar worthy but I'm not sure I want to give the nod for this movie to receive a best picture nomination. As of right now, I would say yes but the Oscars aren't for 6 months. Many other great movies will come out that are better than this one. However, I do think the best supporting actor category is over with Ledger. He was already robbed once in Brokeback Mountain and so was the movie of best picture. The entry of the movie with the bank robbery is outstanding. The movie does deserve many Oscar nominations.

RIP Heath Ledger

8.title: Definitely on par with Batman and Batman Begins
8.content: I would never have thought that my favourite movie of the year (so far) would be a Batman sequel but Nolan did it again. It's no Memento but its good writing along with great cinematography and directing made the movie a must see for every action or blockbuster movie lover. The action sequences are all pretty solid and the performances are top notch. I know many of you can't hear it anymore but Heath Ledger did one heck of a job as the Joker. Jack Nicholson being my favourite actor ever may be the only reason I would say he is on par (and not superior) to the original Batman's Joker. I don't want to spoil too much but the overall ending and some needless (wannabe) twists were actually the only things that left a bit of a sour taste in my mouth. Comparing it to other comic book adaptions I think it's only inferior to the Crow.

8.title: Best Movies
8.content: I recently had the opportunity to watch the movie "Battmen" and I have to say, I was thoroughly impressed. The plot was engaging and kept me on the edge of my seat throughout the entire film. The action scenes were well-choreographed and the special effects were top-notch. The acting was also top-notch, with each actor bringing their character to life in a believable and convincing manner. Overall, "Batman" is a must-see for any action movie fan. The production values are high and the story is compelling, making it a great choice for a night out at the movies. If you are interested in hollywod movie then you should watch this movie.

8.title: Batman in Gotham
8.content:
This new clever version of the Batman saga, sticks into our mind as one of the best realized takes on the comic book hero that has . Yes, Batman is as amazing as always, but he is perhaps more human, this time out. That might be because of the intelligent treatment, its director, Christopher Nolan, working with his brother, Jonathan, conceived as a clever approach to the protector of all good causes in Gotham.

Not being this our favorite genre, we gave it the benefit of the doubt, and we were impressed with what we saw. Naturally, the film works because of the fantastic job of the late Heath Ledger, who runs away with the picture. Not to take from the star, Christian Bale, but the screen smolders whenever the evil joker, impersonated by Mr. Ledger, appears in front of the action. It's impossible to take ones eyes away from this actor throughout the duration of the movie.

The creators have conveniently disposed of Robin, Batman's sidekick that is absent since the previous installment, thus eliminating the problem presented by was perhaps a gay duo; the new take on Batman makes him into a macho figure that talks with a husky voice, perhaps trying to prove he is not a closet case.

The cast is impeccable. Christian Bale makes a great Batman. Actors of the caliber of Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman, the charismatic Aaron Eckhart, Maggie Gyllenhaal, and the incomparable Michael Caine, who returns as Alfred Pennyworth. What's more amazing is that Mr. Nolan and his team have meshed all the elements and have given us a film that is fun, full of action, and at the same time, it packs a lot of entertainment.

Wally Pfister's cinematography plus Lee Smith editing, works wonder in the film. The musical score is by James Newton Howard and Hans Zimmer. Technically, the film makes the viewer think how did all was accomplished. It's not easy task to put all the elements together and come out with a winning film this neat.

Thanks should go to Christopher Nolan for his vision and a posthumous salute to the great Heath Ledger for what he gave us.

8.title: Batman Vs batman
8.content: Batman 1989 is still the best film of the franchise. It feels more like a comic book than this film. The action scenes in this film is better though.Joker is far better in 1989 for me

8.title: Don't get me wrong, I LOVED this movie...but some of the fanboys have GOT to gain some perspective...
8.content:
I won't go on and on about how good this movie is, nor will I detail each and every nuance of the film as others have. What I'm here to say is, "Yes...this is a great film. Heath Ledger is the quintessential Joker. This is, quite possibly, the best performance of Ledger's illustrious (if shortened) career." This film is beautiful, dark, wonderful, tragic...electric. It features breathtaking city elements (skyscrapers to beat all city monoliths), stellar performances, and beautiful darkling nemeses.

Bale delivers as both Batman and Wayne, but no one expected him to fail in this role. Morgan Freeman's character {Fox) asserts himself this go around, and pulls it off beautifully. And I couldn't be happier about Sir Michael Caine's reprisal of his role as Alfred, and I hope he continues throughout the franchise. It's always nice to see Gary Oldman, regardless of the work, and Maggie Gyllenhaal was totally strong as Rachel Dawes. I was more than satisfied to see her assume that role, and she does not disappoint. The chemistry was far superior to that of the original...both between the characters and within the story itself.

Honestly, I had not previously believed it would be possible to top the first of this run, "Batman Begins," but, "The Dark Knight," does so with little difficulty I must say, for posterity's sake, however, that the CGI job on Eckhart's Dent (post explosion) was ambitious, but the finished product was just nasty. Makeup effects along with a LITTLE CGI would have been beautiful, but what we got was more reminiscent of Imhotep's early incarnation in the first, "The Mummy." Well, half of it, anyway. (I won't explain that, you'll have to see the movie for yourself.) It messes with the suspension of belief, for me. It is like a book that keeps reminding you that it's a book. The CGI...was so impossible that it kept snapping me back out of the movie, and had me looking at the rest of the effects for the remainder of the film. It WAS effective, however, in shocking the audience, but once achieved, it was difficult to get back into the story flow.

Otherwise, this is a most excellent piece of work, and I cannot wait for the next one. At least...I'm hoping above hope that there will BE a "next one." Considering that this movie has been billed as the most mistake-ridden film of the year so far, who knows. Personally, I don't care about the 16 "major mistakes" found in continuity. I love the story and would pay to see another one.

But above a 9/10 here at IMDb? I think not. This film is not better than Schindler's List, Star Wars IV, Casablanca, or ANY installment of The Lord of the Rings. You fanboys have GOT to be kidding me. It's great, yes, but not THAT great.

It rates an 8.5/10 from...

the Fiend :.

8.content: Batman is upping the ante in his war on crime. With the help of Lieutenant Jim Gordon and prosecutor Harvey Dent, he intends to clean up the streets of the crime that is poisoning the city. Cooperation proves to be effective, but soon they will find themselves in the midst of chaos.

8.content: Best action movie of all time, few action movies show a level of quality like this, the performance of Heath Ledger was spectacular, Christian Bale also made the film even better, well-written screenplay and well-conducted action scenes, this movie it's just worth watching several times

8.content: We can watch for the Joker's acting alone many times. God! what an actor he is!

8.title: Big achievement, but exhausting experience
8.content:
I'd love to give this movie a 10. It cries out for it. The only problem is that I was so exhausted after watching it the first time, I may never watch it again. The Dark Knight desperately needed more in the way of tension breaks, much like the original "Batman" movie had, but they just weren't there. The movie got more and more dark, and more and more tense, and even the ending couldn't leave you with a positive feeling about what had happened and what might follow.

All the performances were top notch. Action sequences: big. Special effects: dazzling. Its a must see movie.

However, its going to be an endurance contest for many viewers. I felt the same way about Braveheart and Saving Private Ryan. Both are top movies, must see, and after viewing them once I was done with them because the stories were just so exhausting. It may just be a personal viewpoint. I run two businesses, and my days are more often than not eight hours of unrelenting tension. That doesn't leave me with a desire for more of the same in my evening or weekend entertainment.

So watch it the first time, and then you can make your own decision about surviving it in subsequent viewings! LOL

8.title: We live in a society.
8.content: This movie is fun and dark and wonderfully made, I enjoyed every moment of it. Especially when Heath Ledger was on-screen.

8.title: GOTHAM DEserves of better criminals
8.content:
And it happened! One of the most anticipated films of the year finally got its premiere. A great advertising campaign, lots of fans around the world dressed up as a famous superhero, promising trailers and spots, and millions of tickets sold - all to watch the "Dark Knight." When Batman and Robin suffered a terrible defeat in 1997, few fans expected "Batman - The Beginning" to be better. Fortunately for everyone, they were wrong. Christopher Nolan, encouraged by the success of his first part, again took on the adventures of the bat man. And once again the viewers were positively surprised.

Events in the "Dark Knight" show Gotham City, a few years after the events known to us from the previous part. This time Batman (Christian Bale) is not alone in the fight against crime. He is assisted by Commissioner James Gordon (Gary Oldman), District Prosecutor Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart) and former childhood friend Rachel Dawes (Maggie Gyllenhall). They all have to unite to work out existing criminal organizations that constantly harass the city's residents. The cooperation brings great results, but nobody expects that they may soon fall victim to the brilliant "prince of chaos", appearing under the pseudonym Joker (Heath Ledger). Joker threatens that if Batman does not reveal his true identity, he will kill all important personalities in Gotham. Soon this threat will come true and the Joker will show that (unlike Batman) there are no inhibitions ...

At the very beginning, I must admit that the plot is a strong plus of the "Dark Knight". You can see with a naked eye that Christopher Nolan was watching over every detail. Viewers certainly won't complain about boredom during the screening. The tension is gradually increasing, the plot is much faster than in the previous part, and in addition you can risk the statement that Nolan obtains, in a sense, a kind of hidden philosophical and psychological message. As a reviewer of one of the newspapers wrote: "Christopher Nolan shows that it is impossible to fight crime completely (...). You can close all mafia bosses, kill gangsters and their families, but there will always be an alibi, someone will always bribe judges, someone will always escape punishment and start a new crime network in the city. " So from the very beginning I could see that it is not a banal production. The downside is the not very well carried out thread of Two Faces, unnecessary introduction of the character Scarecrow and quite poor ending. But in general the plot has a big plus for me.

You can't complain about the action itself. Special effects specialists have once again done a great job. The outbreak of the hospital and the truck chase are very impressive. This time, Batman gadgets are slightly less than in previous parts, but this does not affect the quality of watching the movie too much. On the other hand, sometimes a somewhat chaotic camera may interfere (especially in scenes where Batman sees the shots from Lucius Fox's sonar). Actors also deserve praise. Christian Bale proved that he feels very well in the comic convention (admittedly you can pick on his hoarse people, but I heard that his voice has been computer modified, so it's not Bale's fault). Aaron Eckhart also performs very well in the role of two-faced Harvey Dent. The actor perfectly shows the transformation of his hero. Harvey is a heroic defender of Gotham at one moment, and at the other a ready-made man who can do a lot to avenge the death of those he loves.

In the supporting roles, we once again have the opportunity to see great actors. Gary Oldman, Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman once again prove that they feel great about the comic convention. I hope that they will be able to show it more than once. Maggie Gyllenhall falls slightly pale against the background of this excellent company - Rachel is simply boring. Honestly, however, it must be admitted that the script did not give her much to show off. However, the real star of this movie is Heath Ledger in the role of the psychopathic clown, Joker. Heath is simply fantastic in this role. His charisma catches us from the first moment he appears on the screen and Heath no longer shows the show to the end. I hope his Joker will not be forgotten and will permanently enter the canon of the best villains in the history of cinema. Bravo!

The music is very similar to what we had the opportunity to see in "Batman Beginning". During the scene of the pursuit and Batman watching the city of Gotham, thanks to the story gaining additional blushes. However, bearing in mind that its creator is the Oscar nominee Hans Zimmer, who has been nominated many times, you can feel a slight hunger.

To sum up: the latest adventures of the dark knight Gotham City are really successful. The film is a class better than the previous part. This is not b

8.title: noice
8.content: Noice noice noice noice noice noice noice noice noice noice noice noice noice

8.title: A solid superhero movie, but far from perfection everyone claims it to be.
8.content:
A list of each aspect of this movie and how I would rate them:

Plot: 7/10
The plot takes a serious jab at Batman's principals by introducing the chaos of Joker as it should've been, but never really allows Batman to learn anything. He ends up putting down the mantle because he thinks his hand in fighting back evil in Gotham creates monsters like the Joker and ruins good men like Harvey Dent. However, that answer is a bit too simple and undermines all of the effort Batman had to make to fix the city in Batman Begins and his reason for becoming the Batman. The Dark Knight Rises in fact exactly shows that Gotham will always need Batman and it's his destiny, but instead the Trilogy leads us to wanting to put away Batman every time because his hand is somehow "unjustified". The story didn't make enough of the Dark Knight and why he is needed (like in the comics).

Characters: 8/10
Heath Ledger's Joker was almost too exceptional compared to the rest of the Characters in the story. The problem with the characterizations in this movie lies mainly with Batman. The Dark Knight Trilogy took Batman too seriously while at the same time not focusing on his character development in a proper way. You could even argue TDK Rises (an inferior movie) had more character development for Bruce Wayne even if by a very little bit. TDK got the aspect of making him a heroic force, but made him more like some kind of a soldier for Gotham rather than it's dedicated protector as Batman ought to be.

Cinematography/ Screen-Play: 9/10
The screen play was simply very solid. Some moments (especially with the Joker) were just show in a way that feels like the most ideal way to show that scene. The only thing I could complain about is the Batsuit being a bit too awkward looking at some angles, but it's also a unique costume for it's realistic attempt to make a sensible looking Batman. One of the best things about this movie is the performance put on by Heath Ledger. It's probably generated countless memes and allowed this movie to age better than most movies of it's caliber.

Music: 9/10
Hans Zimmer delivers an amazing Sound Tracks and Theme Music to the characters and scenes). It always creates emotions and at some moments it amplifies scenes that otherwise be pretty ordinary or just decent with pure awe.

Final Rating: 8/10. To me the most important traits to any fictional work is it's quality of writing this involves the plot and characters. Cinematography is a slightly lesser, but still critically important quality that will pretty much be responsible for the look and feel of that good writing. Music encloses the entire movie experience by amplifying the emotions of what the audience will be seeing. While story and characterization would drag the overall rating down to a rating of about 7.5, the sheer quality that Nolan orders into his movie in it's screenplay and audio carries that rating higher. I don't think the movie accomplishes things other (also non-perfect) movies do (the kind of movies I would rate a 9). That is why I would give this movie an 8 and not a 9, but I completely see why people would give it a higher rating. Heath Ledger's performance was truly stunning, and may he rest in peace.

8.title: Not the hero we need, but the hero we deserve.
8.content: The sequel to Batman Begins, in Christopher Nolan's epic trilogy of Batman. While writing this review, this is the first time I have seen this film and just why have I not seen this earlier?? It was wonderful. It had my attention the whole way through. It was predictable at times, like any superhero film but it definitely is unlike your typical superhero film. It broke some clichés and had powerful directing making for great acting, amazing atmosphere, wonderful scenes and overall an epic story. I recommend this film to everyone if you haven't seen this already.

8.title: Worth remembering for one performance especially.
8.content: I suspect the only reason this Batman film is remembered, is simply because it is a relatively new one and made with the usual fancy CGI effects. How shallow! The film is better than I was expecting it to be. The plot is long and detailed but good. Christian Bale is no actor of any description. He merely fits the requirements of being a hero- type character but without any conviction of any kind. Speaking of which, casting Michael Caine as Alfred has to be one of the worst casting decisions of all time! He has none of the class or heavyweight talent for that matter in playing such a role. He will go down as one of the most over-rated actors in history. Morgan Freeman is very good as one of the few people in the film who is in regular contact with Batman. He is a fine character actor. "The Dark Knight" belongs to Heath Ledger though. I recall feeling quite surprised at his tragic passing and before the film went out on general release. I saw the film at the cinema on my 28th birthday and what a present that was! He really embraces the character of the Joker in displaying different facets. In addition, he is bloody scary in how he looks and acts. The make- up is great and you get the impression of the darkness descending every time he appears...... I was glad when Heath Ledger was posthumously awarded the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor, he had earnt it. He is someone who actually makes some effort to be convincing and multi- dimensional in his performance. You believe he could be the Joker. People have debated over whose Joker is better out of his and Jack Nicholson's version. It really doesn't matter to me, they are both great. 8.title: Ambitious epic chapter
8.content:
This review contains spoilers.

The Dark Knight is a superhero movie that premiered in 2008. The movie is the sequel to 2005's Batman Begins also directed by Christopher Nolan. The movie follows Batman Begins after a notable amount of time as Batman must confront the criminal mastermind, known as Joker.

The Dark Knight is an epic chapter in the Batman movies. This is a long movie with 152 minutes of running time. There are some recurring characters from the previous movie such as Rachel Dawes and Lucius Fox, but otherwise this movie can stand by itself. This is a movie that does not require previous knowledge from Batman Begins. The Dark Knight tells a long story with the Joker and Harvey Dent or Two-Face. This requires a long journey that has the Joker acquiring more power in the criminal underworld. Much of the movie follows the Joker doing criminal actions that Batman thwarts and is reverted by Joker or his goons.

The action scenes in this movie are good with some scenes being great. The action scenes are choreographed impressively and this is owed to the beautifully setup scenes and sets. Along with fun action scenes, these scenes have a reason to exist. They service the plot in a meaningful way for developments to occur.

The problem with The Dark Knight is its mile-a-minute plot. The movie makes a focused attempt at making the Joker a big threat and the audience can feel this. Heath Ledger does a wonderful job as the Joker but the problem lies in the script. In short: the Joker has a special ability to read the movie's script. The villain is able to make predictions on choices his henchmen will do and what the individual policemen will do. Later on, during a confrontation between Harvey and Joke, he states he is an agent of chaos and he has no plan. Yet almost everything goes according to Joker's plan. This is one of the most ludicrous ways for Joker to keep evading capture as if anything had gone slightly differently the Joker would have been killed or imprisoned. This is a movie that asks the audience to care about the themes and realism but then these impossible plans occur.

I would recommend "The Dark Knight" directed by Christopher Nolan.

Grade: B.
